Sports.title: Édouard Mendy: ‘Winning Afcon was 10 times better than the Champions League’
Sports.content:
“I had to stay patient and try to have a cool head because everywhere else there was fire,” Édouard Mendy remembers. In the cauldron of the Stade Prince Moulay Abdellah in Rabat, the Senegal goalkeeper was about to face a penalty against the hosts, Morocco, in stoppage time of the Africa Cup of Nations final.

Mendy had just been shown a yellow card after a 17-minute delay where he and most of his teammates had controversially headed to their dressing room in protest at the referee’s decision to penalise El Hadji Malick Diouf after a Morocco corner.

Senegal had also had a goal disallowed minutes earlier, while Mendy’s complaints to the Congolese referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, about having his towel stolen by Ismael Saibari – a misdemeanour for which the Bayern Munich forward later apologised – and lasers being directed in his eyes from the crowd seemed to fall on deaf ears. Now the goalkeeper who won the Champions League with Chelsea in 2021 tried to maintain his focus as Real Madrid’s Brahim Díaz stood over the ball.

“I realised two steps before he shot … usually when a player does a Panenka they slow down for the last step, but I noticed he did it early,” says Mendy, who is widely regarded as one of the best African goalkeepers having played a central role in the most successful period in Senegal’s history. “I know his preferred side is on the right. But when I saw him slow down way before, I just stood up and managed to catch the ball.”

View image in fullscreen In a chaotic Africa Cup of Nations final, Édouard Mendy kept his head to read Brahim Díaz’s Panenka. Photograph: Youssef Loulidi/AP

Four minutes into extra time, Pape Gueye’s goal meant Senegal and Mendy crowned African champions for the second time in four years. Or so it seemed. More than seven months after Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory in March when the Confederation of African Football ruled Senegal had forfeited the final by leaving the pitch, a preliminary hearing for their appeal is finally set to be heard at the court of arbitration for sport in Switzerland next month.

“The only thing we have to remember is that the game went to the end. We went off the pitch but the game restarted,” Mendy said. “For me there is no issue because the final was completed – we were given the trophy and celebrated in our country. That was it. When you speak to me about the Afcon, I just simply tell you that: ‘Yes, we have won it twice.’ That’s nothing against the Moroccan people or anyone else. It’s just how we feel. I’m not a lawyer but it’s just common sense. You can’t change something that has already been decided.”

In the meantime, Mendy has added to his bulging trophy cabinet by winning a second successive Asian Champions League with Al-Ahli, faced World Cup heartache after sustaining a knee injury against Norway and, at the age of 34, announced his international retirement last week. Even a phone call from Senegal’s new manager, Patrick Vieira, could not persuade him to change his mind and potentially add to his 59 caps.

“He [Vieira] is a legend so to have the chance to work with him was really something that came into my mind,” Mendy says. “But at the end of the call I asked for some time to really think about everything. A couple of days later I called him and explained that I wanted to stick to my decision. I started thinking about it after the Afcon and I just came to the conclusion that it was my time to say stop.”

View image in fullscreen Despite being stripped of the title, Senegal still paraded the trophy in Paris before playing a friendly against France. Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/Reuters

Mendy has high hopes that Senegal’s next generation, which includes Monaco’s Lamine Camara – the midfielder who almost joined Chelsea in the summer – and Aston Villa’s Ibrahim Mbaye can emulate the achievements of his. The Teranga Lions were crowned African champions for the first time in 2022, around eight months after Mendy kept a clean sheet in the 2021 Champions League final. But he says there is no comparison between the two when he looks back now. “[Winning Afcon] was the best moment of my football career: it was 10 times better [than the Champions League]. I can compare now because I’ve also won the Asian Champions League twice.

“To win for your club is something really incredible. But you cannot compare with winning for your country, especially when they have never won anything before. It happens only once in your life so being part of the team that made history was amazing.”

View image in fullscreen Édouard Mendy kept nine clean sheets, a joint record for one tournament, on Chelsea’s run to winning the Champions League in 2021. Photograph: Pierre Philippe Marcou/AP

Mendy’s exploits in 2021 led to him being named best goalkeeper at Fifa’s now defunct The Best awards, but he missed out on the Yashin trophy awarded by the organisers of the Ballon d’Or to Gianluigi Donnarumma. Both have been nominated again for this year’s award and Mendy says he is proud to be in the conversation again after what he describes as “my best year since I became a professional” after a season in which no other goalkeeper won as many major honours.

He says: “To be nominated for the Yashin trophy while I play in Saudi Arabia means a lot to me. My journey has not been easy – everything is about working hard and being resilient. When I see goalkeepers in Senegal wearing the No 16 jersey it makes me so proud. It means that at some point I gave them some inspiration and this is very powerful.”

Mendy was born in Normandy, and started his professional career at Cherbourg but found himself unemployed for a year after enduring successive relegations. He was eventually given another chance by Marseille and is now helping to fund a school in his parents’ hometown of Keur Massar that has recently expanded to 200 students. Mendy is also behind a scheme that supports budding entrepreneurs in the country.

“There is so much talent in Senegal and we have a young population that is very dynamic. That’s why it’s important to give them the opportunity to have a better life,” he says. “When my mum sees the school she is so proud and that is the biggest gift anyone can have.”

Sports.title: ‘It’s bordering on exploitation’: how pseudoscience is duping football
Sports.content:
Dr Claire-Marie Roberts was working at Coventry City when she received a call from someone asking whether she knew how much oxygen was in the atmosphere. As the performance director, responsible for optimising players’ potential, she was accustomed to being pitched the latest gimmick promising miraculous gains. At times, she could receive up to 50 LinkedIn messages a week offering a device, supplement or technology that claimed to produce magical results.

“It is only 21%,” the caller told her. That’s GCSE chemistry, she thought. Then came the sales pitch: “So what we’ve done is put oxygen in a can and we think you might want to use it.”

“Right … oxygen in a can,” Roberts says, laughing at the memory. Suffice to say, she did not take the caller up on his offer to buy oxygen in a can for Coventry’s players.

Roberts has spent decades working in elite athlete performance and professional football, including nine years at the Premier League and two at Coventry, where she played a key role in their promotion as Championship champions before joining the Formula One team McLaren as director of human performance in the summer. She is shocked by how professional football is being duped by pseudoscience: from coaches and performance staff misled by snake-oil sellers, to players desperate for a shortcut and with money to burn.

“It’s the science-practice gap, which is widening in my experience,” Roberts says. “I think it’s getting much worse. There’s so much sparkly marketing behind all these things. It’s bordering on exploitation.

“They’re taking a population that is very susceptible to: ‘How can I hack my performance advantage? How can I shortcut my preparation and recovery?’ Which I don’t think is a great starting point.”

Roberts says some of the practices commonplace in elite football have little evidence behind them. She includes cryotherapy chambers – a common feature at elite training grounds. If unavailable, ice baths are a fallback. Players enjoy them so much that Harry Kane was photographed standing in a wheelie bin full of ice after a Bayern Munich match at last year’s Club World Cup.

View image in fullscreen Claire-Marie Roberts was part of Frank Lampard’s staff during Coventry’s Championship-winning season. Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters

“Most clubs have got cryotherapy chambers – most people cannot articulate to you why they use them, because there’s no evidence for them apart from a very slim piece of work that says it might help prevent dementia,” Roberts says. “There’s very sketchy evidence on cryotherapy.”

They could even be detrimental to recovery, Roberts says. “There’s a recent suggestion that cryotherapy might blunt muscular adaptation. When are you using it and why are you using it? If you’re using it for recovery, sleep and nutrition are your best recovery modalities. No amount of putting anybody in a whole-body cryotherapy chamber is going to help them recover more if those two things aren’t taken care of.”

But players are constantly attempting to shortcut nutrition, too. Supplements are a multibillion-pound industry that has its claws in the game. But beyond vitamin D, in which it is “evidence-based” that people in the northern hemisphere are commonly deficient owing to a lack of sunlight, and vitamin C, which is usually short in our diets, supplementation should, Roberts says, be targeted to deficiencies.

“You’ve got people popping pills not really asking what they’re for. It should always be needs-based. If you don’t eat fish and fish oil is important to you, you might supplement it. It should all be based on need.

“Your athletic performance and recovery is based on sleep quality and nutritional quality and amounts. No amount of supplementation will improve a bad diet, but people think it will. We don’t do enough of the basics and think we can shortcut and hack everything.”

View image in fullscreen Claire-Marie Roberts: ‘Most clubs have got cryotherapy chambers – most people cannot articulate to you why they use them.’ Photograph: Eddie Keogh for The FA/Rex/Shutterstock

Roberts says she used an evidence-based, scientific approach to support Frank Lampard’s squad and that many clubs follow practices from the top of the game when often they are flawed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“People passively suck these things up,” she says. “Because England or Manchester City or Chelsea who have all the resources under the sun have got this, there’s a misappropriation of confidence and understanding of the scientific basis or evidence. It’s powerful in driving behaviour, but it’s driving the wrong behaviour.”

Roberts, a former swimmer who missed the 1996 Atlanta Olympics owing to injury, says: “Football is more susceptible to it than any other sport I’ve experienced first-hand. I think because the stakes are higher.”

Kinesiology tape – or k-tape, as it is commonly known – is another trend that baffles Roberts. Players from Cristiano Ronaldo to Gareth Bale and David Beckham have been spotted wearing it over the years, often resembling strips of gaffer tape stuck to limbs.

“There’s no evidence kinesiology tape has any impact on injury prevention or performance-related outcomes. It gives you a bit of proprioception – maybe you feel like someone has done something – but in any environment I’ve worked in you’d never see anyone wearing k-tape. It’s a big white elephant.

“If an athlete has dislocated their shoulder, you should strap it – strapping is different. It provides an element of external support that can provide minimal protection to the joint and reminds the person they’ve got a problem. It’s a risk-mitigation strategy. It’s not hugely successful, but you’d do it rather than not do it. K-tape is a placebo.”

Often, managers who have been in the game for decades insist on practices they have adopted for years, or because another coach, with no scientific background, has heard about a revolutionary new product. Roberts believes that until football puts science at the centre of decision-making and employs qualified staff to scrutinise claims, the problem will worsen.

“We think we can accelerate to an outcome without putting the hard yards in – the basic things: diet and sleep and the quality of your training,” she says.

“Football in general is very anti-intellectual and it has been for a long time. There are a few clubs that do it well, but the majority don’t. The game is definitely anti-science. There’s a reason for that. There isn’t a critical mass of people that are applying critical thought to situations.”

Sports.title: La Liga president says Real Madrid conspiracy claims are ‘in another galaxy’
Sports.content:
Real Madrid want a new La Liga president in light of what they called “intolerable” comments from the incumbent, Javier Tebas, ⁠who said on Tuesday that claims of officiating bias against the club belonged to “another galaxy”.

After losing 2-1 to Atlético Madrid on ⁠Sunday, Real headlined the ⁠match report ​on their website, “Terrible refereeing decides the derby.”

Real were furious that Atlético’s defender Cristian Romero was not sent off for a stamp on ⁠Jude Bellingham and also complained about a challenge by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde.

Real’s manager, José Mourinho, aimed sharp criticism at the referee, Miguel Ángel Ortiz ⁠Arias, and those who appointed him. Mourinho said his side could win the title “if they ​let us compete on a level playing ‌field”.

He brought two printed screenshots of what he thought were red-card tackles committed by players to his post-match press conference.

Tebas responded to a pro-Real article on social media with a lengthy riposte to allegations of a “conspiracy” against the 15-time European champions.

“Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime’s television, building the same old narrative – the permanent conspiracy,” said Tebas, who has often been at odds with Real Madrid and the club’s outspoken president, Florentino Pérez.

“This article goes further – it claims that referees harm ‘the business that feeds them’. What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership, or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.

“Real Madrid are crucial to La Liga. But claiming that ‘La Liga is worth nothing’ without them reveals the disdain for the other clubs, their fans, and their history. The competition belongs to no one.”

Real responded with a statement on their website, saying: “Our club considers it intolerable that the president of La Liga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking ​Real Madrid.

“Given this inappropriate and persistent behaviour, we believe that the professional football competition in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and realising its full potential with the fundamental duty of neutrality.“

Real sit six points behind the reigning champions and early leaders, Barcelona.

Sports.title: ‘Have some humanity’: Diogo Jota chants at Rúben Neves a wake-up call for Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
The good thing about Cristiano Ronaldo playing in your league is that he is one of the most famous footballers ever and when he scores a great goal or reaches 1,000 (just 21 to go), many people watch. The bad thing about Cristiano Ronaldo playing in your league is that when something negative happens and he is involved, just as many people will watch and listen. Global attention is something that the big European leagues have had for years but it is something the Saudi Pro League, which has spent billions in search of achieving a similar stature, needs to get used to.

On Sunday 13 September, Ronaldo wrote to his 680 million Instagram followers to discuss the events of the night before when Al-Taawoun supporters were coming to terms with a 6-0 home thrashing by Al-Hilal, whose £150m-plus forward line, Ollie Watkins and Gabriel Martinelli, got five between them. Fair to say that some handled it better than others as what followed was in the worst possible taste.

At the end, what seemed to be a small number of fans saw Al-Hilal’s Rúben Neves in the centre circle and started chanting the name of his former Portugal and Wolves teammate Diogo Jota, who died in a car accident in July 2025who tragically died. Neves, who has a tattoo of the Liverpool star, was visibly upset and made a gesture which clearly said to those supporters that “God is watching you”. He also said to Saudi reporters after the game: “I hope they don’t go to pray afterwards.”

Ronaldo then weighed in. “The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” he wrote. “This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave ‌like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again.” Al-Hilal made an official complaint. This was a big story.

Ayman al-Hotami, one of Al-Hilal’s best-known fans, says: “I found the chants hard to believe but those responsible were few in number and very young. Al-Hilal’s fanbase completely condemn the chants and demanded an apology regarding the actions of individuals in their stands. We appreciate the club’s response in condemning this isolated incident, which represents neither the club nor our society.”

Away from home in small stadiums with low attendances, often the case when the big teams play outside Jeddah and Riyadh, the chants of a few can carry far. More than once, Ronaldo has heard the name of a certain Argentinian star coming his way and reacted badly. This, though, was on a completely different level.

View image in fullscreen Rúben Neves (centre) and Diogo Jota (left) played together at club and international level. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

The well-known Saudi broadcaster Waleed al-Farraj says: “To shout ‘Messi’ at Ronaldo is acceptable within the context of the rivalry between them, but to chant the name of his deceased teammate Jota at Neves is an inappropriate act. How can you play on people’s grief like this? You should have some humanity.”

The Saudi legend Sami al-Jaber, who played at four World Cups and had a short spell in England with Wolves, sent a message to Neves: “Rúben, your presence in Saudi football means a great deal to us. As Saudis, we take pride in our values of respect and hospitality … they transcend any sporting rivalry. This behaviour does not reflect those values. I hope you know how warmly you are regarded here, and how much you belong.”

Ronaldo’s call for action was met four days later. “The Saudi Arabian Football Federation (Saff) and the Saudi Pro League (SPL) condemn the unacceptable conduct by some supporters in attendance,” a statement said, adding that the chants were inconsistent with the values of Saudi football and sportsmanship in general. Al-Taawoun have been handed a ban of around £20,000 and ordered to play two matches behind closed doors. An earlier statement said that “exploiting personal tragedies for the purpose of abuse or provocation is unacceptable behaviour that has no place in Saudi football”.

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo spoke out after fans of Al-Taawoun chanted the name of Diogo Jota to taunt Rúben Neves. Photograph: Reuters

Some felt that more could have been made of an opportunity to send a message to the rest of the league, one of zero tolerance and harsh punishments for those individuals responsible. Nobody would have complained – Al-Taawoun had condemned what happened and said it was “not representative of their supporters”. Here was a clearcut case of fans behaving badly as you are going to get.

European football has worked hard to try and stamp out offensive chants. “Stadiums in places such as Portugal and England are nowadays heavily controlled spaces,” says Simon Chadwick, professor of Afro-Eurasian Sport at Emlyon Business School in Paris. “Hence, when someone like Ronaldo encounters [verbal abuse] he will inevitably respond, thereby attracting attention from the media and others. Saudi Arabian fans need to get used to such a reaction fast.”



It is not just the international media that get involved. “Organisations such as the AFC and Fifa may even implement codes of conduct and penalties for situations like the Jota episode,” Chadwick says. “In other words, if Saudi fans and/or the Pro League can’t regulate or control the situation, then someone else will.”

With the Asian Cup coming to the country in January for the first time – and preparation for the 2034 World Cup on the way – Saudi Arabia will be hoping that such action will not be necessary.

Sports.title: ‘Disgrace to my country’ – Ex-Arsenal star hopes players return early with ‘injury’ during international break
Sports.content:
‘Disgrace to my country’ – Ex-Arsenal star hopes players return early with ‘injury’ during international break

Perry Groves has urged Arsenal players to fake injuries on international duty to ensure they're fully fit for Premier League fixtures.

Five high-profile players pulled out of Thomas Tuchel's England squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia, and Croatia.

3 Declan Rice is one of them despite making it past the 80-minute mark in five of the games he's played this season Credit: Getty

Declan Rice was among those who departed the camp, returning to the Emirates Stadium as he cited 'injury issues.'

However, the Three Lions international started for the Gunners in their 3-0 defeat to Brighton and did not appear to leave the pitch injured.

Everton's James Garner has been drafted in to replace Rice for the international clashes.

While critics have condemned players for opting out of representing their country, former Arsenal winger Groves insists the Gunners midfielder has made the right call.

On talkSPORT's Inside Gooners, he said: "You’d hope there’s conversations with Mikel Arteta and the international managers, and you would be telling your players if they’re going away with their international team to play the first game and then suddenly get a little back spasm.

"Seriously, I might be a disgrace to my country for saying it but I’m not bothered. I’ve said before that I want England to do well, but it’s not going to change my life whereas Arsenal winning does.

"Let's be honest, every Arsenal fan will be glued to their phone during the break looking at different international teams and looking at who's not playing or worrying over why players are getting subbed.

"Just go away with your national team, but don’t get injured because that Leeds game is massive. All of them are massive, but because of the way we played against Brighton, a draw against Leeds and the pressure will be ramped up."

Rice fitness concerns

Rice managed to avoid a red card in the closing seconds of the defeat at the Amex Stadium after losing his composure.

Seagulls winger Malick Yalcouye leaned into the England international in order to cause a reaction. Rice then chased down Yalcouye and swiped his legs from underneath him, sending him down to the ground.

3 Tuchel's long-term focus has now switched to Euro 2028, which will be played on home soil Credit: Getty

Additionally, the 27-year-old has been managing a persistent neural issue affecting his lower back and hamstring since early 2026, which restricted his overall impact for Tuchel's side during the summer World Cup.

During the tournament, there was multiple concerns for the midfielder including from Gabby Agbonlahor, who said: "He’s not 100 per cent, let’s put it that way."

Stuart Pearce responded: "Yeah, exactly, but you wouldn’t think it with his performances.

"[But] is that [continuing to play while nursing an issue] going to do him more damage and is he likely to break down? If there is a risk there, I think you’d be foolish as a manager to play him."

Arsenal defender Marli Salmon has also withdrawn from the England Under-18 squad due to injury.

The highly-rated prospect was handed his first senior outing of the season in the 4-2 win over Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup last Tuesday.

3 Arsenal have strong expertise in developing young stars Credit: Getty

Under-18 boss Will Antwi has since called up Chelsea defender Gabriel Sambou instead, who has represented Poland and England at youth level.

The youngster should hopefully return to action for the club's Under-21 side in a Premier League 2 fixture against Sunderland, unless Mikel Arteta includes him in the squad for the Premier League meeting with Leeds on the same day.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe reveals just how close he came to Liverpool transfer in bombshell revelation
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe reveals just how close he came to Liverpool transfer in bombshell revelation

Kylian Mbappe has confirmed he defied his mum's wishes to sign for Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool in 2017.

The France captain burst onto the scene with AS Monaco as a 16-year-old in 2015, with Europe’s big hitters already circling for his signature.



5 Mbappe showed huge promise at formative club Monaco, earning himself a big-money move to Paris Saint-Germain Credit: Getty

Two-years later, Liverpool were poised to lure the starlet to Anfield but faced competition from Real Madrid and Mbappe’s hometown club Paris Saint-Germain.

If the decision had been down to his mum and agent Fayza Lamari, then Mbappe would have been lacing up his boots for the Reds.

But Mbappe had other ideas despite having held a meeting with Klopp on board a private jet over the south of France in 2017.



The plane took off from Blackpool before landing in Nice where Klopp met with Mbappe and his mother.

Klopp then spent several hours mid-air trying to persuade Mbappe to sign for Liverpool rather than a move back to home city Paris.



Inside Mbappe's Liverpool snub

“It was while I was playing in Monaco, I had to take a decision. And yes, I was close to Liverpool,” Mbappe recalled in an interview with The Athletic.

“My mum was a big fan of Jurgen Klopp and the favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.



“I didn’t listen because I wanted to play in my city, Paris. I didn’t want to leave my country before I was someone.

“But yes, my mum was always saying ‘Liverpool – you’re going to be there, playing at Anfield, it’s going to be insane for you.’ I was like, ‘OK!’

“She went there (for) the first step of the negotiations. She went to the city, she went to the stadium, she met the people. She was like, ‘It’s a wonderful club, everybody’s so kind, it’s a family club, a big club.’

5 Klopp and maintained a strong relationship with Mbappe throughout the years Credit: getty



5 Mbappe's mum has served as his agent throughout his career Credit: X:@mbappecentral

“She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.

“All the time we were talking. ‘What do you think, Mum?’. She’d say, ‘For me, you have to go to Liverpool. I said, ‘OK, OK, OK!’ because Jurgen Klopp was an amazing manager. I met him and had a wonderful relationship with him. I had big respect for him.”

Mbappe, famously spearheaded Monaco's Ligue 1 title charge in the 2016/17 season, pipping his future club in the process.



And it was then and at the age of just 18 when Mbappe fired in 15 goals in 29 Ligue 1 matches and a further six goals in Monaco’s run to the Champions League semi-finals.

That was enough for big-spending PSG to agree an initial loan deal leading to a whopping £166million transfer for the talented forward who grew up in the Parisian Suburb of Bondy.

Despite completing his move to the Parc des Princes, links with Liverpool continued.

5 Mbappe scored 256 time for PSG to overtake Edinson Cavani as the club's all-time leading scorer Credit: Getty



Mbappe, who was nearing the end of his PSG deal in 2022, was again touted as a possible arrival at Anfield.

He later snubbed both Liverpool and Real Madrid to sign a money-spinning contract extension at PSG but later conceded that he was closer to signing for the Reds in 2017 than he was this time round.

Is the door still open for Mbappe and Liverpool?

According to French football expert Julien Laurens, a future stint at Anfield is not entirely out of the question.

"He's 27 going on 28. He will be 28 in December. I think I can see him staying there [Real Madrid] for a long time but then I don't think it's impossible to see him [leave] at some point," Laurens told talkSPORT in May.



"We know that Liverpool is the club that his mum loves. They were the team and the club that they watched the most and they were really loving.

"It's funny because all those of English teams tried to sign him when he was 12, 14, 15, 17. Some went all the way to Nice and parked the private jet at the airport just waiting in case he was not staying in Monaco and decided to leave.

5 Mbappe has picked up a host of goalscoring awards at Real Madrid Credit: Getty

"They were all there ready to make him an offer. So, maybe one day, I think he would be great in the Premier League.



"I think he's got the game for it and he watches it all."

Breaking records in La Liga

Mbappe completed a dream switch to Real Madrid in 2024 on a free transfer and has gone on to score a staggering 94 goals in 111 games for Los Blancos.

He is yet to lead the club to a major honour since his arrival, something he will hope to change under the tutelage of Jose Mourinho this season.

Mbappe is in the running for this year’s Ballon d’Or having finished as top scorer in the La Liga and the Champions League last season.

He also wrote himself into World Cup folklore this summer when he became the tournament’s all-time leading scorer with 22 goals.

Sports.title: Rory Jennings fears Chelsea could have record-breaking defensive woes this season
Sports.content:
Rory Jennings fears Chelsea could have record-breaking defensive woes this season

Chelsea have been warned they could set an unwanted Premier League record of most goals conceded this season.

The Blues' defensive issues were laid bare during Friday's 3-0 defeat at Brentford.



3 Rory Jennings fears Chelsea will set a new Premier League record for goals conceded this season Credit: Getty

Xabi Alonso's side have now conceded 12 goals in just five league matches so far this season.

It took until November for Chelsea to concede as many times last term, with the figure reached in their 13th fixture.

Chelsea warning

talkSPORT's Rory Jennings is now concerned they could make history if they do not improve defensively.



He joined Jeff Stelling and Andy Townsend on Tuesday's Breakfast show to reflect on Chelsea's performance against Brentford.

Jennings admitted: "Chelsea shouldn’t be losing at Brentford. They were worthy winners, they were far better than us, but we were the architects of our own downfall as well.



"We were so basic. Every time they broke, Kevin Schade just felt like he was in loads of space.

"You look at the way we concede goals from set pieces, that needs to be nullified."



As for the defence, he continued: "They’re on 12 goals conceded. We’re on course for Swindon Town’s record. We genuinely are.

"If it continues at this rate, we’re going to concede in excess of 90 goals this season. That needs to stop.

"I don’t quite know where it’s going so wrong. Xabi Alonso came in, it was clearly the remit to sort out the back line.

3 Austin MacPhee joined the club as set piece coach this summer but is yet to make a difference, says Jennings Credit: Getty



"We brought in Austin MacPhee, who was supposed to sort out the set pieces and what you saw at Brentford could easily have been overseen by Liam Rosenior, let alone Xabi Alonso.

"The upturn hasn’t really happened, there have been moments, there have been glimpses of the brilliance that we hoped to see, but it’s been a fairly stuttering start to the season which is fairly depressing."

Former Aston Villa set piece coach Austin MacPhee joined the club in July after leaving his role at Villa Park.

However, Brentford opened the scoring from a corner on Friday night.

Unwanted Premier League history

The three goals scored by the Bees leaves Chelsea on course to concede 91 league goals this season.



If realised, it would see them become only the second club to concede more than 90 times in a 38-game Premier League season.

3 Chelsea have already conceded 12 goals in five Premier League matches this term Credit: Getty

Sheffield United currently hold the record with 104 conceded during the 2023/24 campaign.

The Blades surpassed the previous figure set by Swindon Town in 1993/94 of 100, although Swindon's came during a 42-game season.



As for Chelsea, they have yet to keep a clean sheet this term and have conceded at least two goals in each of their Premier League outings.

The Blues currently sit tenth in the table, already eight points adrift of leaders Manchester City.

Alonso now faces a three-week international break to find a solution to their defensive woes.

Chelsea return to action at home to Bournemouth on Saturday, October 10.

Sports.title: Where to watch Portugal vs Wales plus kick-off time and team news with Ronaldo in action
Sports.content:
Where to watch Portugal vs Wales plus kick-off time and team news with Ronaldo in action

Wales kick off their Nations League campaign with an away trip to defending champions Portugal on Thursday.

The two nations experienced vastly different summers, with the Dragons set for their first competitive fixture after missing out on the World Cup following their play-off heartbreak.



4 Craig Bellamy remains Wales' manager after turning down Burnley Credit: Getty

Craig Bellamy's side were beaten by Bosnia and Herzegovina on penalties in their semi-final in March to deny them a place in this summer's showpiece in North America.

Now though, Wales have returned to the top tier of the Nations League after winning their League B group in 2024.

And they face a stern test in their opening game, with 2025 competition winners Portugal up first in Lisbon.



Following their last-16 exit at the World Cup, a new era has begun for the Selecao das Quinas with Jorge Jesus succeeding Roberto Martinez in the dugout.

One thing that hasn't changed though is Cristiano Ronaldo's presence in the national team.



The 41-year-old has been named in the Portugal squad despite sparking retirement fears following his country's World Cup exit, and is now looking to add to his record-breaking international goal haul.

Portugal vs Wales: Date and how to follow

This Nations League Group A4 game will take place on Thursday, September 24.



Kick off at the Estadio Jose Alvalade, Lisbon is scheduled for 7:45pm UK time.

Fans will be able to watch the action live on BBC iPlayer and BBC One Wales in the UK.

talkSPORT's Kick Off will also provides regular updates from the clash with Natalie Sawyer and Dean Saunders presenting.

4 Cristiano Ronaldo is the most-capped men's international player of all time Credit: Getty



Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.



Portugal vs Wales: Team news

Wales face an immediate uphill task against Portugal, with a number of number absentees leaving them rather depleted.

Star man Harry Wilson was forced to withdraw due to a quad injury, before Nathan Broadhead and goalkeeper Karl Darlow did the same.

4 Harry Wilson has withdrawn from the Wales squad for their upcoming internationals against Portugal, Denmark and Norway Credit: Getty

In their place, an uncapped duo of veteran Leicester keeper David Cornell and Huddersfield forward Joe Taylor have been called up, as well as Reading midfielder Charlie Savage.



Adding to Bellamy's woes, key defenders Joe Rodon and Dylan Lawlor had already been ruled out of the upcoming fixtures through injury.

As for Portugal, they can call on a strong of huge names, with Ronaldo the headline act.

Elsewhere, the European nations' squad also boasts Ruben Dias, Joao Cancelo, Nuno Mendes, Vitinha, Joao Neves and Bruno Fernandes.

Wales squad:

Goalkeepers: David Cornell (Leicester), Danny Ward (Wrexham), Tom King (Everton)



Defenders: Jay Dasilva (Coventry City), Jayden Lienou (Leeds United), Ben Davies (Tottenham Hotspur), Rhys Norrington-Davies (Sheffield United), Chris Mepham (West Bromwich Albion), Ben Cabanago (Swansea City), Neco Williams (Nottingham Forest)

Midfielders: Connor Roberts (Burnley), Ethan Ampadu (Leeds United), Josh Sheehan (Bolton Wanderers), Jordan James (Wolverhampton Wanderers- On loan from Stade Rennais), Liam Cullen (Leicester City), Joel Colwill (Cardiff City), Charlie Savage (Reading)

Forwards: Joe Taylor (Huddersfield), Cian Ashford (Cardiff City), Brennan Johnson (Everton), Sorba Thomas (Hull City), Cameron Congreve (KVC Westerlo), Lewis Koumas (Liverpool), Kieffer Moore (Wrexham), Mark Harris (Oxford United), Dan James (Leeds United), David Brooks (Bournemouth), Wes Burns (Leicester City).

Portugal v Wales: What has been said?

Despite having a depleted squad up against one of Europe's strongest nations, Wales midfielder Jordan James insisted Wales won't be star-struck in their tough opening international.



"Obviously they're the best players in the world at the end of the day, you can't really sugarcoat it," James said.

"They've got Champions League winners, they've got these kinds of things.

4 As well as Ronaldo, Portugal boast PFA Players' Player of the Year Bruno Fernandes Credit: AFP

"I think we're always underdogs. We're used to it, so hopefully we can use that to benefit ourselves.



"You can't count us out. We've got a puncher's chance at the end of the day and we're going there to sort of cause an upset."

Sports.title: Man United target reveals ‘no-brainer’ reason why he snubbed summer transfer
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall has lifted the lid on his decision to sign a new long-term deal with Newcastle United.

The England defender was the subject of considerable transfer interest from Manchester United throughout the summer.



3 Hall has revealed the reason behind his decision to snub United for a new Newcastle contract Credit: Getty

However, he opted against a potential move to Old Trafford in order to commit his future to the Magpies.

Hall penned a new five-year deal through to 2030 earlier this month.

His contract extension does not include a release clause in a further boost to Newcastle.

Why did Hall snub United?

The 22-year-old has now admitted new manager Matthias Jaissle and the club's own transfer business contributed to his decision.



Speaking to the Newcastle Chronicle, Hall was asked if the transfer interest during the summer affected him.

He explained: "No, honestly, it didn’t. I guess whenever you’re linked to another team, you know that you’re doing something right.



"I guess it’s just a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, how you are as a person.

"I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I knew how much I love playing here and I knew that since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.



"After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club and I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer really to sign."

United were keen on a move for Hall throughout the transfer window, with enquiries made over his availability.

3 Jaissle's impact since joining the club played a part in Hall committing his future to Newcastle Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The Red Devils were ultimately unable to secure his signature, though.



Newcastle under Jaissle

Hall has since played every minute for Newcastle across all competitions so far this term as well as earning an England recall.

His goal against Hull City on Saturday added to two assists across seven appearances under Jaissle.

The German was appointed as Eddie Howe's successor in August ahead of the start of the new season.

Meanwhile, Newcastle spent almost £280million in the summer rebuilding their squad.



It followed the departures of key men Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon.

3 Hall has already scored once and provided two assists from left-back this season Credit: Getty

However, they have invested heavily in the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Nico Gonzalez and Bazoumana Toure.

Jaissle's side returned to winning ways against Hull at the weekend following a shock 4-1 defeat at Leeds United.



The result leaves Newcastle ninth in the Premier League after five matches.

They return to action away to Coventry City on October 12 following the international break.

Sports.title: Fabian Hurzeler says Brighton planning for next summer’s exits – but why he’s ‘delighted’ for players
Sports.content:
Fabian Hurzeler says Brighton planning for next summer’s exits – but why he’s ‘delighted’ for players

Fabian Hurzeler has admitted he feels 'delighted' when clubs show interest in his Brighton players.

The Seagulls boss once again saw several key names depart his squad during the summer.



3 Hurzeler admits he feels 'delighted' when clubs show transfer interest in his Brighton players Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Carlos Baleba and Jan Paul van Hecke were the notable exits from the Amex following last season's eighth place finish in the Premier League.

The pair joined Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur, respectively, for a combined £122million.

However, Brighton have since made an impressive start to the campaign under Hurzeler.



His side sit third in the table after five matches having beaten Arsenal 3-0 at home on Saturday.

Hurzeler's honest view on Brighton sales

Hurzeler joined Jim White and Simon Jordan live on talkSPORT on Tuesday to discuss his side's transfer policy amid their ongoing success.



When asked for his honest feelings when bids come in for the likes of Baleba and Van Hecke, he told White & Jordan: "Honestly, I feel first of all really, really delighted for the players because what I always do as a coach is build a lot of relationships towards them.

"I think that is also one of our key strengths that we not only take care of the player, we really take care of the human beings and our environment.



"Therefore, you automatically build a social bond towards them and this social bond creates this being delighted for them, really happy that they have this great opportunity.

"Besides that, of course I can’t be happy losing one of my best players. I know again, that’s part of my identity. That’s why I see it more as an opportunity.

"I’m not this guy who is frustrated or complains about these things. I see it (as) ‘alright, let’s go and face this opportunity’. Let’s try to make the best out of it.

3 Baleba became the latest key player to leave Brighton after his £70million move to United Credit: Getty



"Let’s try to rebuild our style of play to make sure all these new players are getting integrated as quickly as possible and can add themselves how I want to express themselves.

"That’s really, really strong in our environment. We don’t try to change characters, really try to let them be how they can be, then they can show what they’re capable of doing and then we try to find solutions together with them."

Brighton expect transfer interest

Last season's eighth place finish also saw Brighton qualify for the Conference League, marking just their second-ever European campaign.

After beating Tromso on aggregate in August, the Seagulls are into the league phase of the competition.



Meanwhile, Hurzeler has guided his side into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup by beating Manchester United earlier this month.

Brighton's form so far this term could see more interest follow in current stars such as Charalampos Kostoulas and Ferdi Kadioglu.

3 Brighton are braced for more bids next summer, with Kostoulas tipped to attract interest Credit: Getty

The duo have been amongst their standout performers this season, with Kostoulas scoring four goals and adding three assists in eight appearances across all competitions.



Hurzeler added: "I think when we are successful as a club, we can't avoid these kinds of bids, they will come, and then it's about us, what decision will we do then?

"If we are successful as a club, you will shine as an individual, and they need to understand that, they need to be fully, fully committed to this club.

"They need to be fully committed for this badge because they know if we are successful as a club, then they get in the spotlight, and in the end, there are some players who have big dreams.

"There are some players who have visions, who I want to go to, and I think they should have it because these kinds of visions, these kinds of dreams, they promise you to never give up these things you want to achieve."



Hurzeler has been in charge of Brighton since 2024 having replaced Roberto De Zerbi in the dugout.

He has since secured back-to-back eighth place finishes despite Joao Pedro being amongst those to leave the club last summer.

The 33-year-old was rewarded with a new three-year deal by the club in May which runs until the summer of 2029.

Sports.title: I never got an England cap – I hope Declan Rice and Cole Palmer’s withdrawals are genuine
Sports.content:
I never got an England cap – I hope Declan Rice and Cole Palmer’s withdrawals are genuine

Steve Bruce could not fathom a world in which the quintet of withdrawals from the England squad weren't genuine.

Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford were all confirmed to have pulled out of international duty on Monday, with Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner called up as their replacements.

3 Rashford has started all but two of Manchester United's games this season Credit: AFP

What are the injuries sustained by those who withdrew from England duty?

In the case of Palmer, talkSPORT understands he has picked up a small injury, but there are also concerns from Chelsea about his load management.

As for Rashford, he is said to be dealing with a hip injury while Mainoo has an issue.

Newcastle full-back Livramento felt 'some discomfort' in his knee and was sent for scans ahead of the Magpies' 2-1 win over Hull on Saturday.

Rice, who revealed during the World Cup he'd been battling nerve pain in his hamstring since December, is reported to have withdrawn over load management concerns given he's started six games across all competitions for Arsenal this term.

All five players are fortunate enough to have won multiple caps for England, meaning they have not been robbed of making their international debut.

Steve Bruce's verdict on the five players who pulled out of England duty

But for Bruce, seeing players pass up the opportunity to do something he never did in his glittering career would not sit well unless they had a valid reason.

"I never got an England cap," Bruce said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"And the one thing, when I sit here now, is have that regret that I never represented my country.

"It is a strange one, that's for sure. You just hope they genuinely have a knock and they need a rest for a couple of weeks.

"I feel for some of these lads, to be perfectly honest. They've had a long, long summer playing in World Cups.

3 Rice made 55 appearances for the Gunners last term, 49 of which were starts Credit: AFP

"But to pull out, if you're not quite right, is an awful conundrum.

Bruce's only senior international experience came in the form of a solitary cap for England's B team in 1987.

The 65-year-old is considered as one of the best players who did not win an England cap given he made over 400 appearances for Manchester United.

Throughout his stint with the Red Devils, Bruce helped them win three Premier League titles, three FA Cups and the League Cup.

But when it came to England, the likes of Mark Wright, Tony Adams and Des Walker were preferred over Bruce.

Did Steve Bruce ever get the chance to pay for England?

Bruce did eventually receive the opportunity to win his first Three Lions cap when Terry Venables was in charge.

3 Bruce was there when Man United ended a 26-year wait for a league title in 1993 Credit: Getty

However, Bruce explained in an interview with the Daily Express in 2014 why he felt compelled to turn it down.

"My best mate, Bryan Robson, was Terry Venables' assistant and he was desperate for me to get a cap," Bruce said.

"I turned it down. I was close to 35 and I said, 'I'm sorry, I would rather not have had an international career than just a sympathy cap."

When do England play in the international break?

For those who did not have to withdraw from the England squad, they will face World Cup champions Spain at Wembley on September 26, live on talkSPORT.

Thomas Tuchel's side then travel to Prague for a match against Czechia three days later.

Another away clash follows on October 3 when England take on Croatia in Rijeka before rounding out the international break back on home soil against Czechia on October 6.

Sports.title: Fabian Hurzeler reveals Brighton blueprint for huge Arsenal win but denies ‘perfect’ performance
Sports.content:
Fabian Hurzeler has detailed the game plan that saw his Brighton side crush champions Arsenal 3-0 in the Premier League.

Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas fired the Seagulls into a two-goal lead by half-time, with Chema Andres grabbing the third against the holders before the hour mark on a memorable afternoon.

3 Brighton boss Hurzeler has explained how he masterminded the huge weekend win against champions Arsenal Credit: AFP

Arsenal, whose midfielder Declan Rice was lucky to avoid a red card, had the lion's share of possession but failed to make the most of it.

Brighton ended the champions' four-match win streak and extended their own unbeaten run in the league to five this season as they sit third on ten points, earning them an A in our top flight grades.

They are also the fourth side after Manchester United, Bournemouth and Manchester City to beat Arsenal in the Premier League in 2026.

Hurzeler produced a hugely impressive result that has rightly earned plaudits across the division, and he was on hand to tell talkSPORT just how he went about doing it.

Speaking on Brighton's approach against Arsenal when appearing on White and Jordan, he said: "We focused on us, really. We wanted to win the small battles first, what I mean is win the first header, win the first tackle, win the first throw-in, win the first corner.

"It sounds a little bit old school but it really was our approach because when you win these small battles, then you grow into the game.

"Then you can maybe create a bigger chance, then you can create a bigger win of scoring a goal. But first of all, it's getting into this game, having this commitment to our style of play, to our principles, and then winning the small battles.

"When you win the small battles, the players gain confidence, the players create self-belief, the players really trust each other. We grew into this game, and we also had the right moments on our side."

Brighton were 'exceptional', but not 'perfect'

None of Coventry City, Aston Villa, Chelsea and Sunderland, as well as Napoli in the Champions League and Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup, could beat Arsenal in their clashes - Brighton are an exception.

They showed intensity right from kick-off and managed to exploit a sense of nervousness from the Gunners, who played like anything but title defenders.

3 Hurzeler believes much of their success in the three-goal display came from winning 'the small battles' Credit: Getty

Host Jim White even went as far as to suggest that Brighton may well have delivered a perfect performance, but a humble Hurzeler was not one to agree.

"Our philosophy is we want to play intense football, having a good balance between defensive ability and controlling the game in possession.

"Therefore, if you want to control the game in possession, you need to have this intensity to win the ball back as quickly as possible.

"You need players who have this commitment to our pressing and I think that was definitely key - they played, we scored, and that was our commitment from the first second.

"Was it a perfect game? I'm a perfectionist, I wouldn't say it was a perfect game.

"There's still things to improve. But, overall, our challenge now will be to make these kind of exceptional performances normal. This is the challenge we have now.

3 Hurzeler has insisted that, whilst the performance was strong, it wasn't perfect and there is still room for improvement Credit: AFP

"We have this phrase, 'We want to challenge the establishment'. Challenging the establishment doesn't mean to challenge them in one-to-one games, you have to challenge them when you're not playing against them.

"So, we have to be consistent in performances and these kind of performances, they have to get normal for us and that, I think, is the biggest challenge we can set ourselves."

Sports.title: Spanish clubs eye swoop for Alejandro Garnacho as ex-Man United star's Aston Villa spell unravels - with £43m attacker playing just 31 MINUTES under Unai Emery
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho is being monitored by clubs in La Liga as he struggles to make an impression during his early days at Aston Villa. The Argentine moved to Villa from Chelsea in the summer on a season’s loan deal, which will become a permanent £43million move if Garnacho hits certain targets. Chelsea describe these conditions as ‘easily achievable’. Yet Garnacho is yet to start a game for Villa and has only played 31 minutes of competitive action for Unai Emery’s team. He has been an unused substitute in each of the last two matches and may not even have made the bench for Villa’s 3-2 win at Tottenham had Brazilian winger Alysson not been ruled out with injury. At this stage there are no thoughts from any of the relevant parties about changing the conditions of the deal. Yet Daily Mail Sport understands that clubs in Spain’s top flight are watching the situation closely. Even though he is an Argentina international, Garnacho was born in Madrid and spent time in the Atletico Madrid academy before moving to Manchester United in 2020, aged 16. La Liga clubs are eyeing a move for Alejandro Garnacho, who has played just 31 minutes on loan at Aston Villa this season Garnacho was signed to play on the left. But youngster George Hemmings has made outstanding progress and is now ahead of him, as are Emi Buendia and Ibrahim Mbaye. John McGinn can operate across the attacking line and Alysson has also made considerable strides. These are still early days in the season and if Garnacho shines during Villa’s training camp in Seville during the international break, his chance may come in October and November. ‘Continue working. Work, work, train, work,' said Emery when asked about Garnacho after Villa’s win at Coventry in the Carabao Cup. 'When he can have minutes to play, try to play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now. 'George Hemmings is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. Mbaye also responded well. 'We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs.’
