Sports.title: 'We lost the edge, what's the point?': Liverpool's £241m signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz couldn't settle because team-mates 'didn't care' after Diogo Jota's death, says Andy Robertson
Sports.content:
'We lost the edge, what's the point?': Liverpool's £241m signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz couldn't settle because team-mates 'didn't care' after Diogo Jota's death, says Andy Robertson

Former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson has admitted that Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz struggled to settle in at Anfield last season because the squad 'didn't care about football' following the death of Diogo Jota.

Jota was tragically killed in a car accident alongside his brother Andre Silva in northern Spain in July 2025. The 28-year-old had been on his way to report to Merseyside for pre-season training.

In the same summer, Liverpool purchased both Isak and Wirtz for a combined £241million. However, both players struggled in what was a difficult season for the Reds, as they finished fifth in the Premier League.

Robertson, who is now at Tottenham following nine years at Anfield, was a close friend of Jota's and, during an episode of The Overlap, has explained how the forward's sudden death affected the settling-in period of the big-money signings.

An emotional Robertson said: 'It's difficult to describe or talk about really because what we went through, it was horrendous.

'If I'm talking about the new signings, they're coming into a club that is heartbroken. And that is where I felt so sorry for these guys because they had signed and had signed for big money and all.

Former Liverpool defender has opened up on how the death of Diogo Jota affected the Reds squad last season

The Scot said that Alexander Isak (left) and Florian Wirtz (right) struggled to settle at Anfield because of how Jota's death impacted the club

'If I'm talking about football, it took them months to settle in because we didn't care about football. That was the truth of it because we just lost one of your best mates in the changing room.'

Robertson was entering the final year of his Reds deal, having already won everything there is to win during his time at the club, when he learned that his friend and team-mate had passed away suddenly.

The Scotland international confessed that the Liverpool squad 'lost' their determination on the pitch due to the tragedy, which led to poor results, and ultimately, a trophyless season.

He continued: 'I think all footballers we all have that edge, don't we? I think when you lose that edge sometimes, then you can't perform to your best. And I think last season we lost the edge.

'When I look back on it, we lost that maybe determination a little bit, and things like that because I know at times we were going "What's the point?" Look at what Jotsy's family are going through, look at his kids.

'But yeah, we were grieving as a group. It was our mate at the end of the day. He's not a footballer to us. He was a team-mate, he was a friend, he was an everything.'

“He was our mate. He wasn’t just a footballer to us.” 😞



Andy Robertson opens up about the tragic passing of Diogo Jota and the profound impact it had on everyone at Liverpool. ❤️ pic.twitter.com/KcCuSvAwLa — The Overlap (@WeAreTheOverlap) September 22, 2026

Robertson was a very close friend of Jota during their five years together at Anfield

The Scot had gone to Jota's wedding weeks before he died before attending his funeral

Jota and his brother were on a road trip to the northern Spanish port city of Santander, in order to catch a ferry to the UK as Jota was due to return to Liverpool for his sixth pre-season on Merseyside.

Jota was driving after being advised by medical professionals not to travel by plane following lung surgery earlier in the summer.

He had married his childhood sweetheart Rute Cardoso at a church in Porto, Portugal, just 11 days before the devastating collision, which Robertson and fellow former Liverpool team-mate Caoimhin Kelleher attended.

'For us, it was incredibly difficult,' Robertson added. 'I mean, the week before he died, I was at his wedding.

'That's one of the most difficult things you will ever go through. Seeing him on the happiest day of his life then the next week you are seeing his family torn apart.'

Sports.title: 'I'd blow up the sport and change it forever': EDDIE HEARN reveals his radical masterplan for PREM rugby - and the special clause in Henry Pollock's new Northampton contract after England star 'left hundreds of thousands on the table'
Sports.content:
'I'd blow up the sport and change it forever': EDDIE HEARN reveals his radical masterplan for PREM rugby - and the special clause in Henry Pollock's new Northampton contract after England star 'left hundreds of thousands on the table'

Over in Monaco, Eddie Hearn is already plotting his next rugby move. The ink has barely dried on Henry Pollock’s new Northampton contract but the promoter does not want to stop there.

Hearn will fly back to the UK on his private jet for meetings with the sport’s establishment next month. He will sit down with PREM Rugby executives to discuss a formal partnership that extends far beyond adding an extra zero to Pollock’s pay cheque.

Hearn has already flipped the world of boxing, darts and snooker. He has witnessed the boom of Anthony Joshua, Luke Littler and Ronnie O’Sullivan and soon he will decide if he can have a similar effect on rugby.

‘We've had 50 rugby players come on to us since we started working with Henry, asking us to represent them,’ Hearn told Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s not going to be lucrative enough for us as a business to start a management company for rugby players. We wanted a couple of the big guys, so we signed Henry and Finn Russell.

‘If we're going to move more into rugby, I think it’s at a deeper level – getting involved in the infrastructure, changing the sport from the grassroots all the way up to the very top. We come in and we reorganise and reinvent sports. That's what we do.

'It's not about PREM Rugby saying: "Eddie, do you want to be a consultant?” I’ve not got time to do that. If we come in, we come in as a partnership with them to blow it up and actually change the sport for ever.

The ink has only just dried on Henry Pollock's new Northampton contract, but Eddie Hearn (left) is already plotting his next move in rugby

‘Henry left a lot of money on the table to stay with Northampton and I think that should be applauded in today's world,’ says Hearn

‘Boxing was dead before we came in 20 years ago. Darts was non-existent commercially and now it's a huge commercial beast. Snooker was living in the 1980s. We don't miss. Look at the foundations, the history and the brand that you already have in rugby, compared to those sports.

‘I sit in those rooms with all these big broadcasters that spend billions of dollars a year on sports, and rugby is not particularly spoken about in a very high regard commercially. I know what needs to be done and I don't even think it's that tough a job. I've got meetings with PREM Rugby in two weeks' time and after that meeting, I will probably decide whether I'm going to move into rugby or not.’

It may surprise many when Hearn describes himself as a ‘traditionalist’. He scoffs at proposals to take Six Nations Tests to the USA – claiming the international game is ‘flying’ and ‘making a fortune’.

He agrees with the protectionist principle to keep English talent in the PREM but insists the sport must scrap the salary cap if it wants to dictate terms to its players. Pollock settled on a three-year contract worth around £450,000-a-year with Northampton but he could have commanded ‘three times more money’ in the open market.

‘Henry left a lot of money on the table to stay with Northampton and I think that should be applauded in today's world,’ said Hearn. ‘You always hear a lot of noise from me but really, behind closed doors, he was never leaving.

'I said, “Look, you can make double, treble, tell me what you want”. The first time we discussed it, he said, "I don't want to leave”. He loves Northampton, he loves the people, and he wants to win championships.

‘It's quite unusual for me to sit in a meeting and tell someone they could earn two or three times more money in this other deal and not even entertain it. That shows me he's a competitor.

At times it feels like Pollock is operating in a different ecosystem to the rest of the rugby world. Yet despite the hype and the headlines, he has never looked close to leaving Franklin’s Gardens

Pollock settled on a three-year contract worth around £450,000-a-year with Northampton

'Once people know Henry's available, the bigger clubs with big money want to look at him and think, “If we can bring Henry to the club and we unveil him in our jersey, this is huge for the club”. There were a number of those domestically and internationally, like Japan.

‘It’s good to keep our stars in the country. But as the disparity becomes too much between the different countries, we could get in a position where players turn their back on international rugby, which would be a disaster, right?

'How can you have a salary cap, where the players don’t really earn a lot of money, yet say to them, “By the way, you can't leave and earn a load of money abroad because if you do, then we won't allow you to play for England”. You're handcuffed. It's rubbish. You've got Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane playing football internationally but they have the freedom to earn big money at Spurs or wherever.

‘I sometimes see comments from that old guard within rugby. “Oh, not sure about these comments. We don't do that. How are you supposed to do that with a salary cap." What's wrong with one team tearing up the Premier League and another one of the minnows trying to survive and compete with the big boys? You see it all the time in Premier League football. Listen to me, you’ve got to get out of the 1970s, 80s or 90s or wherever you are.

'I hate people that come in and just bastardise the sport and do all these funky things. The infrastructure, the clubs, the brands that that exist are actually OK. I just think there's got to be changes and one of them is salary caps.

‘Now it's time to take the shackles off, take the stabilisers off, and let the players earn their money. You want these big boys – Red Bull (at Newcastle), Dyson (at Bath) - to have a little bit of ego about them. Make people spend money.

'The fans win if they get better players, international players. The broadcasters turn around and go, "This is great. We've got even more big names now. There's a real buzz around rugby, we'll put more money in”. The sponsors will look at it and say, "Wow, bigger audience numbers, greater viewership across the sport. We'll be reinvesting”. It's about the ecosystem.’

At times it feels like Pollock is operating in a different ecosystem to the rest of the rugby world. His profile has rocketed, growing at a faster rate than he has been able to accumulate Test caps for England. His name was pedalled constantly during the summer tour of South Africa, where he became public enemy No1 among the Springbok fans.

'It's time to take the shackles off, take the stabilisers off, and let the players earn their money'

‘Look at the storylines in South Africa, all that was being talked about was Pollock,’ said Hearn. ‘It’s quite funny, when I had a meeting with Pollock on my boat during the summer, two of the crew are South African. They were like, "We smashed you up, boy”. I’m thinking, “This is great”. This is storylines. When I go on holiday, kids say, “Oh, you got Pollock!”. This is what we want.

‘Look at look at guys like Fin Smith. You see all his team-mates dancing around in the changing room. Unbelievable characters. You've got to do almost the job that we're doing with Henry on all of the star players within the team.

‘We'll be announcing four or five deals for Henry in the next two or three weeks, and we have got every brand, every sector, every industry. We’re having conversations with companies that we don't generally have conversations with. I'm talking about major financial institutions that never look at boxing, never look at darts, sometimes look at snooker.'

Yet despite the hype and the headlines, Pollock has never looked close to leaving Franklin’s Gardens. However, he still harbours ambitions away from the club, with clauses written into his new contract that allow him to explore wider opportunities.

‘I was really pleased with Northampton,' added Hearn. 'They really stepped up financially, they were smart, they were commercially open-minded because they know the importance of keeping Henry at the club.

‘Henry likes sevens and he obviously loves the thought of winning Olympic gold. That doesn't mean he's going to leave the principal format, but the deal with Northampton allows him to look at other opportunities around that.

‘If he's going to turn down three times more money to go elsewhere, you also can't handcuff him in a position that's going to limit him commercially. You could be talking about a sevens tournament, an all-stars game in Las Vegas. But the club is what matters to him.’

With Hearn in Pollock’s corner, anything could happen.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta rewarded for title triumph with bumper new Arsenal deal that could take him beyond 10 years at club
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta rewarded for title triumph with bumper new Arsenal deal that could take him beyond 10 years at club

Mikel Arteta has agreed a new long-term contract with Arsenal which is set to take his tenure at the club beyond 10 years.

The 44-year-old, who led the Gunners to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season, is already the longest serving boss in the top flight having been in charge of Arsenal since December 2019.

After taking the club from 10th position to league champions, as well as reaching the Champions League final, Arteta has been rewarded with a lucrative deal which will boost his current salary - which is worth up to £15million with bonuses.

It is also set to see him enter a decade at the Emirates, with the deal’s length still to be announced. His current terms expire next summer but this new agreement will shut down any speculation over his future.

Daily Mail Sport understands that talks began early in the year with confidence from both Arteta and Arsenal for months that a new contract would be agreed.

CEO Richard Garlick last month said Arteta's future at the club will be ‘resolved very shortly’, adding: ‘Mikel wants to be at Arsenal and we want Mikel at Arsenal. It's only a matter of time before we put that into a new contract.’

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has been rewarded after guiding Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season

Arteta led the title celebrations at Selhurst Park on the last day of the 2025-26 season

Arteta said last week: ‘They (the fans) don’t have to worry about any of that (contract talks) because I want to be here.

‘I’m extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with.’

The Spaniard was already the Premier League’s highest paid manager, yet his new terms could put him among the most well-paid bosses in world football.

It’s been previously reported that only Al-Hilal’s Simone Inzaghi and Atletico Madrid‘s Diego Simeone were on bigger pay-packets than Arteta, which are £22.34m and £20.19m respectively.

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Latest in JJ Gabriel saga as key deadline looms and super agents fight over wonderkid, tug-of-war over academy star and 'very positive' milestone for new stadium
Sports.content:
Manchester United have two weeks to convince JJ Gabriel that his future lies at Old Trafford as the teenage star tries to force a move to a European rival.

Gabriel’s 16th birthday is in 14 days’ time on October 6, when he can be legally represented by an agent and join a foreign club using his Irish passport. He has already held talks with Real Madrid and Barcelona.

United still hope the issue can be resolved and they can persuade Gabriel and his family that they are the right club for him.

The Old Trafford hierarchy are refusing to bow to Gabriel’s demand to rip up his registration and leave as a free agent – a move that could earn the club just £300,000 in compensation for a player who might soon be worth millions.

If United insist on keeping him until the end of the season, the 15-year-old could launch an appeal to the Premier League or even FIFA.

Because of his age, it would be difficult for United to stop his family from relocating to Spain or another European country, particularly if they can make a convincing argument it is being driven by a business opportunity unrelated to football and not because clubs are offering them a financial inducement.

JJ Gabriel’s 16th birthday is in 14 days’ time on October 6, when he can be legally represented by an agent and join a foreign club using his Irish passport

The Old Trafford hierarchy are refusing to bow to Gabriel’s demand to rip up his registration and leave as a free agent

FIFA regulations also include specific criteria over a young player’s education, but there are ways around those rules such as home-schooling.

Given that Gabriel has not been seen at United for nearly two weeks since scoring a hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League win over Sabah, and there is no expectation that he will be back, the club may be left with little choice but to accept the situation and try to strike the best deal in the circumstances.

Gabriel’s name was still on the bottom of the squad listed in the match programme for United’s Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton last Wednesday – when he could feasibly have become the club’s youngest-ever debutant – but it had been deleted when they played at Fulham on Sunday.

United insiders say the club’s main priority is Gabriel’s welfare, pointing out that the club still have a duty of care while he remains their player.

The youngster is said to be concerned over his pathway at United after he didn’t play for the senior side against Sabah in the Champions League. His family have privately questioned whether the club can match Europe’s top clubs and Premier League rivals like Manchester City and Arsenal by giving him the right environment to maximise his talent.

Gabriel’s camp are believed to have held talks with Real Madrid, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain on a trip to Spain and France last week.

Although he cannot formally have an agent until he turns 16, the family can take advice without having formal representation. Ali Barat is believed to have been involved in discussions so far, but he is facing competition from rival super agent Jorge Mendes.

Gabriel was included on the list of United players in the matchday programme for the Brighton game (left), but conspicuous by his absence in the equivalent at Fulham (right)

Gabriel (pictured meeting Lamine Yamal two years ago) has already held talks with Barca and Real Madrid

Ben backed over shin dig

Slovenia defender Jaka Bijol has told Benjamin Sesko to ignore comments from former United stars Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt questioning his shin injury.

United’s £74million striker has had to pull out of the upcoming Nations League games over the problem, which dates back to last season, meaning he won’t have played for his country for more than a year.

The former United duo appeared to cast doubt over Sesko’s injury on their podcast, The Good, The Bad and The Football. Scholes told Sesko: ‘If it isn’t broken, just wear your shinpads.’ Butt added: ‘You’re a player – you either break your shin or you play!’

The comments haven’t gone down well in Slovenia, but Leeds defender Bijol has backed Sesko to rise above it.

‘I hope and believe that Beni knows how to distance himself from this kind of pressure,’ he said. ‘When things aren't going your best on the pitch and you have certain doubts, reading things like this can make your confidence even worse.

‘He shouldn't pay too much attention to it, since we all know what quality he has. He himself knows what kind of footballer he is, and I think he always shows it with incredible things on the pitch.’

It isn’t the first time that Scholes and Butt have ruffled feathers among the United squad. In January, Lisandro Martinez challenged Scholes to go round to his house and repeat comments he made before the Manchester derby.

Scholes had joked that Martinez facing Erling Haaland was such a mismatch that the 6ft 5in City striker would pick up the 5ft 9in United defender and throw him in the back of the net.

Slovenia defender Jaka Bijol has told Benjamin Sesko (pictured) to ignore comments from former United stars Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt questioning his shin injury

Tug-of-war over teen ace

Speaking of young players being fast-tracked, Confidential can reveal United’s Under 18s midfielder Jay McEvoy is at the centre of a tug-of-war between Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland over his international allegiance.

The 17-year-old, who was recently drafted into first-team training as United look to show him a pathway for his development, is wanted by both nations having represented them in younger age groups.

Both the Irish FA, which looks after Northern Ireland, and the Football Association of Ireland, which governs football in Republic of Ireland, have made pitches to McEvoy and his family.

Confidential has been told Northern Ireland manager Michael O’Neill is aware of the situation and is set to sit down with the player and his family in the coming weeks in a decisive move to keep him out of the clutches of the FAI.

McEvoy, who has been at United since Under-9s level, has hit form at the right time in recent weeks and is standing out among his peers, leading to United offering him a professional contract.

United, along with the IFA and the FAI, have some convincing to do to show the midfielder and his representatives the long-term direction of travel before he commits on both fronts.

Both Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland are trying to persuade United midfielder Jay McEvoy to represent them

Reds OK as stars dash off

United are comfortable with the security arrangements at Fulham on Sunday after video footage emerged of Bruno Fernandes, Marcus Rashford and Matheus Cunha walking through crowds of fans in the busy streets around Craven Cottage.

The United players were bound for international duty and were rushing to catch flights which had been agreed beforehand with their national teams.

Even though Craven Cottage is one of the Premier League’s less intimidating grounds, the volume of fans still outside meant the three players had to be escorted by police and security stewards as they made their way to waiting cars.

United sources have told Confidential the situation was planned because they knew the road directly outside the stadium was closed for an hour after the game, and some players were in a hurry to get away. Rashford later pulled out of the England squad through injury along with his United team-mate Kobbie Mainoo.

Harry’s agent split

Confidential has learned Harry Amass has separated from long-standing agent Jason Mac and joined M+C Saatchi Football, the agency launched in conjunction with Jamie Redknapp.

The 19-year-old failed to secure a move away in the summer, in part due to United not being able to recruit Newcastle’s Lewis Hall or any other left back, as well as uncertainty around whether he would be leaving permanently or on loan. Burnley were among the sides to hold talks over Amass.

The move to Amass' new agency was made in August but there is some doubt over just how long that arrangement will last, with many determined to take over representation of the United teen.

Multiple agents are circling to try and convince Amass and his family to join their stable of players, with the youngster a January target for teams in the Championship, Germany and the Netherlands.

Amass has found opportunities hard to come by this season despite United being short at left back with Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui all preferred so far by boss Michael Carrick.

Having the right representation will be key to lining up a move – likely a loan – in the January window.

Multiple agents are circling to try and convince left back Harry Amass to join their stable of players

Jose up to his old tricks

When Jose Mourinho turned up for his press conference after losing the Madrid derby on Sunday with ‘evidence’ showing that two Atletico players should have been sent off, Confidential was reminded of the Portuguese coach’s early days at United a decade ago.

Back in 2016, Mourinho asked club staff to discreetly circulate visual evidence to the media of what he saw as unfair refereeing decisions against his team only to be told that is not the way United work.

On this occasion, Mourinho took matters into his own hands after Real Madrid’s 2-1 defeat and arrived to speak to the Spanish media armed with printouts of screenshots to back up his claims that Cristian Romero and Lee Kang-in should have been shown red cards in the first half.

There were echoes of his predecessor at Old Trafford, Louis van Gaal, walking into a press conference at Carrington in February 2015 with four pages of statistics challenging Sam Allardyce’s claims that United had played long-ball football in a game against West Ham.

Baleba's birthday treat

A nice moment on what was a difficult afternoon down at Fulham as £70million summer signing Carlos Baleba, in the matchday squad for the first time, gifted his No 20 shirt to a young fan celebrating his birthday in the away end.

The youngster, lifted up by his dad, was picked out by Baleba, who passed on his jersey in what is the very first of his United career. Talk about setting the bar high for everyone else’s presents!

New stadium edges closer

Today marks another milestone in plans to build a new £2billion stadium to replace Old Trafford as the borough council’s public consultation process over the wider regeneration project formally draws to a close.

The council have held sessions at four venues throughout the local area since they unveiled plans at Old Trafford in July – at Trafford Town Hall, Media City, Gorse Hill Studios and Metro Sports Club – and listened to comments from hundreds of residents as well as many more members of the public who gave their feedback online.

United had representatives in attendance at all the meetings, and the engagement process is said to have been very positive. The council will use the feedback to tweak their masterplan which is expected to create 48,000 jobs and 15,000 new homes, boosting the UK economy by £7.3billion-a-year.

The next step in the process will be for United to consult with fans over the design of the new stadium. The club’s CEO of new stadium development, Collette Roche, said at the council launch in July that the controversial tent design unveiled at Foster + Partners headquarters in London last year is ‘not set in stone’.

Sports.title: 'His brain works at 100 miles an hour': Inside Brighton owner Tony Bloom's top-secret Starlizard HQ - as sources reveal the cloak-and-dagger meetings, maths geniuses, intense working hours and 'paranoia' fuelling Seagulls' remarkable success
Sports.content:
'His brain works at 100 miles an hour': Inside Brighton owner Tony Bloom's top-secret Starlizard HQ - as sources reveal the cloak-and-dagger meetings, maths geniuses, intense working hours and 'paranoia' fuelling Seagulls' remarkable success

It’s a warm Friday lunchtime around London’s Camden Lock and office workers are mingling with tourists, enjoying the blue skies and the summer warmth.

Only the young professionals who emerge from a modern canal-side edifice called The Iceworks know that a business of cutting-edge Premier League significance lies within this place.

They step out from the redbrick building in the kind of casual attire which suggests an unstuffy working environment designed to keep minds clear and sharp. A motivational message placed at one of the airy atriums inside states: ‘Calm.’

The quality of the working environment in the building – a substantial gymnasium, sauna, cafe with barista coffee and, we’re told, a kitchen with a private chef providing fresh food including two types of fish and different menus every day: all of this free – is a measure of the company’s attempt to recruit and retain the brightest minds.

The only significant clue to the football connection is the lime green fabric lizard placed on a dark-green baize background in the airy dining area overlooking the canal.

The company is Starlizard – the brainchild and intellectual home of Tony Bloom, the Brighton and Hove Albion owner, whose cold-eyed calculation at the poker tables earned him a fortune and the nickname ‘the lizard’ long before he applied his mathematical genius to the club who have just thrashed champions Arsenal and eliminated Manchester United from the Carabao Cup in the space of four days.

Brighton's genius owner Tony Bloom has transformed the fortunes of the club since his cold-eyed calculation at the poker tables earned him a fortune and the nickname ‘the lizard’

The HQ of Bloom's company Starlizard at London's Camden Lock (Starlizard's office is in the redbrick building left-of-centre)

Brighton's 3-0 demolition of champions Arsenal on Saturday took them into the Premier League's top three

Starlizard is the engine of Brighton's enduring success and The Iceworks is, you might say, the building where the secret codes are kept; the place where algorithms which pull together and weigh up every conceivable piece of predictive data about players and results are used to find value in the places where competitors aren’t looking.

Recruits must sign non-disclosure agreements which have always cloaked the company in secrecy. But drawing on the testimonies of insiders, who have spoken to us on condition of anonymity, Daily Mail Sport has attempted to build a picture of the company fuelling Brighton’s extraordinary success.

Behind the Iceworks walls, it is a picture of tight security and circumspection with unrestricted access for very few and employees sitting in rooms which require security cards to access. Meeting areas carve off into those private rooms with framed Brighton shirts on the walls – ‘all quite lock and key,’ in the words of one source – rather than this nerve centre resembling a frantic trading floor.

And contrary to the notion that an army of statistics geeks are crunching numbers here, it’s a relatively small team, perhaps 40 or 50 people, tapping into the real gold nuggets of the entire operation – the algorithms – which we understand are being developed far from The Iceworks by University of Exeter mathematics graduates, hired by Bloom and based off-site.

The Exeter recruits are the computer wizards; football industry equivalents of what the investment banking world calls quantitative analysts, or ‘quants'.

Though Bloom is neither a director nor owner of the Starlizard business, it is very much his – and his intellectual involvement on the small details of how to assess a player, team or likely result remains intense. The very few within the inner sanctum who get a look at the recruitment models and data include Brighton technical directors who have worked closely on the model with Bloom.

It explains why Brighton's football department has been in such high demand in recent years. Executives like Paul Winstanley and Sam Jewell have been snapped up by Chelsea on the basis that if a club can't have access to Brighton’s technology, they might get insights by hiring the people who used it.

Dan Ashworth, former Brighton technical director, knew the codes and reached Manchester United but Sir Jim Ratcliffe decided he had no need of him.

Bloom has a tight circle of people he trusts. Among them is Paul Barber (centre), Brighton's impressive chief executive

Brighton's recruitment model is the stuff of legend - with Moises Caicedo, now of Chelsea, one of the finest examples

It is Bloom’s formidable intellect which our sources all describe. ‘He's pretty much got to a stage where he can model where Brighton ought to finish based on tens of thousands of simulations of his own,’ says one.

‘You have to be intellectually on your game to hold a conversation with him. He's not intimidating in that regard. He's very, very down-to-earth – but directly intelligent. You can't really waffle your way through a conversation with Tony. He wants clarity. He wants facts. He wants access to information quickly. His brain works at a hundred miles an hour and he's a mathematician at heart, so you can't really bluff your way through those sorts of conversations.’

This intellectual intensity means that working at a high level for Starlizard is not a job for those who can’t face it being very, very full-on – akin to a graduate job at a City bank or broker.

Some describe an expectation from Bloom that work must be your life. Those seeking a more normal work-life balance depart, leaving those who live and breathe Starlizard to be a part of arguably the greatest ‘Moneyball’ success in football.

Moises Caicedo, bought for £4million and sold to Chelsea for more than 20 times as much. Marc Cucurella, bought and sold for a £46m profit inside a year. Alexis Mac Allister, sold for £48m after also contributing hugely on the field.

Starlizard was set up 20 years ago to use data and prediction models for Bloom to identify market inefficiencies in betting prices across the globe, often for fairly offbeat sporting events where you could place significant capital on the outcome.

When that had reaped him millions, the company sold access to its database to high-roller syndicates and clients, allowing them to place their own bets. And then, after Bloom bought Brighton in 2009, Starlizard's data helped build successful football teams.

Bloom’s success as an investor in Royale Union Saint-Gilloise, transformed from a dormant lower-tier team into a dominant force in Belgian football, and Hearts, who came close to the Scottish title last season, have shown it’s been no fluke at Brighton, his home-town team. Starlizard's profits have also provided the capital for Bloom to invest in Brighton.

All those we have spoken to describe the unusual significance Bloom attaches to loyalty and perhaps that is not surprising, given the highly secretive nature of his business. Many of those he has around him have been with him for a long time.

Fabian Hurzeler (pictured celebrating the Seagulls' win over Arsenal) is the latest in a long line of successful managerial hires

There is no love lost between Bloom and his former employee Matthew Benham (left), now the owner of Brentford

Bloom has become inseparable from Adam Franks, his ‘No 1 disciple’ and right-hand man according to one source. Franks, a fellow mathematician he met when they were undergraduates at Manchester University, is now his key lieutenant who communicates and translates Bloom’s wishes to staff across his businesses. The two are very alike in personality.

Marc Sugarman and Steve Edery are other very long-standing lieutenants. So is Brighton chief executive Paul Barber, who will sometimes travel to games with Bloom and is the impressive public-facing leader of the club: the yin to Bloom's yang. Their relationship has been a vital asset for Brighton.

An in-depth report on Starlizard by the US financial news website Business Insider in 2016 found that the Camden company’s employees were offered a stake in Bloom’s syndicate once they had completed a probationary period.

This meant that the office staff, who watch and record match data on anything from weather, morale, form and training information to feed into the algorithms and make betting assessments, could make anything between £100 to upwards of £500,000 every six months, depending on their stake. But if the syndicate sustained losses, its members would have to compensate Starlizard by topping up the pot available to lay future bets.

Some we have spoken to ascribe Bloom’s ‘paranoia’ around access and discretion at Starlizard to the way his one-time close friend and employee Matthew Benham left his business, to set up a rival company and, of course, run his own highly successful Premier League team, in Brentford.

Benham, who studied at Oxford and secured a job as a city derivatives trader, worked for Bloom at Premier Bet, the online bookmaker he’d founded, and certainly met his then boss’s intellectual expectations. But Benham left Premier Bet in 2004, taking staff and what Bloom considered to be proprietary information with him, to set up Smartodds. With loyalty so important to Bloom, Benham’s actions stung. The split was very acrimonious.

This has fed into the now fierce rivalry between Brighton and Brentford, whose fans know their owners can't abide each other. Bloom has been known to sit in the away end at Brentford’s stadium and celebrate goals with Brighton’s fans. ‘He won't go in the directors' box when Matthew's there,’ says a source.

That obsession about trust would have been reinforced by the High Court documents lodged in January by a former member of Bloom’s Starlizard gambling syndicate, Ryan Dudfield, who claimed the billionaire owed him a share of nearly £190m in gambling profits.

Dudfield alleged the Brighton owner screened his identity, to prevent being shut out of betting sites, by funnelling bets through sportsmen and businessmen. The case is understood to be unresolved. Dudfield claimed Starlizard made about £600m a year in winnings. Bloom rejected Dudfield's claims.

Those who earn Bloom’s trust have benefitted after leaving his employment. In the past few years, he has helped a select few former colleagues by allowing them to access his football recruitment analytics data via a facility called Jamestown Analytics.

Bloom (front row, centre) has been known to sit in the away end at Brentford’s stadium and celebrate goals with Brighton’s fans. ‘He won't go in the directors' box when Matthew's there,’ says a source

Under Bloom, Brighton continuously defy those who say other clubs are catching up and the dream era is over

One of Jamestown's beneficiaries is Grimsby Town, whose chief executive, Polly Bancroft, was a much-respected head of women's football at Brighton before leaving, with Bloom’s blessing, for the same role at Manchester United. She was recruited to Grimsby's Blundell Park in 2024.

Swansea City, also beneficiaries of Jamestown, have former Brighton head of marketing and women's team director Tom Gorringe as their chief executive.

Grimsby have mounted a push for promotion to League One, beat Manchester United in last season’s Carabao Cup and reached the fourth round of the FA Cup. Swansea are currently top of the Championship.

But it is Brighton on which Bloom continues to focus his Starlizard ‘quants’ and number crunchers, and the club, sitting third in the Premier League, are defying a view, prevalent in football all summer, that others had caught up with their data prowess and their dream era was over.

Maxim De Cuyper and the re-signed Pascal Gross are among the league’s outstanding players and though the £50m outlay to Tottenham for Luka Vuskovic looked high by Brighton’s standards, he has so far looked like another they may sell for double that.

How the beleaguered Michael Carrick could use a little of the Exeter University algorithm expertise which Starlizard’s Camden Lock staff are putting into effect at their canal-side location. There’s no chance of that, of course.

‘Brighton's position is Tony’s priority and he won't provide any access to clubs that will directly compete with them,’ says a source.

Sports.title: India embroiled in cricket storm as they convince umpire to overturn wide call against Japan... and prevent one of the biggest shocks in the sport's history
Sports.content:
India embroiled in cricket storm as they convince umpire to overturn wide call against Japan... and prevent one of the biggest shocks in the sport's history

T20 world champions India have become embroiled in a storm after appearing to persuade the umpire to overturn his wide call - which helped avoid a humiliating defeat against minnows Japan.

The first-ever meeting between the nations was reduced by rain from a T20 to a five-over shootout, and the hosts restricted India to a score of 32 in Sano.

Washington Sundar conceded seven runs and bagged one wicket in the penultimate over of Japan's reply before Axar Patel took control for the final six balls. Needing only eight runs in the final over, hosts Japan were one hit away from producing the biggest upset in international cricket history.

And with the hosts needed six runs from the final four balls, batter Alexander Shirai-Patmore attempted to reverse-sweep Axar, who spun his delivery down the leg side.

Umpire Chris Thurgate called a wide but - baffled by the verdict - bowler Axar and wicketkeeper Sanju Samson voiced their displeasure towards the decision before Indian captain Shreyas Iyer stepped up and reached out to leg umpire Chris Brown.

After a brief discussion between the umpires, Thurgate overturned the verdict - seemingly being persuaded that Shirai-Patmore changing his stance meant the ball should not have been considered a wide.

Axar Patel's delivery was adjudged a wide after spinning past right-handed batter Alexander Shirai-Patmore, who was attempting a reverse sweep

Axar was surprised by the wide call by umpire Chris Thurgate...

... and captain Shreyas Iyer took up the issue with umpire Chris Brown before the call was overturned

The decision meant that Japan needed six runs from their final three deliveries, rather than a far more straightforward five runs from four.

Axar then conceded just three more runs to secure a thrilling two-run win over Japan as India replaced England at the top of the T20 rankings.

And although the correct decision appeared to have been made eventually, the Indian players were accused by fans online of ‘bullying the umpires’ as Japan were denied an extra run - and an extra delivery.

Players challenging the verdict of umpires are frowned upon in cricket - and the final decision also arrived in a T20I where the Decision Review System (DRS) was not available.

The final-over flourish sparked a huge debate as Iyer’s men were blamed for acting contrary to the ‘spirit of cricket’.

'It doesn't matter how good a team you are, because the opposition is also competitive, and the attitude and approach the Japanese team showed today was impeccable. Kudos to them,' India skipper Iyer said after the match.

Sports.title: 'You don't get away with it... you get found out': Paul Scholes delivers chastening verdict on 36-year-old Jordan Henderson after Chelsea's defeat at Brentford
Sports.content:
Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has said he was shocked by Jordan Henderson starting in the Premier League at 36, insisting 'he's a last-20-minutes man'.

Scholes, 51, took to his podcast, The Good The Bad and The Football, to reflect on his surprise at Xabi Alonso's decision to start the ex– Liverpool captain in Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brentford on Friday night.

The 11-time Premier League winner said: 'We've been there at 35, 36, 37, you're a million miles away from where you should be. You can use your experience to get through games, but these days it's more of a young man's game and you will get found out starting a game.'

Henderson joined Chelsea as a free agent in the summer and most assumed he would appear sporadically, providing the Chelsea dressing room with much-needed leadership and experience.

A guiding light off the field with England at the World Cup, Henderson was trusted to start for his new side at the G-tech and had a poor performance against his old club, provoking questions about whether he is still able to perform at the highest level.

The one time Champions League winner struggled to keep up with the pace of the game throughout and looked out of his depth in Alonso's 3-4-3 system, bickering with teammates at times. He was also at fault for Brentford's second, giving the ball away cheaply in midfield after a poor attempted through ball allowing the Bees to counter and put the game to bed.

Scholes was adamant that he is not good enough anymore, saying: 'I never expected him to play a Premier League game. Playing at that age in the Premier League you get found out.'

Jordan Henderson has plenty to offer in the dressing room but struggled on the field

Paul Scholes appearing on his podcast, co-hosted by Nicky Butt and Paddy McGuinness

Scholes said he could empathise with Henderson, saying he knew when he started slowing down and losing the edge to play in the Premier league.

The midfield legend, who won everything available to him at club level, said: 'I remember I did it against City, I might have been 36, the manager actually picked me and I thought I shouldn't be playing this game, I shouldn't be starting this game. I never touched the ball. I just knew it was too much for me.'

Henderson may be having similar thoughts after a poor Chelsea bow but he has always been credited for his work rate and professionalism and may yet have something left in the tank.

Yet Scholes added: 'I never expected him to be starting a Premier League game. I don't care how old you are, how much you look after yourself, playing in the Premier League at that age you've got to be a machine, you've got to be athletic. You don't get away with it, you get found out.'

Under new owners BlueCo, Chelsea have almost exclusively signed younger players on long-term deals. In an about turn this summer, they opted for experience.

Welbeck (far left, next to Scholes) celebrating Manchester United's 2012-13 Premier League title along with Ryan Giggs and Rio Ferdinand (right)

Welbeck has three Carabao Cup goals for Chelsea but he struggled in the Brentford defeat

Henderson, as well as 35-year-old Danny Welbeck, have added plenty of Premier League know-how to a young Chelsea squad and were clearly major targets for new boss Alonso in the summer.

Scholes, though, feels the Spaniard may have tipped the scales too far saying: 'When you're playing another, Danny (Welbeck) at centre forward - there's two in your team - you're thinking, bloody hell.'

Welbeck, who has three Carabao Cup goals this season, played alongside Scholes at Manchester United and won a Premier League title there but that didn't spare him from criticism from his old team-mate.

The veteran number nine was unable to get a foothold in the game registering only four touches in the opposition box and not having a single attempt on goal or a completed dribble. To make matters worse, Welbeck was partially at fault for the opener as his lackadaisical marking left Jaidon Anthony completely alone in the six-yard-box gifting Brentford the lead.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho given fresh escape route after nightmare Aston Villa start
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho given fresh escape route after nightmare Aston Villa start

Former Manchester United star Alejandro Garnacho only joined Aston Villa from Chelsea in the summer but the forward could potentially be on the move once again, with clubs already eyeing him

View 2 Images Garnacho joined Aston Villa from Chelsea in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Alejandro Garnacho is reportedly being monitored by Spanish clubs after a difficult start to life with Aston Villa. The former Manchester United man only joined the Midlands side on a season-long loan deal in the summer from Chelsea.

‌



But Garnacho, 22, has been limited to just 31 minutes of action so far this season, and has not even come off the bench in any of Villa’s last three games.

‌



His switch to Villa Park will become permanent for a fee of around £43million should certain conditions be met. But that already appears unlikely.

‌



According to Mail Online, clubs in La Liga are watching Garnacho’s situation. The forward was actually born in Madrid and had a spell with Atletico Madrid’s academy before his switch to Manchester United.

Asked recently what Garnacho needs to do to earn an opportunity with the club, Villa boss Unai Emery said: “Continue working. Work, work, train, work.

“When he can have minutes to play, try to play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now. George Hemmings is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. [Ibrahim] Mbaye also responded well.

“We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs.”

‌



View 2 Images Garnacho has played just 31 minutes for Aston Villa this season (Image: Getty Images)

Having been left out of the latest Argentina squad, he will now join Villa on a mid-season training camp in Spain, where he will certainly hope to catch Emery’s eye.

Garnacho’s career has taken a sharp downturn over recent seasons. After scoring 26 goals in 144 appearances for Manchester United, he left the club in a £40m move to Premier League rivals Chelsea last summer.

Article continues below

He netted eight goals in 43 appearances for Chelsea across his debut campaign but just one of those came in the Premier League. New boss Xabi Alonso made it clear that he had little future at Stamford Bridge ahead of his move to Villa. Garnacho has just under six years remaining on his current contract at Stamford Bridge.

Villa have a just under three-week wait for their next Premier League game which is set to come against Brentford on October 10. They will then take on Fenerbahce in their first Champions League home game of the campaign.

Sports.title: Andrew Robertson ‘feels sorry’ for Trent Alexander-Arnold amid Real Madrid issues
Sports.content:
Andrew Robertson ‘feels sorry’ for Trent Alexander-Arnold amid Real Madrid issues

Former Liverpool star Trent Alexander-Arnold has endured a tricky time since joining Real Madrid last summer and his former teammate Andrew Robertson has now spoken out

View 2 Images Andrew Robertson has leapt to Trent Alexander-Arnold's defence (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Liverpool star Andrew Robertson has admitted he feels sorry for former teammate Trent Alexander-Arnold due to the increased level of criticism he receives. The pair struck up a brilliant partnership during their respective spells at Anfield.

‌



They were key to Liverpool claiming two Premier League titles under Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot, while they also played a role in the club’s Champions League success. Despite their glittering spell at Anfield, Alexander-Arnold faced severe criticism for defensive errors, while he has never quite managed to establish himself in the England side.

‌



And Robertson says he sympathised with his former teammate. Speaking on The Overlap, the Scottish defender said: "It's very different when you are English, compared to another nationality.

‌



“I always said to Trent, 'I will never get as much high praise as you, but I'll never get as much criticism as you.'"

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He added: "The way I defended at Liverpool compared to Trent was very different. I had Sadio helping me out and he was a bit more aggressive so if I missed [a tackle], he'd usually be there.

“With Mo [Salah], we didn't want him coming back towards our box. A lot of times, Trent was waiting on someone like [Jordan Henderson] to come over, so, sometimes, I started to feel sorry for him."

Alexander-Arnold has since departed Liverpool, having joined Spanish giants Real Madrid on a free transfer last summer. He has endured an inconsistent spell in La Liga so far, having started just 14 league games during his debut campaign.

‌



View 2 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold has not hit the heights expected of him at Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

That has continued this season, with new manager Jose Mourinho preferring Denzel Dumfries at right-back. But Robertson remains sure that Alexander-Arnold has the talent to be a success at the Bernabeu.

"I've seen him lock out [Kylian] Mbappe at PSG. In the Champions League finals, he was unbelievable," he said. "Trent is a very, very good defender… [in his] best games, he was an unbelievable one-v-one defender.

Article continues below

"Now, at times, he maybe makes mistakes. But we all do. But it's if [Trent] had this stigma around him, that he can't defend. And he's had that from a very early age. It's as if he can't shift it."

Like Alexander-Arnold, Robertson left Liverpool this summer as he joined Premier League rivals Tottenham. The 32-year-old has started all but one of his new club’s league games this season, with Roberto De Zerbi’s men currently without a win and bottom of the table.

Sports.title: Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham reignites World Cup feud - 'You don't talk without Messi'
Sports.content:
Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham reignites World Cup feud - 'You don't talk without Messi'

Jude Bellingham and Cristian Romero came to blows during Sunday's Madrid derby, having also clashed during the World Cup semi-final between England and Argentina

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham and Cristian Romero locked horns at the weekend

Jude Bellingham and Cristian Romero clashed during the Madrid derby at the weekend as the opposing players reignited their World Cup feud.

‌



Atletico Madrid got the better of Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid in an ill-tempered affair, which saw Bellingham and the former Tottenham defender clash and the match end 2-1.

‌



The duo were seen exchanging words through the match at the Metropolitano, with their World Cup semi-final clash clearly still fresh in the memory. England took the lead that night before the South Americans rallied late on, scoring their winner in stoppage time.

‌



According to Movistar’s El Día Después, Bellingham poked fun at Romero, claiming he was less vocal when he didn't have Lionel Messi in his team.

He allegedly said: "When you’re with [Lionel] Messi, you talk a lot. But here, nothing." Bellingham also called the Argentine a "coward."

Romero responded by calling Bellingham a "cry baby" and mocked the Englishman for cutting an emotional figure as he said: "you cried over there [at the World Cup]".

Earlier in the game, Bellingham was on the receiving end of a nasty challenge from Romero, which saw the former Spurs star shown a yellow card despite a VAR review. Real also felt Kang-in Lee should've been shown a red card for his ankle-high challenge on Federico Valverde. They later had Dean Huijsen sent off, which only added to their frustration.

‌



Bellingham was furious at full-time, leading the protests against referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias by repeatedly shouting ‘"two red cards, two!" at the official.

View 2 Images The Englishman and the Argentina star were quick to recall their World Cup encounter

Mourinho was critical of the officials after the contest, with defeat leaving Los Blancos in fourth and six points off the pace set by Barcelona. He arrived his post-match news conference carrying an A4 sheet of printed paper with screenshots displaying two incidents he believed should have resulted in Atletico dismissals.

Article continues below

"We can skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," the Special One said as he showed media the printed images. "Those were two clear red cards. Given the difficulties we faced afterwards playing 11 against 10, we can only imagine what 50 minutes of 11 against nine would have been like."

Sports.title: Value Scope Extra: Saffie Osborne could have more reasons to be tearful at Ascot
Sports.content:
There will have been plenty of tears in the Osborne household over the last week and a half.

Up-and-coming jockey Saffie sparked the waterworks when becoming the first female rider to win a British Classic when landing the St Leger on Highwayman for Joseph O’Brien.

Proud parents Jamie and Katie were, understandably, more than a little moist around the eye area but there’s a chance they might flood the Ascot winners’ enclosure on Qatar Racing British Champions Day. Trainer Jamie has entered smart recruit WHITE BIRCH in the feature race at the glittering end-of-season celebrations in just over three weeks.

Jockeys to wear black armbands on Tuesday after death of popular ex-rider READ MORE :

He had some top-class form when trained in Ireland with his 2024 defeat of Derby hero Auguste Rodin in the Group 1 Tattersalls Gold Cup the clear highlight.

‌



It’s only 16 months since he was a little unlucky not to retain that crown and he has only had one start this season after switching to Osborne. He will have to improve considerably on that third in a Windsor Listed race, no doubt, when having his first run since being gelded and undergoing a breathing operation.

That effort is sure to have blown away the dust and, if the weather finally turns, the 66-1 currently on offer could be a steal.

He’s likely to come up against top-class pair Calandagan and Ombudsman – first and second in last year’s Champion Stakes – but there’s definite potential for the race to cut up with most of the other leading contenders having other targets. Soft ground would only increase those chances.

View 3 Images Zavateri: Ascot bound (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

‌



ZAVATERI would also enjoy a wet start to October ahead of Champions Day. He is a 7-1 shot for the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes and he looked very good when running away with the Celebration Mile on soft ground at Goodwood last month.

Missing three months earlier in the season means he’ll be fresher than most and, although he is hardly a fancy price, his odds have the potential to tumble in the next few weeks.

View 3 Images Harry Charlton (Image: Getty Images)

Keep a close eye on Harry Charlton’s runners in nurseries

Another Encore’s Leicester victory on Monday took the Wiltshire trainer’ record in two-year-olds’ handicaps to four wins from five runners this year.

‌



GIVE HAND could be the next. He has entries at Haydock on Saturday and Epsom the following day. SECANO and ASTRALITE, who could have his final qualifying run at Newmarket on Friday, are others to keep tabs on.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer accused of FAKING injury and pulling out of England camp with 'the hump'
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer accused of FAKING injury and pulling out of England camp with 'the hump'

After Cole Palmer pulled out of the England squad for the upcoming international break, a huge accusation has been levelled at the Chelsea star

View 3 Images Cole Palmer is suffering from a "small muscular injury" (Image: 2026 Gaspafotos/MB Media)

Ex-West Ham United defender James Collins has accused Chelsea midfielder Cole Palmer of fabricating an injury to pull out of the England squad. Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel called him up for England's Nations League clashes against Spain, Czechia and Croatia.

‌



Palmer, 24, was snubbed by Tuchel for the Three Lions' World Cup squad, which proved to be one on the German's most controversial selection decisions. Under Xabi Alonso, Palmer started impressively by contributing four goals and two assists in seven appearances for the west Londoners.

‌



It was claimed Palmer had a "small muscular injury" which was picked up after he was named in Tuchel's squad. However, Collins, based solely of his own experience in the game (which was not with Palmer), has suggested the injury may not be genuine.

‌



Speaking on Boyle Sports and Footy Accumulators’ podcast, 'No Tippy Tappy Football', Collins said: "I would say that Cole Palmer had got the hump. He’s got the hump that he didn’t go to the World Cup, and he’s pulled out of the England squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"That’s my opinion. I don’t know the lad, but from an ex-player point of view, I think he’s got the hump. It sounds to me as an ex-player that he’s gone to the fitness coach at Chelsea and said, 'Really, I don’t fancy it, just say something’. It might not be that, but I’ve played the game, and that’s what it looks like to me.”

Chelsea have been approached for a comment. But according to football.london, the Blues want to carefully manage his muscle injury, particularly after his campaign last season was disrupted with injuries.

View 3 Images Collins made the comment on a recent podcast (Image: 2023 Jacques Feeney/Offside)

‌



It will nonetheless be frustrating for Tuchel, who praised the ex-Manchester City ace for his return to form this season. When asked why he chose to recall Palmer and Real Madrid ace Trent Alexander-Arnold, the ex-Chelsea boss said: "They had a good start to the season. They never did something wrong. We just chose different players.

"So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back - he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back - so that is why he is in the squad."

View 3 Images Tuchel was keen to see Palmer play after not selecting him for the World Cup (Image: AFP or licensors)

Article continues below

Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Declan Rice have also pulled out of the squad. Tuchel has since responded by bringing in Morgan Gibbs-White of Nottingham Forest and Everton ace James Garner.

There has, however, not been a recall for Phil Foden, which may surprise many given the Manchester City ace could deputise for Palmer, Rashford and Mainoo. Tuchel has also chosen not to call-up Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton, despite losing many midfielders to injury.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua questions Tyson Fury drug testing for mega-fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua questions Tyson Fury drug testing for mega-fight

Joshua and Fury will clash in Cardiff on December 11 with an official announcement now imminent and a press conference expected to take place in London early next week

View Image Anthony Joshua speaks out (Image: Mark Robinson, Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua has appeared to question why Tyson Fury has not enrolled in drug-testing for their mega-fight.

‌



Joshua and Fury will clash in Cardiff on December 11 with an official announcement now imminent and a press conference expected to take place in London early next week. But questions have been raised over Fury's drug-testing protocol with Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn insisting testing should be underway by now.

‌



Joshua has now posted a copy of an email to his Snapchat account, showing correspondence between the VADA drug-testing agency and an unknown recipient. The email reads: "Is Mr. Fury going to enroll? Typically, we enroll opponents at the same time. We also need the whereabouts form to enroll either fighter." Joshua posted the email along with a caption which read: "I'm not accusing TF of anything".

‌



In response, a statement from Fury's team read: "Once the fight has been officially finalised, VADA will be the first people we will be calling."

Tyson Fury breaks silence with TWO Anthony Joshua rants READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua could have secret weapon for Tyson Fury fight READ MORE :

Speaking on Saturday night, Hearn claimed Fury should have started testing when he signed to contract to fight Joshua. “The drug testing protocol is the same as what has always been in the contract," he said. “It wasn’t adhered to in its form.

‌



"I don’t actually, necessarily blame Tyson Fury for that because I don’t think – as we have found out on many occasions – I don’t think what is in AJ’s contract is the same as what is in AJ’s contract. Testing was supposed to start when the original contracts were signed. And it didn’t for them.

"I don’t think it had it in his contract that it had to start then, so this is not me saying he didn’t enrol, I don’t think he was obligated to enrol. But in our contract he was obligated to enrol."

Joshua and Fury signed separate contracts and Hearn explained why this has caused issues. “There have been many issues along the way, with the contracts, that we have let slip, because we want to stay in the fight and we want to make sure the fight happens," he added.

Article continues below

"The ones we weren’t willing to let slip were the location and TKO’s involvement. The protocol was supposed to start earlier but it is now in line with most other fights. I don’t necessarily blame Tyson Fury for that, I just think what we asked for was not in his personal contract, so he did not have to do it."

Fury served a backdated two-year ban from UK Anti-Doping after tests in 2015 showed elevated levels of nandrolone. Fury blamed the positive test on eating uncastrated wild boar.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel 'reaches first major agreement' as Man Utd star tells four clubs his preference
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel 'reaches first major agreement' as Man Utd star tells four clubs his preference

Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel expressed a desire to leave Old Trafford last week and has since been linked with some of the biggest clubs in the world

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel reportedly wants to move to Spain if he is granted an exit from the Red Devils. It emerged earlier this month that Gabriel had expressed a desire to leave United, and there are already reports of where the playmaker could end up joining.

‌



Reports last week claimed that Gabriel had refused to take part in training for United ahead of their Carabao Cup third-round tie against Brighton. The 15-year-old was expected to be involved in the matchday squad for Michael Carrick’s side before expressing a desire to leave United.

‌



Gabriel has been tipped to have a bright future in the game, and would have been United’s youngest-ever player had he made his debut against the Seagulls at Old Trafford last week. Yet Gabriel's determination to leave United has sparked intense speculation surrounding the youngster's next move.

‌



A new update has surfaced from Spain suggesting that Gabriel could be heading across Europe should he leave United. Spanish publication Sport have reported that Gabriel's shortlist of potential destinations now features four clubs, two of which are based in Spain. Real Madrid and Barcelona are among those reportedly keen on securing Gabriel's signature, alongside Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The report further claims that Gabriel and his camp have already visited Spain, touring both Madrid and Barcelona. The United starlet has reportedly reached a 'first major agreement' to join one of those clubs instead of any other team. Reports suggest Gabriel is now keen on a move to Spain, giving Barcelona and Real Madrid the upper hand in the race to sign the coveted United youngster.

Gabriel has enjoyed an impressive opening few weeks of the season, most recently scoring a hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League earlier this month. The playmaker has also contributed two goals and two assists across just two appearances for United's Under-21s in Premier League 2.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Despite his request to depart, Gabriel remains registered with United for the remainder of the season and cannot be de-registered. United believe the matter can still be resolved, despite Gabriel's unexpected desire to leave the club. The teenager is just a couple of weeks away from being eligible to sign a scholarship with United when he turns 16 on October 6, and will need to wait until his 17th birthday before putting pen to paper on a professional contract.

Speaking on Friday, Carrick was keen to shift the focus away from speculation surrounding the teenager and towards his wellbeing. He said: "I’ll just repeat what I said [earlier this week]: he’s a young boy, it’s important we don’t put anything out here, the exposure and scrutiny we have to be careful.

"We have to be sensible and think about him. The situation will work itself out."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta 'receives bumper pay rise' as Arsenal boss reaches new contract agreement
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta 'receives bumper pay rise' as Arsenal boss reaches new contract agreement

After a hugely successful year last season, Mikel Arteta has decided to extend his stay at the Emirates Stadium by agreeing to sign a new Arsenal deal

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is set to remain at Arsenal for the long-term (Image: Getty)

Mikel Arteta has reportedly reached an agreement with Arsenal to sign a bumper new contract at the Emirates Stadium. His current deal in north London expires at the end of the current season.

‌



However, fresh terms between the Gunners manager and the club have been agreed, and he is set to sign a new deal, according to the BBC. Moreover, his new terms are set to include a sizeable pay rise from his current £10million-per-year deal, which includes an additional £5m in bonuses.

‌



It's unclear as to how long the contract will be, but it's believed it will take Arteta, who was appointed as manager in 2019, into his tenth year of service.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Last week, Arteta was asked about contract talks with the club. He replied: "They [the fans] don't have to worry about any of that because I want to be here. I'm extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with."

Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke also made it clear at the start of June that the club would do everything they could to ensure Arteta remained in north London.

‌



Shortly after the Gunners won the Premier League, the American said: "Keeping Mikel around is [an] utmost priority. I think the good news for Arsenal fans worldwide is he's enjoying the project.

View 3 Images Kroenke stated keeping Arteta was of vital importance to the north Londoners (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"He's enjoying being here and from his time as a player all the way up until now, he's an Arsenal man through and through."

‌



He also added: "If there is a singular person you can trace this all back to, I'm going to give 100% credit to Mikel, his staff and the players.

"Those are the ones. As much as Mikel is putting together our tactics, the players have got to go play the games, they've got to go and win for you."

View 3 Images Arsenal suffered their first defeat of the season (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Last year, Arsenal ended their barren 22-year run without a league title and were a penalty shootout away from winning the Champions League. They also got to the final of the League Cup, only to lose 2-0 to Manchester City at Wembley Stadium.

The north Londoners have started the new campaign well, winning all but one of their matches in all competitions. Their winning start was ended last weekend by Brighton and Hove Albion, who secured a shock 3-0 victory on the South Coast.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
