Renan Calheiros took on Braskem and his political rivals on Tuesday, calling a 2023 compensation deal over Maceió’s sinking neighbourhoods “criminal”. The veteran senator, who is seeking re-election on 4 October, spoke on TV Gazeta, a television station in Alagoas state.

The deal he attacked is three years old. Maceió’s city hall signed it in July 2023 with Braskem, Brazil’s largest petrochemical company.

Braskem paid the city 1.7 billion reais (about US$330 million) in compensation for damage from its rock-salt mining. In return, the city granted a full release from further claims and handed over public land in the evacuated zone.

Conversions in this article use the Central Bank of Brazil’s reference rate of 5.12 to the US dollar on 22 September 2026.

What Calheiros said on air

Calheiros was interviewed live on Bom Dia Alagoas, TV Gazeta’s morning programme, on 22 September 2026. The broadcast began at 7:30 a.m. BRT, which is Brasília time, and also ran on the group’s radio stations and website.

According to GazetaWeb, the group’s news site, he called the city’s agreement “criminal”. He objected to the transfer of land to the company.

He also said the city must explain how the money was spent. The Renan Calheiros Braskem dispute is now part of the Alagoas campaign.

He placed the political blame on the mayor who signed it, João Henrique Caldas, widely known as JHC. Calheiros also claimed that nearly 60,000 people from the affected area had not been approached or compensated, GazetaWeb reported.

Braskem gives a different picture of its own programme. The company says more than 99.6% of the compensation it planned has been paid, covering about 14,500 properties.

Calheiros promised to keep pursuing Braskem from the Senate. He chairs the Senate’s economic affairs committee, which on 1 September approved his request to hear from the heads of Braskem’s owners.

A family feud on the ballot

The charge lands less than two weeks before an election in which the Calheiros and Caldas families are direct rivals. JHC resigned as mayor on 4 April 2026 to run for governor of Alagoas against Renan Filho, the senator’s son.

JHC’s wife, Marina Candia, is running for the Senate for the PSDB, a centre-right party. A Paraná Pesquisas poll released on 21 September put her second with 37.8% and Calheiros third with 34.6%, a statistical tie.

Arthur Lira of the centre-right PP, a former speaker of the lower house, led with 41.2%. Alagoas elects two senators this year, so each voter could name two candidates.

The poll, commissioned by TV Pajuçara, surveyed 1,400 voters from 18 to 20 September, with a margin of error of 2.7 points. No response from JHC or Braskem to Tuesday’s remarks had been reported by Tuesday afternoon.

Aerial view of part of Maceió beside a lagoon, with cleared ground among houses; the media record identifies it as the mine area. File photograph. (Photo: Rio Times media library)

The company supplies electricity and other inputs to second-generation producers; sells utilities, such as steam, water, compressed air and industrial gases; industrial services; and engages in the production, supply, and sale…

What the 2023 agreement says

Braskem says the 1.7 billion reais (about US$330 million) fully compensated the city for the subsidence and the evacuation. Managing the money is the city’s responsibility, the company adds.

The release it gave Braskem was “general, full, irrevocable and irretractable”, the Brasília news site Congresso em Foco reported. The text allows renegotiation if the map of the affected area grows significantly.

The land clause is what Calheiros singled out.

The city agreed to transfer ownership of public property in the zone, GazetaWeb reported in 2024. That includes streets, squares, gardens, parks and pavements.

Senator Rogério Carvalho was the rapporteur of a 2024 Senate inquiry into Braskem. In April 2024 he argued that nothing stopped the company from one day building there.

Calheiros had pushed for that inquiry but left it in February 2024.

The Alagoas state government, then led by Governor Paulo Dantas of Calheiros’s MDB party, fought the settlements in court. In late 2023 a federal court in Maceió rejected its request to review the city’s deal.

The state also asked the Supreme Court to strike down clauses of Braskem’s settlements with prosecutors. Justice Cármen Lúcia rejected that case on procedural grounds in June 2024.

Braskem made its final payment to the city in December 2024, the regional news site Política Alagoana reported. It noted that how the money would be spent remained unclear.

Separately, in November 2025, Braskem agreed to pay the state of Alagoas 1.2 billion reais (about US$235 million), mostly over ten years. The deal also ended the state’s lawsuit against the company, Gazeta do Povo reported.

Why Maceió’s neighbourhoods sank

For about four decades, Braskem and its predecessors extracted rock salt from 35 wells beneath Maceió, the state capital. The salt feeds chemical plants making chlorine and PVC plastic.

In March 2018, after an earth tremor, cracks spread through streets and buildings in the Pinheiro district. A 2019 report by the Brazilian Geological Service linked the ground movement to the salt extraction.

Five neighbourhoods were eventually emptied: Pinheiro, Mutange, Bebedouro, Bom Parto and Farol. About 60,000 people left their homes, turning whole districts into ghost towns.

On 29 November 2023 the city declared an emergency over a mine cavity under Mutange. Part of it collapsed on 10 December 2023.

What comes next for Braskem and Maceió

Braskem has asked for an out-of-court restructuring of about 56 billion reais (about US$10.9 billion) of debt. Its owners are the state-controlled oil company Petrobras and the investment firm IG4 Capital.

In his committee request, Calheiros argued that this reorganisation must not undervalue, hide or delay Braskem’s obligations to Maceió. Agência Senado, the Senate’s news service, said a date would be set later.

For now, the fight over the sunken districts is also a fight over votes. Alagoas goes to the polls on Sunday 4 October 2026.

More: Brazil coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Renan Calheiros say about Braskem?

In a live TV Gazeta interview on 22 September 2026, he called the 2023 agreement between Maceió’s city hall and Braskem “criminal”, according to GazetaWeb. He objected to the transfer of public land to the company and said the use of the money must be explained. He promised to keep pressing Braskem in the Senate.

Is the Maceió deal new?

No. The city signed it in July 2023, and a federal court in Maceió rejected a state request to review it later that year. Braskem paid the city 1.7 billion reais (about US$330 million), completing payment in December 2024 according to Política Alagoana.

Why did parts of Maceió sink?

Braskem and its predecessors mined rock salt beneath the city for about four decades. After cracks appeared in 2018, the Brazilian Geological Service linked the subsidence to the mining in 2019. About 60,000 people left five neighbourhoods.

Why is this political?

JHC, the mayor who signed the deal, is running for governor of Alagoas against Renan Filho, the senator’s son. JHC’s wife, Marina Candia, is competing with Calheiros for one of the state’s two Senate seats on 4 October 2026.

World.title: As Belize celebrates 45th Independence, Guatemala receives US military weapons amid renewed Sarstoon tensions
World.content:
As Belize celebrates 45th Independence, Guatemala receives US military weapons amid renewed Sarstoon tensions

By Breaking Belize News Staff: As Belizeans celebrated the country’s 45th anniversary of Independence on Monday, September 21, neighbouring Guatemala was receiving a major shipment of United States military weapons and equipment — at a particularly sensitive moment in relations between the two countries.

The shipment arrived in Guatemala aboard a U.S. military aircraft and forms part of a more than US$5 million military acquisition through the United States’ Foreign Military Sales programme. Guatemala’s government says the equipment is intended to modernize its armed forces and strengthen operations against drug trafficking and transnational organized crime.

According to Guatemala’s official government news agency, the acquisition includes 2,699 M4A1 rifles, 59 M240 machine guns, 57 grenade launchers and 11,220 30-round magazines, at a total cost of approximately US$5.03 million. Guatemala has described the purchase as its first acquisition of U.S. military weapons following nearly five decades of restrictions on military sales.

German news agency dpa reported that the package also includes equipment for special nighttime operations. The restrictions on U.S. arms transfers dated back to the late 1970s amid concerns over serious human rights abuses during Guatemala’s internal armed conflict.

And the shipments are not expected to stop there.

The U.S. Army Security Assistance Command said in July that additional Foreign Military Sales cases for Guatemala over the coming years will include other weapons systems and various aircraft as Guatemala continues modernizing its military. Guatemalan government reporting has also indicated that future acquisitions are expected to include aircraft, vessels and other military equipment.

The United States and Guatemala have been strengthening their defence relationship, with U.S. Southern Command saying in June that cooperation is being expanded as part of joint efforts against cartels and transnational criminal organizations.

For Belize, however, the timing is noteworthy.

The weapons arrived on September 21 — Belize’s Independence Day — less than two weeks after one of the most serious recent confrontations in the Sarstoon, an area at the centre of persistent tensions between Belize and Guatemala while Guatemala’s territorial, insular and maritime claim remains before the International Court of Justice.

On September 10, the Belize Territorial Volunteers (BTV) travelled to the Sarstoon for their traditional September expedition, during which they have historically sought to circle Sarstoon Island and plant the Belizean flag.

This year, they were unable to do so.

Belizean reports said approximately 14 to 18 Guatemalan military and civilian vessels were in the area. The BTV, accompanied by the Belize Defence Force and Belize Coast Guard, went no farther than Belize’s Forward Operating Base after authorities determined that proceeding toward the island posed an unacceptable risk.

Belize’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs subsequently lodged what it described as its strongest protest, maintaining that Guatemalan vessels had entered Belizean waters and obstructed the lawful passage of Belizean nationals. Belize maintains that the international boundary follows the mid-channel of the Sarstoon River and that Sarstoon Island itself belongs to Belize.

Then, on September 15 — Guatemala’s Independence Day — Guatemalan Marine Infantry personnel carried out patriotic activities with families in the Sarstoon River and displayed the Guatemalan flag in the area. Guatemalan reporting described the activity as taking the national flag to what it called a corner of “Guatemalan territory” — terminology sharply at odds with Belize’s longstanding position on the area.

The developments come as the decades-old territorial dispute enters one of its most important stages.

Guatemala’s Foreign Ministry announced last week that oral hearings in the Guatemala’s Territorial, Insular and Maritime Claim against Belize have been scheduled at the International Court of Justice for February 22 to 26, 2027. The dispute was formally submitted to the Court in 2019 following referenda in both countries.

Under the Special Agreement taking the dispute to the ICJ, Belize and Guatemala agreed to accept the Court’s eventual decision as final and binding.

There is no indication that the U.S. weapons shipment to Guatemala is connected to the territorial dispute with Belize or the recent Sarstoon incidents. Both Washington and Guatemala have publicly described the military modernization programme as aimed primarily at combating narcotics trafficking, organized crime and other transnational security threats.

Nevertheless, the arrival of thousands of U.S.-supplied military weapons in Guatemala on the very day Belize marked 45 years as an independent nation comes against a backdrop of renewed sensitivity over sovereignty, the Sarstoon and a territorial case that will finally move into oral hearings at The Hague in just five months.

World.title: Woman detained after police find crack pipe hidden in bra
World.content:
Woman detained after police find crack pipe hidden in bra

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 39 year old woman was detained after police allegedly found a suspected crack pipe concealed inside her bra during an early morning patrol in Bella Vista Village.

According to police, officers were conducting mobile patrol on an unnamed street in the village at around 2:30 a.m. on Sunday, September 20, when their attention was drawn to a woman riding a bicycle.

Police say the woman allegedly began acting suspiciously after noticing the officers.

An officer approached the woman, identified herself as a police officer and informed her that a search would be conducted for drugs.

During the search, police allegedly discovered a silver coloured pipe inside the woman’s bra.

The item was suspected of being used for smoking crack cocaine.

The woman was informed of the alleged offence, cautioned and taken into custody.

Police identified her as Ivis Marleny Reyes, 39, a labourer of Bella Vista Village.

She was escorted to the Bella Vista Police Sub Station, where police say she was informed of her rights in a language she understood.

Police reported that charges for possession of a pipe were pending.

World.title: Woman suffers neck and back injuries after attack at home
World.content:
Woman suffers neck and back injuries after attack at home

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Police in Independence Village are investigating a domestic violence complaint after a 35 year old woman reported that she was choked twice and pushed against a dresser during an argument inside her home.

According to police, the woman reported that she was at home at around 8:30 p.m. on Saturday, September 19, when she became involved in a verbal altercation with a man known to her.

The dispute reportedly began inside a bedroom.

Police say the woman alleged that the man became angry, approached her and grabbed her by the neck with his hand before pushing her toward a dresser.

She reportedly struck her back against the furniture and experienced pain to her neck and back.

The woman alleged that the man released her, walked away briefly and then returned and choked her a second time before again pushing her against the dresser.

She told police that she feared for her life during the incident.

After the man left the bedroom, the woman reportedly locked the door and called police for assistance.

A medico legal form was issued and a doctor subsequently classified her injuries as harm.

Police identified a 44 year old man as the person of interest. The matter remains under investigation.

World.title: Santa Cruz man charged with three traffic offences after motorcycle stop
World.content:
Santa Cruz man charged with three traffic offences after motorcycle stop

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 54 year old Santa Cruz Village man has been charged with three traffic offences after police reportedly found that the motorcycle he was riding was unlicensed, uninsured and that he did not hold the required licence class to operate it.

According to police information, officers were conducting mobile patrol in Santa Cruz Village at around 5:55 p.m. on Saturday, September 19, when they noticed a red Lifan motorcycle travelling in the opposite direction.

Police say a female passenger on the motorcycle was not wearing a helmet.

The motorcycle was stopped and officers requested the vehicle documents.

Police say the insurance disc had expired in January 2025, while the motorcycle licence had expired in December 2024.

Officers also reportedly determined that the rider’s Belize driver’s licence did not include the class required to operate a motorcycle.

The rider was identified as Edward Walter King, 54, a driver of Santa Cruz Village.

He was taken to the Santa Cruz Police Station and the motorcycle was impounded.

King was later formally arrested and charged with using an unlicensed motor vehicle, using a motor vehicle not covered by third party risk insurance, and driving without a valid Belize driver’s licence in respect to class.

Police say he was granted bail in the sum of $500 and was ordered to appear before the Independence Magistrate Court on September 22.

World.title: Woman says ex entered her home uninvited after confrontation at church parade
World.content:
Woman says ex entered her home uninvited after confrontation at church parade

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Police in Independence Village are investigating a complaint involving alleged common assault, indecent words and burglary after a woman reported that her ex common law partner confronted her at a church parade and later entered her home without permission.

According to police information, the 27 year old woman was at Triangular Park in Independence Village at around 9:30 p.m. on Sunday, September 20, when she decided to leave with her nine year old son.

As she entered her vehicle, she reportedly saw her ex common law partner open the driver’s side door and ask to take their son.

The woman told police that she detected a strong smell of alcohol on his breath and refused.

She alleged that the man became upset, threatened to get revenge, used insulting language and pointed in her face, causing her to feel afraid.

The woman then drove home.

Police say that after a telephone conversation between the two, the man later arrived at her residence and allegedly walked inside through an open door without being invited.

He reportedly began shouting at the child and questioning why the boy did not want to go with him.

Police identified the detained man as Richard Florencio Quinteros, 29, a labourer of Bella Vista Village.

Police say charges for burglary, indecent words and common assault are pending.

The matter remains under investigation.

World.title: ‘Two years after ComPol said it was sexual assault’: Another young boy filmed in highly sexualized dancing with three women at Orange Walk Carnival
World.content:
‘Two years after ComPol said it was sexual assault’: Another young boy filmed in highly sexualized dancing with three women at Orange Walk Carnival

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Two years after police and Carnival officials condemned a viral video of an adult woman dancing sexually with a young boy during Carnival, disturbing new footage from Monday’s Orange Walk Carnival shows the same troubling issue has not disappeared but instead appears to have gotten worse.

The video, recorded during the September 21 Carnival Road March in Orange Walk, shows a young boy engaging in highly sexualized dancing with three different adult female revelers at separate points in the short clip. The women are seen bending and dancing provocatively in front of the child as he dances closely behind them, mimicking the grinding and “wining” normally associated with adult Carnival revelry.

The woman who posted the footage identifies the child as her son, writing, “One thing bout my son, Fun da fun.” BBN has blurred the child’s face in the footage being published.

The scenes bear a striking resemblance to an incident at the 2024 Belize City Carnival which prompted former Commissioner of Police Chester Williams to publicly intervene. At the time, Williams described sexually suggestive dancing between an adult woman and a young boy as “tantamount to an assault of a sexual nature upon that child.”

Williams stressed then that the fact that the child appeared to be laughing did not make the conduct acceptable, saying: “The child is laughing, but he does not know what was being done to him.” Police subsequently announced an investigation.

Belize Carnival Association President Patrick Thompson was equally forceful at the time, telling BBN: “That is something the Association will not tolerate. That is something that we definitely will condemn.” Thompson said junior Carnival bands were deliberately required to keep children fully clothed “because we don’t want anyone to prey on our children.”

Yet, two years later, highly sexualized interaction between adults and children has again surfaced publicly at a Belizean Carnival. BBN has not located any subsequent public report explaining what ultimately became of the 2024 investigation, and it remains unclear whether police, social services or Carnival authorities will take any action in relation to Monday’s Orange Walk footage.

The video also comes just weeks after the Belize Council of Churches called for greater modesty and clearer standards at Carnival, particularly where children are concerned. The Council urged organizers to establish clearer costume guidelines and called on parents and guardians to exercise discretion over their children’s participation and exposure to increasingly adult aspects of Carnival.

The Church statement followed a recent BBN commentary, “Was Granny a ‘Hot Gial’? Today’s Carnival is nothing like the original road march,” which examined how Belize Carnival evolved from a largely child-centred community celebration involving handmade costumes and choreographed dancing into an event increasingly associated with revealing costumes, alcohol and overtly sexualized dancing.

That concern is not new. Original Carnival organizer Soli Arguelles, speaking about the direction Carnival had taken and particularly its impact on children, told News Five years ago: “This is not what we wanted.”

The latest footage now raises the question once again: if authorities, Carnival organizers and child-protection advocates agreed two years ago that adults engaging children in sexualized Carnival dancing crossed a line, why is the same behaviour still happening—and what, if anything, will be done about it?

World.title: Showers and thunderstorms expected across Belize today
World.content:
Showers and thunderstorms expected across Belize today

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belizeans can expect another hot and unsettled day, with showers and isolated thunderstorms forecast across parts of the country.

The National Meteorological Service says moist and relatively unstable conditions continue to prevail over Belize.

Today will be sunny with cloudy spells. A few showers and isolated thunderstorms will linger mostly offshore and along coastal areas this morning before spreading around the country and over inland areas this afternoon.

Tonight, rainfall activity is expected to become concentrated mainly offshore and along coastal areas.

Temperatures will remain warm, with inland areas reaching a high of 94 degrees Fahrenheit. Coastal areas can expect highs near 89 degrees, while temperatures in the hills will reach around 80 degrees.

Winds over the sea will blow from the east to southeast at 5 to 15 knots. Sea conditions will range from slight to a light chop, with waves between one and four feet.

Similar unsettled weather is expected on Wednesday, with cloudy spells and a few showers and thunderstorms developing around the country.

Meanwhile, Tropical Storm Fay remains far out in the Atlantic and poses no threat to Belize.

World.title: ‘Not The Time Or The Place’: Toledo East Rep Osmond Martinez draws backlash after Independence Day attack on UDP candidate, accuses UDP of racism, quotes Bible, gets heckled
World.content:
‘Not The Time Or The Place’: Toledo East Rep Osmond Martinez draws backlash after Independence Day attack on UDP candidate, accuses UDP of racism, quotes Bible, gets heckled

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Honduran-born Toledo East Area Representative and Minister of State for Economic Transformation Dr. Osmond Martinez is facing criticism after using his Independence Day address in Punta Gorda to launch a lengthy political broadside against UDP mayoral candidate Franklin “Kranka” Polonio and the United Democratic Party. Martinez currently serves as Minister of State for Economic Transformation, while Polonio is the UDP’s mayoral candidate for Punta Gorda ahead of the March 3, 2027 municipal elections.

Martinez spent much of his address, approximately 11-minutes, contrasting the PUP’s record in Toledo with that of the UDP and Polonio, at one point challenging Polonio to compare what he accomplished during six years in municipal government with what Martinez said has been achieved over the past two years.

The speech took an especially sharp turn when Martinez accused the UDP of discriminating against Maya and Hispanic Belizeans. “Because the UDP is a party that endorses discrimination against the Mayan people, the Hispanic people,” Martinez declared, after alleging that Maya communities had previously been abandoned and denied development, including electricity.

Martinez then pointed to infrastructure works in Bella Vista as evidence of the current administration’s record, telling the gathering that the village now has one concrete street and promising more. “Bella Vista for the first time has a concrete street. We will have a second and a third street before the year is done,” he said. He also cited plans for a market and a new police station.

The remarks did not go uninterrupted. Martinez was heckled several times from the gathering, including while invoking the Bible. In one exchange, a person could be heard objecting in Kriol, apparently telling Martinez not to “bring up” the Bible because he was “wicked.” Another person challenged him over the political nature of his remarks.

Reaction online was also heated. In comments beneath one Facebook post carrying the video, several viewers argued that Independence Day was the wrong occasion for partisan attacks. “There is a place and time for everything,” one commenter wrote, while another said, “This was not the time n place for that sir.” Others defended Martinez, with one commenter writing, “Truth be told!!! Bridge must be crossed. Bravo Minister.” The thread had attracted more than 100 comments and dozens of shares at the time it was captured, but the comments represent reactions to that particular post and not a scientific measure of wider public opinion.

Former UDP Chairman Alberto August issued an even harsher response, accusing Martinez of using a “national day of unity” as a political platform and repeatedly referring to him as a “JACKASS.” August also wrote that while he was “no proponent of violence,” if Martinez had been “stoned off stage” it was something he had “earned.” August is a former senior UDP official who remains publicly active in political commentary.

UDP Toledo East also responded online, claiming Martinez’s speech showed that he was “frustrated” and that the PUP was “losing ground” in Toledo East. Those are partisan assertions ahead of the municipal campaign and not independently established facts.

The PUP will contest Punta Gorda under mayoral candidate Maclovio Ack, who won the party’s August convention, setting the stage for another closely watched municipal contest in a town where the 2024 mayoral race between the PUP and Polonio was decided by a narrow margin.

World.title: ‘Pastor shot me twice’
World.content:
SMITH... was pastor of Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James

A witness broke down in tears on Monday while recounting the terrifying ordeal of being shot twice in the back by his late pastor, Dr Kevin Smith, who had assured him that he was immortal and could not die.

The witness, who also testified that Smith emptied two firearm magazines at members of the security forces on October 17, 2021 at Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James, received permission from Justice Leighton Pusey to remove his shirt in court to show the scars from the ordeal.

Last week, the witness told the court that Smith had another member of the congregation stab him in the back. He also used the opportunity, while he was shirtless, to point to the area of his back where he had been stabbed.

Monday was the witness’s second day on the stand in the Home Circuit Court murder trial in Kingston of Andre Ruddock, who is accused of killing 39-year-old Taneka Gardner during an alleged human sacrifice ritual at the church on October 17, 2021.

Ruddock allegedly acted on the instructions of Pastor Smith, who had asked Gardner if she believed that he could bring her back to life if her throat was cut.

Gardner’s throat was subsequently cut, allegedly by Ruddock, after she gave an answer in the affirmative to Smith’s question.

The witness had testified that after Gardner’s throat was cut, Smith further instructed Ruddock to cut her head off. It was alleged that while Ruddock was doing as he was instructed, a cow broke loose from a section of the church property and Ruddock’s attention was shifted from Gardner after Smith gave more instructions for the cow to be caught and slaughtered. A member of the church allegedly chased the cow.

The witness, Gardner, and Ruddock were members of Smith’s congregation.

The witness recalled Smith walking over to him while he was on the ground in agony and stuffing his fingers in his wounds.

“I was saying, ‘I am in pain, I am in pain.’ I remember he walked over to me. I don’t remember him speaking but I can remember him pushing his fingers in the wounds in my back. On the compound, there were a lot of individuals sitting on the boardwalk. The persons he [Smith] had called to come in, they were also sitting on the boardwalk. I looked up and I saw my mom sitting there,” the witness said.

He also testified that police and soldiers came to the boardwalk.

“One of the soldiers was kicking me in my side. He was saying to me that I was shooting at him. I told him I wasn’t doing that, and a police officer came and said to the soldier to ‘Stop, don’t you see that he was shot and cramped?’

“The soldiers started ordering the other [church] members outside, telling them to hold their heads straight. They were very hostile. An ambulance came and the police assisted them to wrap my back. They placed me on a stretcher and brought me through the side gate that was there,” the witness said, explaining that Gardner’s body was still laying on the church compound at that time.

“Taneka’s body was there. Blood was there. I was able to see. I was laying face down on the stretcher so I was able to see because the compound was not dark. When I was going through the gate, I saw Andre Ruddock on the ground. He was laying on his side. I also saw Dr Smith on the ground with his hands behind him. There was nothing blocking my view. Kevin Smith was laying face down. Security forces were all over the compound. At the gate there were police and soldiers. I was taken to the Cornwall Regional Hospital,” he told the court.

The witness said Smith was the one who shot him with a firearm he had taken from a member of the church.

“There were like three police jeeps on the outside of the premises. They were opposite the gate on the other side. At that time, a police officer was climbing on the fence [to see what was happening]. Mr Smith started to say he was Elijah and he was saying just as Elijah called down fire from heaven to consume the army, he said ‘If I be a prophet of God, I call down fire from heaven to consume these 50. He said it like three times, and he then called out for a member of the Jamaica Constabulary Force who was there [as a member of the church]. She came to him and he spoke to her and she spoke back to him,” the witness said.

By that time, Gardner was already killed, allegedly by Ruddock.

The witness, who was asked by lead prosecutor LaToya Bernard to tell the court what happened after the member of the police force spoke to Smith, explained that the pastor used the gun he had received from the member of the church to open fire at the security forces who were outside the compound of the church.

“Dr Smith started shooting at the police. At that time I stepped away and went right behind a round column that was there when Dr Smith took the gun from her. I could see him firing the gun from behind the column. He was firing the gun towards the police. I wasn’t observing everything happening on the compound. I was mainly watching him and was wondering if the police were going to shoot back,” the witness told the court.

“That was why I was behind the column. When I was looking towards where the police were I could see police bending down. I did not see them return any fire. After that happened, Dr Kevin Smith then called [the police member of the church] to bring an extra magazine [for the gun]. Dr Smith continued to fire. The police did not retaliate. Outside the premises there were members from the congregation out there along with the police. Those members on the outside weren’t running or moving or anything at all. They were just out there,” the witness testified.

He said the next thing he remembered after Smith shot at the security forces were loud explosions at the gate where the police shot and killed a member of the church who was following Smith’s instructions to attack them with a knife.

After he put his shirt back on, the witness, who had been standing during his testimony, was given an opportunity to sit and compose himself while he cried.

“Yes, Mr Kevin Smith shot me. I can remember hearing loud explosions coming from right beside me, where Mr Smith was. I fell to the ground after I felt like I got a hard punch. I remember jumping up back like I was shocked. He looked on me and said to me that, ‘You are immortal and you cannot die’. Yes, that’s what he said. I could see some police officers standing at the top of where a boardwalk was. They were on the premises by this time.

“Mr Smith then spoke to Kevaughn Plummer. I can’t recall where Andre Ruddock was at the time when Dr Smith was firing at the police. Dr Smith spoke to Kevaughn Plummer and he ran towards the police to attack them. He had a knife and he ran towards them to attack them. Upon reaching close proximity to the police, I just started seeing fire coming from the police’s gun. I could hear the loud explosions. I saw when Kevaughn Plummer’s body fell to the ground. It happened so quickly. It was just a lot of shots being fired all over the compound. By that time, because of the pain I was feeling, I was laying flat on my belly at that time on the boardwalk. I was hearing a lot of shots. At that time I turned my head and saw him [Dr Smith] sitting in the same place where he was sitting when we first came up the boardwalk. He was sitting and pointing to the sky,” the witness said.

Pastor Smith died on October 25, 2021 in a motor vehicle crash on the Linstead bypass in St Catherine while being transported to Kingston to face charges.

World.title: Motorcycle mayhem
World.content:
In this file photo Inspector Amos Thompson points to a number of motorcycles that were seized by the Westmoreland police.

WESTMORELAND is recording one of its lowest murder counts in years but police say the parish is facing another public safety threat involving motorcycles, prompting a call for tougher national measures to tackle dangerous riding.

Commanding officer for the division, Senior Superintendent Othneil Dobson said the police will continue seizing and prosecuting offenders but believes the country must change its approach to the motorcycle problem.

The call comes as Westmoreland records a 29 per cent reduction in murders between January 1 and September 12, with the number falling from 28 in 2025 to 20 this year.

But while the division works to maintain the reduction in violent crime, Dobson said motorcycle-related crashes remain a persistent road safety concern, particularly in a parish where motorcycles are widely used as a means of transportation.

Speaking during a recent episode of the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s Force4Good Podcast, Dobson said the police have been carrying out daily enforcement operations, supported by specialised teams, but dangerous riding continues to result in fatalities.

“I would not sit here and tell you that most of the persons are obeying the road traffic law. Most of the accidents are a result of careless driving, persons not having the best will or thinking about the other road users. So, we have high numbers of fatalities — but it’s not a lack of trying from the police,” he said.

Dobson reported the police have recorded some success, but the recurring nature of motorcycle crashes means enforcement must be accompanied by broader public education and changes in how Jamaica manages the issue.

“As a country, we’ll have to change some of what we’re doing with motorcycles. Most of the stations in Westmoreland are overrun with motorcycles… You seize 20 or 30 bikes and you’re driving to work the next morning and you see four or five persons riding past you with new bikes. They don’t even come back to the stations to retrieve the bikes after going through the licensing process again,” he said.

“So, as a country, we have to go from a policy perspective in terms of dealing with this bike situation. We will continue to seize, we will continue to prosecute, we will continue to educate… but the penalties just have to be higher penalties as it relates to bikes,” he argued.

World.title: Love & Harmony turns 10 with a family affair at sea
World.content:
The Love and Harmony entertainment package for 2027 will include: (clockwise from top left) Aidonia, I-Wayne, D’Yani, Kevin Downswell, Beres Hammond and Sanchez.

For a decade, Love & Harmony Cruise has been bringing Caribbean music lovers together on the high seas. Next year the celebration is getting even more personal as the popular music cruise marks its 10th anniversary.

With a special Mother’s Day voyage scheduled from May 6 to 11, 2027, the whole family will be invited to celebrate a milestone that has become as much about community as it is about music.

Reggae icon Beres Hammond will be captaining the ship once more and, as it has done for the past nine years, the Love and Harmony crew expects to deliver an unforgettable experience on the high seas.

Veteran Beres Hammond will be joined by Sanchez, D’Yani, Aidonia, Kevin Downswell, and I-Wayne for the special anniversary sail dates, with more artistes and entertainment still to be announced.

The six-day, five-night experience will be a round trip from Miami aboard the Norwegian Jewel, making stops in Montego Bay, Jamaica, and Nassau, Bahamas.

But while the 10th anniversary promises the concerts, parties, and entertainment that guests have come to expect, organisers are placing a special emphasis on family this time around.

“Ten years is an incredible milestone for Love & Harmony, but what makes this anniversary even more meaningful is that we are sailing over Mother’s Day weekend,” Director of Marketing and Public Relations Ronnie Tomlinson said.

“Love & Harmony Cruise has always felt like a family reunion at sea. We have guests who return year after year, and this time we want them to bring their mothers, children, and loved ones and celebrate together. This is more than a cruise, it is six days of Caribbean culture, music, food, laughter and memories,” he said

That family-friendly approach is reflected in the offer for the 2027 sailing, with children 12 and younger sailing for free, subject to applicable taxes and fees.

And for those who have experienced Love & Harmony before, the promise is familiar: Once the ship leaves Miami, the party does not stop simply because the sun goes down.

Live concerts, themed parties, DJ experiences, karaoke, games, comedy, poolside activities, and the Captain’s Dinner will fill the schedule, while Caribbean flavours will remain an important part of the experience.

Guests can expect a mix of Caribbean and American fare alongside Norwegian Jewel’s fine and casual dining options, with Jamaican favourites such as oxtail, ackee and saltfish, jerk chicken, and curry goat among the flavours that have helped bring the island experience aboard.

While music remains the heartbeat of Love & Harmony, laughter has increasingly become part of its soundtrack and as such comedy will play a big part in the cruise’s itinerary come May. Canadian comedian Trixx will return following his appearance on the 2026 sailing, while Jamaican-British comedian White Yardie will make his Love & Harmony debut. The comedy offering adds another layer to a voyage that has evolved beyond a traditional music cruise, giving guests something to do whether they are catching a concert, lounging poolside, or simply looking for a reason to laugh.

The anniversary celebration makes its way back to Jamaican soil when the Norwegian Jewel docks in Montego Bay on Saturday, May 8. Love & Harmony will take over Tropical Bliss Beach for a special destination experience hosted by dancehall star Aidonia, giving guests the chance to trade the ship for sand, sea, and the unmistakable energy of Montego Bay. The ship is scheduled to be in port from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, allowing Harmonisers to spend the day experiencing Jamaica before returning to the vessel and continuing the anniversary festivities.

Then, on Sunday, May 9 — Mother’s Day — the ship will remain at sea.

For organisers, the timing is intentional.

Rather than rushing from one destination to another, families will have the entire day to celebrate together, surrounded by music, food, entertainment, and the community that Love & Harmony has cultivated over the past decade.

The cruise will then head to Nassau, Bahamas, on May 10 before returning to Miami on May 11.

With additional artistes, DJs, special events and anniversary surprises still to be announced, the 2027 sailing is shaping up to be both a look back at Love & Harmony’s first decade and a celebration of the people who helped make the journey possible.

World.title: THE HUNDRED THAT WASN’T ENOUGH
World.content:
Jayden Seales of Antigua and Barbuda Falcons celebrates the dismissal of Kirk McKenzie of Jamaica Kingsmen during the Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League Final on Sunday.

JAMAICA Kingsmen Captain Rovman Powell said he was proud of his team despite an eight-wicket defeat to Antigua and Barbuda Falcons in the Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League final at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados, on Sunday.

Antigua and Barbuda Falcons needed just 16.4 overs to chase down Kingsmen 170-9 and win their first-ever Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) title, turning Maaz Sadaqat’s brutal 114 from 58 balls into a footnote.

“It’s a good feeling, to be honest. I think it’s a very hard-fought campaign for us. I’m so proud of the boys,” Powell said in a televised interview.

Batting first after losing the toss, Kingsmen were 30-2 in the fourth over before Sadaqat exploded. The left-hander hammered nine sixes and eight fours in a stunning hundred, adding 80 runs for the third wicket with Saim Ayub (29) to surge to 100-2 after 10 overs where it looked like the Kingsmen would have reached the 200-run mark.

However, the Falcons’ left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqim produced the spell of the tournament — four for 14 runs from four overs — and ripped the guts from the Kingsmen’s innings. After Ayub’s dismissal at 110-3 in the 12th over, no Kingsmen batsman made double figures.

Powell said his side fell short with the bat in the second half of their innings.

“I think after the halfway stage we felt as if we were 10 to 15 runs short,” Powell admitted.

“We knew it was a pretty good batting wicket. Credit has to be given to our batters for the first 10 overs. Maaz played fantastically for us, and the partnership he strung with Saim Ayub carried us to 100 for 2 in 10 overs. It’s disappointing that as a batting group on such a good wicket we didn’t really capitalise on that start,” he further said, hailing Ayub’s removal of Rakheem Cornwall (20) at 20-1 in the first over, and Evin Lewis’s (38) fall to Vitel Lawes at 84-2 in the eighth over.

Despite these feats, however, the chase was a demolition as

Amir Jangoo (57 not out) and Hasan Nawaz (47 not out) never looked troubled as they finished the job with 20 balls to spare.

“I think as a batting group, when we lost four wickets in the middle overs, four key batters who were supposed to put the impetus on the game in the last 10 overs, and as a bowling group, we didn’t control the powerplay as well as we wanted to,” Powell said.

But for Jamaica, a team that lost its first few games and was written off, Powell said that the final itself was redemption.

“I honestly feel it’s a proud journey for us. We have accomplished a lot of things. We set out to be in the finals, and when we came to the tournament we wanted to see if we could progress all the way. It was a slow start to the competition, as we lost our first few games, but we built a little bit of momentum with our home crowd back home in Jamaica and from there the guys started to believe that we could actually play cricket,” Powell said.”

“We went to Trinidad, which is a difficult place to play cricket, and we played a very good game down there. That confidence kept building within the team. We knew that as soon as we squeezed into the last four of the competition how dangerous our team could be, and the guys just kept chipping in. Credit has to be given to them throughout the entire competition. They listened to the leadership that myself and the head coach provided and I am actually proud of the boys,” he said.

World.title: BAILEY’S OUT!
World.content:
Jamaica footballer Leon Bailey (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

WITH the Jamaica’s Reggae Boyz eyeing a spot in the knockout stages of the Concacaf Nations League, they will have to do so without winger Leon Bailey who has withdrawn from the entire group stage campaign.

Bailey, who recently signed for perennial Greek champions Olympiakos FC, was one of the marquee names in interim head coach Rudolph Speid’s 24-man squad and was due to join the group on Monday, ahead of their opening game against Guatemala at the National Stadium on Friday.

Although the Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) made no official announcement on Bailey’s withdrawal, Bailey didn’t arrive on the island and will stay in Greece as he recovers from an injury.

The 29-year-old has reportedly been suffering with the injury since playing just over 13 minutes in Olympiakos’s 2-1 win over Jagiellonia Bialystok in the UEFA Europa League last Thursday. Bailey missed the club’s Sunday’s Super League Greece clash against Levadiakos.

Greek journalist George Stasinopoulos played down the severity of the injury but said, “Olympiacos came to an agreement with the medical staff of the Jamaican national team, with both sides coming to an agreement and ultimately Leon Bailey not getting on the plane to make the trip for his national team.

“He suffered from injuries last season and faced several issues, so they have decided to pay enough attention to the Jamaican and take advantage of the break.”

Europa League champion Bailey will miss not only Friday’s game against Guatemala and Monday’s clash with Honduras at the National Stadium, but also the away fixtures against El Salvador next Friday and Honduras on October 5, which will complete Jamaica’s Group B fixtures in Nations League A.

It’s the second-consecutive season where he’s missed the national team’s group stage campaign, having missed all four games in 2024 against Cuba, Honduras (twice) and Nicaragua.

Bailey, who has seven goals in 41 caps for the Reggae Boyz, also missed the entirety of last year’s final round of Concacaf World Cup Qualifiers after picking up several injuries during his short loan spell at AS Roma in Serie A. Jamaica ultimately finished runners-up behind Curacao, and missed automatic qualification to the 2026 FIFA World Cup in United States, Mexico and Canada.

The former Aston Villa winger did feature in the World Cup play-offs in March against New Caledonia and DR Congo but has missed 17 of Jamaica’s last 28 competitive fixtures.

The Jamaica Observer has learnt that a replacement for Bailey is set to be announced Tuesday, with Speid and his technical staff still considering their options as late as Monday afternoon.

Last Friday, Speid revealed he scouted 72 players for the Nations League group stage before selecting the final squad. He also said he invited players outside of the initial 24 to train with the squad as part of a scouting mission, but those names haven’t been made public.

Most of the group participated in an activation session on Monday, with the others set to join the team in their first training session on Tuesday at the National Stadium.

The Reggae Boyz need to finish top two in their group to advance to the quarter-finals where they would play one of Concacaf’s top four nations, Mexico, USA, Canada or Panama, which were pre-seeded.

World.title: The Wellness Wedding: How Healthy Living Is Changing the Guest Experience
World.content:
Wedding bar trends are evolving rapidly. Mindful drinking is becoming increasingly common amongst guests, prompting couples to serve elevated zero-proof options.

Weddings have traditionally been celebrations of indulgence — open bars, impressive appetizers, fancy dinners, decadent desserts and late-night comfort food.. But as lifestyles change, so do weddings.

Today’s younger couples are increasingly health-conscious. They drink less, pay more attention to what they eat and are more aware of dietary restrictions and overall wellness. Naturally, those habits are beginning to influence how they entertain their wedding guests.

The result isn’t the completely “healthy wedding”. It is a more conscious wedding experience, where indulgence and enjoyment coexist with choice.

The Bar Is Changing

One of the biggest shifts is at the bar. Not drinking — or simply drinking less — has become increasingly normal, and zero-proof options are moving well beyond basic fruit punch.

Zero-proof spirits, botanical spritzes, alcohol-free sparkling wines and beautifully constructed mocktails can now be presented with the same attention as traditional cocktails. Couples can even create alcoholic and zero-proof versions of their signature drink.

The message isn’t that we don’t drink. It is you don’t have to drink to fully participate in the celebration.

Food Is Becoming Lighter But Not Boring

Wedding menus are changing too. Couples are increasingly balancing fried hors d’oeuvres, heavy sauces and late-night comfort foods with grilled proteins, ceviches, sushi, fresh seafood, vegetable-forward dishes, salads and fruit.

This isn’t about putting wedding guests on a diet. It is about balance.

A Jamaican wedding doesn’t have to abandon jerk, curry or other favourites. Those dishes can sit comfortably beside grilled seafood, roasted vegetables, vibrant salads and fresh tropical fruit. Guests can indulge while still having choices that reflect how they normally eat.

Dietary Consciousness Is Hospitality

Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free and allergy-conscious options are also becoming part of normal event planning rather than afterthoughts.

Couples can collect dietary requirements through RSVPs, clearly label buffet selections and ensure alternative meals receive the same attention as the main menu. The vegetarian guest should no longer be served whatever the kitchen can quickly assemble after everyone else has eaten.

That is where wellness becomes good hospitality.

Smoking Is Being Reconsidered

Smoking is another part of the guest experience couples are approaching differently. Cigarette and cigar smoke doesn’t have to drift through lounges, dining areas or dance floors simply because a wedding is outdoors.

Designated smoking areas and thoughtfully positioned cigar lounges allow those who want the experience to enjoy it without imposing it on everyone else.

Wellness Beyond the Reception

For destination weddings, wellness can extend across the entire weekend through morning yoga, spa experiences, fresh juice and smoothie stations, healthier welcome amenities and lighter morning-after brunches.

The idea is simple: Enjoy yourself tonight and still feel good tomorrow.

A New Definition of Luxury

None of this means taking the fun out of weddings. Serve the Champagne, cake and late-night comfort food. Just remember that not everyone drinks, eats meat, wants fried food, or smokes.

The strongest interpretation of the wellness trend isn’t restriction. It is choice.

Luxury hospitality has always been about anticipating what guests might want before they have to ask. For today’s couples, that increasingly means creating a celebration where different lifestyles can comfortably coexist.

The modern wedding isn’t becoming less indulgent. It is becoming more considerate — and perhaps that is one of the most meaningful shifts in the modern guest experience.

World.title: A Cuban zoo, and its animals, in epic battle for survival
World.content:
Two Bengal tiger cubs (Panthera tigris) rest at the National Zoo of Havana in Havana on September 15, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

HAVANA, Cuba (AFP) — Every day, veterinarians and zookeepers make their way to Cuba’s National Zoo by whatever means they can, determined to not abandon the nearly 1,000 animals in their care and help save species at risk of extinction.

Their dedication and food donations are vital to keeping alive an array of rhinos, jaguars and tigers — including an extremely rare white tiger — in the midst of a severe crisis that has left many Cubans struggling to feed themselves.

Just getting to the reserve situated 20 kilometres (12 miles) from central Havana is a headache for staff, as public transportation has come to a near standstill nine months into a US fuel blockade.

“The workers come by bicycle, pedal scooter or electric motorbike to ensure the animals have food and water every day,” said Yoel Machado, the zoo’s animal welfare manager.

Their efforts are about more than keeping the animals fed.

The 345-hectare (850-acre) park serves as a genetic reserve of international conservation importance, housing breeding populations of vulnerable or endangered species, including black and white rhinos, hippos and jaguars.

Yet the same crisis that has left workers scrambling to source meat, medicine and water has forced the zoo to curb reproduction programs and increasingly rely on handouts to sustain its animals.

During a recent visit by AFP, two Bengal tiger cubs, one an extremely rare white specimen, frolicked in their enclosure beneath the watchful gaze of their mother, oblivious to the strenuous efforts made to keep them alive.

AFP did not see any animals that appeared malnourished or ill, but Angel Cordero, the veterinarian in charge of big cats, said the tiger cubs “could be in better shape.”

He revealed he needed to ration their food to prevent it from running out.

“It’s no use giving them plenty if it only lasts three days,” he said.

Big cats need about seven kilograms (15 pounds) of meat per day per adult, but such quantities are hard to come by.

Even when it is available, recurring blackouts of up to 30 hours at a stretch make it difficult to preserve.

With fuel extremely scarce, there’s also the issue of how to distribute food in a nature reserve the size of New York’s Central Park.

For now, private donors have come to the rescue for the zoo’s various needs.

Every Monday, Ana Fernandez, a Cuban-American woman born in Tennessee who has been living in Cuba for nine years, donates meat.

“The animals shouldn’t have to suffer,” the 50-year-old said, though she added that “some days it’s not enough for all of them.”

Recently, the reserve went 23 days without electricity, which meant it also lacked running water.

The staff “didn’t just sit around waiting for things to fall from the sky,” the zoo’s director Juan Carlos Corella said.

“We looked for solutions, water trucks were brought in, and we found food for the animals almost daily,” he said, while admitting that keeping the park open has become “very difficult.”

An exodus of vets has added to the zoo’s woes.

More than a third have left for better-paying jobs elsewhere, mostly in Cuba’s burgeoning private sector.

Some wait tables in cafes while others work for private veterinary clinics.

The zoo is home to the only breeding group of black rhinos outside of Africa, as well as a large population of white rhinos, the largest herd of Grant’s zebras in the Americas and hippos that regularly bear calves.

“Here we have a high genetic value, and one of immense international importance,” Machado, the animal welfare manager, explained.

However, the crisis has forced the park to slow down its breeding programs.

The reason is simple: each new offspring requires more food, medicine, and staff.

“We can’t keep increasing the number of animals,” Machado said, adding that he preferred to ensure the current population was “as well cared for as possible.”

And yet life keeps renewing itself, regardless.

In recent months, the zoo has welcomed baby tigers, hyenas, jackals, and a black dromedary named Esperanza (Spanish for “Hope”), the first of its kind born in Cuba in three decades.

World.title: Golding makes fresh bid to overhaul Crown lands law
World.content:
A screen grab of PNP President Mark Golding addressing the public session of the party's 88th Annual Conference on Sunday.

SAVANNA-LA-MAR, Westmoreland — Following two failed attempts to introduce a private member’s bill that would reduce the qualifying period for Jamaicans illegally occupying Crown lands from 60 to 25 years, People’s National Party (PNP) President Mark Golding announced that another attempt will be made to have the bill accepted by Parliament.

Golding stated this will take place as soon as Parliament returns from its summer break which is slated for Tuesday.

“And I will seek the support of both sides of the House of Representatives to pass it into law. We want justice when it comes to land in Jamaica,” stated Golding as he delivered the main addressing the PNP’s 88th Annual Conference at Independence Park in Savanna-la-Mar on Sunday.

​According to Golding, he took the bill to Parliament in July, where two attempts were made to have it tabled before the summer recess.

“I was blocked from doing so by the Speaker of the House.”

Currently, the qualifying period to acquire ownership of Government land through adverse possession — the legal principle allowing individuals to claim ownership of land through unauthorised, continuous, and open occupation for a specific period — is 60 years.

This contrasts with the 12 years it takes for persons occupying private property to be able to make a claim.

Golding pointed out that this duration was legislated in the 1830s around the time of emancipation, when life expectancy in Jamaica was less than 60 years.

“The formerly enslaved people of Jamaica were not given any land at emancipation, and that 60-year rule was plainly intended to ensure that the people did not acquire ownership of land by possession when they left those plantations,” argued Golding.

“That is why I have prepared the legislation entitled The Crown Lands Reform Act 2026, which seeks Parliament to reduce 60 years to 25 years, subject to a fair legal process.

Golding said the proposed bill would also enable an area impacted by a disaster such as Hurricane Melissa last October, to be declared a Disaster Adjudication Area so that legitimate claims for ownership by possession or otherwise can be settled quickly and titles issued to those who can establish their entitlement.

The Opposition Leader had first made the proposal for the change in the law while on the campaign trail in the lead up to the September 2025 General Election.

At that time Golding had told a party meeting in Spanish Town, St Catherine: “When I think of all the thousands of Jamaicans who live on land, and have occupied that land for years but don’t have security of tenure, and they can’t use their investment in the property to further themselves with education, or in business or to deal with any emergency, I say time come to reform that 1833 law that says you have to be on land of government for 60 years before you can become an owner.

“And we going to drop it substantially so that the people who have been there for at least 25 years will be entitled to their titles. It’s not one or two, but tens of thousands, possibly hundreds of thousands of Jamaicans who will benefit from becoming owners of the rock because of that one piece of emancipatory legislation that we will be bringing forward”.

World.title: France extends fuel subsidies to shield consumers from skyrocketing energy prices
World.content:
PARIS — The French government said Tuesday it would spend €450 million to extend fuel subsidies until the end of the year to help companies and workers affected by the economic consequences of the war in the Middle East.

“We hear the concerns of the French people, which sometimes take the form of anger. These concerns and this anger are sincere, and we must address them. That is what we are doing today,” Economy and Finance Minister Roland Lescure told reporters Tuesday.

The package includes a €0.15 per liter subsidy on non-road diesel for farmers and €0.20 per liter subsidy for construction company trucks. The government will also double the subsidy from €0.20 to €0.40 for those with low incomes who must drive for work, such as nurses who carry out home visits.

World.title: Nothing ‘to be ashamed of:’ EU’s center-right clashes with Socialists over far-right votes
World.content:
“We should go beyond that. On some issues, I think that they [the far right] are relatively sane. On some other issues, there’s insanity,” he added, while insisting a majority of votes in Parliament will involve the mainstream parties.

Since the 2024 EU election, the EPP has repeatedly passed legislation with support from right-wing and far-right groups, particularly on migration and green policy — topics where the centrist groups have the widest gaps between them — sidelining its traditional centrist and center-left partners.

Liberals and Social Democrats are now pushing for binding, coalition-style commitments among the three centrist forces to prevent the EPP from turning to the far right.

“We need to step up also our game in the center … if we don’t find compromises within files, we have to find it across files,” said René Repasi, head of the German Social Democrats in the Parliament, who was taking part in the panel debate with Aaltola. “We need to not to dilute everything in compromises, but give everybody their wins, and that is the point: You need to have this in an agreement with a binding governance structure that includes many other members than simply the leaders in order to increase ownership.”

However, Aaltola pushed back against the idea, arguing that the Parliament’s political reality is more diverse. “That’s kind of a Soviet election result type of politics, there’s always going to be diversity,” he said. “That’s what democracy is all about, and so we cannot hammer out that coalition agreement that would be millimeter tight, and no voter will buy it from us.”

Renew Europe Vice Chair Gerben-Jan Gerbrandy, who was also on the panel, argued that centrist unity is essential to tackle Ukraine, geopolitics, climate change, and the cost-of-living crisis, warning that fights over the far-right firewall are distracting from more pressing concerns for EU citizens.

World.title: EU and Canada to unveil new partnership, but it may not be ‘associate membership,’ says ambassador
World.content:
“Ultimately, I’m less fussed about what we end up calling it. I’m more fussed about that we have initiatives that are really going to drive prosperity, economic security, and a range of things moving forward,” he said.

The EU and Canada are in the process of identifying areas to upgrade their partnership, including critical raw materials, AI, research and innovation. Asked when those deals could be signed, Wilkinson said they would be coming “pretty soon,” with several planned for the joint EU–Canada summit in October.

“This is not something that you commit to do, and it’s five years later. This is something that we’re looking to do within the next 12 months,” he went on. “I’m not sure what you’re going to call it, but a much deeper and closer relationship.”

The idea of associate membership raised eyebrows among EU diplomats, who said capitals had not been asked whether they supported the plan — and pointed out that no such legal relationship is defined in the bloc’s foundational treaties.

However, two EU officials, granted anonymity to explain the arrangement, said it was a way to brand a new kind of partnership that goes deeper than existing trade, research and defense agreements.

World.title: Trump signs ‘fantastic’ Greenland security deal with Denmark
World.content:
Trump promised to build two “very major military bases” on the territory, adding that he’s “formed a bond” with the people of “beautiful” Denmark and the Greenlanders during the negotiations. The legal text of the deal is available here.

“I know it’s going to be a long-term, fantastic relationship,” Trump said at the signing ceremony later, alongside the prime ministers of Denmark, Mette Frederiksen, and Greenland, Jens-Frederik Nielsen.

Frederiksen thanked Trump for the agreement, labeling it a good deal for the U.S., Denmark and Greenland that would keep enemies and adversaries away.

“Seventy-five years ago, we entered into an agreement about the defense of Greenland,” she said. “Today we are signing an even bigger and better agreement — a deal that can last forever.”

Nielsen said Greenland’s territory had been supporting U.S. security since World War II. “We are, have been and will remain a steadfast friend of the United States and a part of the Western alliance. Your security is our security, and our security is your security,” he said.

At the start of the year, Trump horrified European and NATO allies with his push to annex the sovereign Danish territory. Denmark has been a member of NATO since the alliance was founded in 1949.

World.title: US fighter jet crashes at air base in western Germany
World.content:
The Spangdahlem Air Base in Germany is pictured in October 2020. | Maja Hitij/Getty Images

An F-16 Fighting Falcon fighter jet assigned to the U.S. Air Force’s 52nd Fighter Wing crashed at Spangdahlem Air Base in western Germany on Tuesday afternoon.

The aircraft came down at around 2:30 p.m. local time, the 52nd Fighter Wing told POLITICO. The pilot ejected safely and received immediate medical care from emergency-response personnel. An investigation into the incident is ongoing, and “additional information will be released as it becomes available,” the spokesperson said.

German air traffic control told German outlet SWR that the crash followed an exercise involving several aircraft. Other planes diverted to Ramstein air base after the incident.

World.title: France opposes foreign aid cuts in EU budget
World.content:
EU governments, including France, are lobbying the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU — which is steering the budget talks — to reflect their positions in a new budget negotiating document, known as a negobox, that is expected to be unveiled in early October.

Several capitals have signaled that savings to the Global Europe Fund — a €200 billion pot governing the bloc’s support to foreign countries — are preferable to cuts to domestic policies, such as agriculture, defense and regional payments.

The European Commission has internally simulated the impact of slashing its development aid budget by as much as 40% in its next long-term budget. However, the Irish presidency is expected to propose milder cuts.

According to Haddad, the real challenge is to ensure that EU policy on trade, migration and development is better organized across different institutions.

“All of this is very scattered through the institutions today. Sometimes [we are] not able to really leverage all the different instruments for our external policy,” he said.

Speaking alongside Haddad, his Polish counterpart Ignacy Niemczycki said that increases to foreign aid from the last budget have been smaller than in other areas such as defense and competitiveness.

“Even if we see some minor changes, it doesn’t have to automatically mean that it will need to get rid of whole programs, but then it really depends on where we land with the negotiations,” he said.

World.title: New Princess Diana memoir hits shelves amid royal tensions
World.content:
Charles Spencer’s new book about his late sister, Princess Diana, goes on sale after searing extracts prompted a rare and sharp rebuttal from King Charles III.

 

In ‘Swan Song: Diana, My Sister’, Spencer says he wants to speak on Diana’s behalf and correct untruths that have become accepted over time. The memoir alleges rows with the then-Prince Charles over the 1997 funeral and accuses him of contempt for his ex-wife.

Spencer claims he argued with Charles over palace plans for Prince William and Prince Harry, then 15 and 12, to walk behind their mother’s coffin. He says the then-Prince Charles “went ballistic” and told him: “Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.” He also says Charles sounded “elated” after Diana’s death in a Paris car crash at 36.

Buckingham Palace responded with a strongly worded statement, saying grief can cloud reason and colour memory.

World.title: Trump signs Greenland security deal allowing US to expand military presence
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has signed a new Greenland security deal with Denmark and the island territory.

 

Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, and Greenland PM Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed the agreement on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday.

Under the terms of the deal, shared online by the Danish Foreign Ministry, the US will be permitted to expand its military presence on Greenland through the modernisation and enlargement of its current Pituffik Space Base and the establishment of new defence areas at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig.

It will also allow the US "free access to and movement between" defence areas across Greenland, "including the Territorial Waters, by land, air and sea." American aircraft may also fly over and land in any territory on the island, it states.

Trump previously said the deal - which also reaffirms the "sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark" and recognises Greenland's "right to self determination" - would see Washington take "permanent control" of the island's security.

"From now on, no U.S. adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval," he wrote in a post on Truth Social on Friday.

Both Frederiksen and Nielsen have welcomed the agreement - which stops short of Trump's wish to seize the territory for the US, a move he had argued was essential for the US' "national security."

In a statement on Friday, Frederiksen said the deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic Area," while Nielsen said it was "to the benefit of us all."

The US is reported to have had 17 military facilities and over 10,000 troops on Greenland at the height of the Cold War. It currently operates just one base on the island, the Pituffik Space Base - the US Department of Defense's northernmost installation.

Pituffik is used for missile warning, missile defense and space surveillance missions, per the US Space Force.

World.title: EU budget talks face deadlock despite push for year-end deal
World.content:
European affairs ministers met in Brussels on Tuesday for another round of negotiations on the EU’s next seven-year budget. Despite a shared ambition to reach a deal by the end of the year, negotiations appear to have stalled, with significant differences still unresolved.

 

"This is my fourth [Multiannual Financial Framework] negotiations, so I have to admit that some of the discussions come with a large sense of déjà vu," European Commissioner for the Budget Piotr Serafin said during a debate with EU ministers on Tuesday.

“Many positions are quite predictable, as they have been consistently repeated over the last decades,” the commissioner added.

The next key stage in the negotiations will come at the European Council in Brussels in mid-October. Ahead of that meeting, the Irish government, which is currently chairing negotiations among the member states, will present a compromise text for leaders to consider.

“There is a general agreement to reach a deal by the end of the year,” Irish Minister for European Affairs Thomas Byrne told journalists on Tuesday, referring to discussions among the EU’s 27 member states.

October's text would mark the penultimate stage before a final compromise is expected in December, when EU leaders will need to bridge their differences and find a workable trade-off to break the deadlock.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa have repeatedly called for an ambitious budget, backed by new EU taxes and sufficient spending to match Europe’s ambitions in strategic sectors such as AI and defence, while preserving adequate funding for traditional areas such as agriculture and fisheries.

EU institutions want to avoid a repeat of the previous budget negotiations, when member states ultimately failed to agree on new sources of EU revenue, known as “own resources.” This time, however, growing global uncertainty and the Commission’s push to strengthen Europe’s competitiveness on the global stage have made the need for additional EU revenue to invest in strategic sectors even more pressing.

The €2 trillion proposal presented by the Commission in July 2025 reflected this trend. It provided increased funding for competitiveness, security, and defence, alongside significant cuts to agricultural and regional funds, compared with the current budget.

The two camps

Two main camps have emerged among member states in recent months. One, made up of 17 countries and known as the “Friends of Cohesion,” is pushing to preserve funding for agriculture and regional development.

Another group, including Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Finland, Sweden and Denmark, is calling for cuts of “several hundred billion euros” across the budget, while prioritising spending on defence and competitiveness. They refer to themselves as the “modernisers,” although they are also commonly described as the “frugals.”

Germany is leading the group of frugal countries and used the occasion on Tuesday to escalate its rhetoric, even in opposition to the position of EU institutions. Targeting Costa in particular—who has been outspoken against major budget cuts—German Minister Gunther Krichbaum said he had lost touch with reality. “You have to ask yourself whether Mr. Costa has now completely lost his grip on reality,” the minister told journalists on the sidelines of the meeting, as Germany continues to push for substantial cuts.

The “Friends of Cohesion” generally support the introduction of new “own resources,” while the frugal countries remain more sceptical.

They argue that, as net contributors, they will bear a disproportionate share of the cost of the next budget, noting that they already account for around 40% of contributions to the current one.

The budget is likely to be financed through a combination of contributions based on a percentage of member states’ gross national income (GNI) and new “own resources.” Member states will have to agree on the share of GNI to be allocated to the EU budget and determine which own resources should be mobilised to make up the remaining funding.

"I see many different ways of computing national contributions. It seems that there is a competition going on between capitals to come up with numbers that show that their national contribution increases the most. This is not really helpful," Serafin said during the debate on Tuesday, calling EU countries to build a "common understanding on the actual numbers" to present in the most objective way.

Byrne told journalists on Monday that the Irish presidency would put forward a set of proposals on own resources as part of the text to be presented in October.

To reach a deal, all the 27 member states have to agree on the new budget.

The final deal will also require the backing of the European Parliament, whose position on the budget differs significantly from that of the member states.

EU lawmakers are calling for a 10% increase in funding across the main budget headings and want the repayment of the Recovery Plan loans, issued in 2020 to support the economy following the COVID-19 pandemic, to be kept outside the regular EU budget.

During the discussion on Tuesday, leading MEPs asked the member states to avoid cuts.

"If we reduce the EU budget, EU countries will have to address these challenges separately at national level, and likely at a higher cost," said Romanian MEP Siegfried Mureșan, who is co-leading the negotiations on behalf of the European Parliament alongside Portuguese MEP Carla Tavares.

Tavares also urged member states to step up the negotiations.

"The clock is ticking, and we need to make progress if we are to reach an agreement on the next MFF in time. Parliament is ready to work towards the conditions needed for its consent, but the Council still needs to move forward as well, particularly on new genuine own resources," she said.
