World.title: Russia quietly modernises bomb shelters in Moscow and St Petersburg
World.content:
Russia is quietly modernising bomb shelters in Moscow and St Petersburg, with procurement data showing tens of millions of roubles being allocated for repairs that have not been publicly announced, as Ukrainian drones intensify strikes on Russian territory.

 

State procurement records, reported by Russian independent media, show 39 million roubles (€400,000) allocated in early September to restore nine facilities in three districts of Moscow's South-West administrative region, an area home to dozens of research institutes and defence contractors.

Work is due to be completed by 30 November and covers entrances, internal partitions, doors and utility systems including water, electricity, sewage, ventilation and communications.

Further funds have been earmarked for shelters in Moscow's eastern Novogireyevo district, and a major overhaul is planned in New Moscow for a shelter built in 1971 that includes its own diesel power station.

Tenders worth 200 million roubles (€2 million) were published at the start of summer for repairs to shelters in 17 districts, mainly in Moscow's eastern region.

In St Petersburg, the metro operator published a contractor search in early September to build bomb shelters at nine stations, four compartments and 35 kilometres of track.

The project involves large-scale adaptation of both operating and unfinished stations to civil defence requirements, including air filtration and pressurised air supply systems.

'End war, choose peace'

The Kremlin has increasingly felt the heat of Ukraine's strikes on its energy and business sectors, in Kyiv's ongoing bid to strip Russia's war machine of as much funding as possible.

On Sunday night, Ukrainian drones struck the Moscow refinery in Kapotnya, halting operations due to fires at primary oil processing units, according to reports.

In August, Ukrainian rocket developer FirePoint and former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said the Ukrainian armed forces could begin striking Moscow with new ballistic missiles by the end of the year.

"Moscow should not be building layered rings of air defence at the expense of other regions, but ending its brutal war and choosing peace," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

"There are steps for de-escalation on the table: in energy, in food security. What is needed is political will."

Moscow and St Petersburg's civil defence infrastructure largely dates to the 20th century and consists of command bunkers for government and military communications, and mass shelters for civilians, including the metro.

Recent inventories in St Petersburg found many shelters in need of repair, and a significant portion of basement space in residential buildings has passed into private hands.

Ukraine's metro systems — particularly in Kyiv, Kharkiv and Dnipro — have functioned as round-the-clock bomb shelters since Russia's full-scale invasion began in early 2022, with tens of thousands of people at a time sheltering in them during Moscow's daily air raids.

In frontline regions without a metro, purpose-built underground schools have been constructed so children can attend classes. Ukraine's public education system has also shifted to remote formats because of the persistent threat of Russian air strikes.

World.title: 17-year-old detained in Poland over alleged plans for terrorist attack
World.content:
Authorities in Poland have detained a 17-year-old accused of preparing an attack on a school and a mosque.

 

A court has ordered that the teenager, named as Paweł G, be held in pre-trial detention for three months.

The case is part of an ongoing investigation by Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) looking into individuals active in online neo-Nazi and extremist circles.

On 18 September, ABW reported the detention of two minors who were active in groups bringing together people linked to such ideologies.

At the time, officials stressed that the investigation was ongoing, with officers analysing the detainees' contacts and checking whether other individuals may have been involved.

This led investigators to Paweł G.

Officers from ABW in Katowice then detained him and searched his home, securing electronic devices and data carriers that were then subjected to detailed analysis.

According to ABW's findings, Paweł G., like the minors detained earlier, was active on the Telegram and Discord platforms, where groups linked to neo-Nazi and extremist communities operated.

He took part in discussions about previous terrorist attacks and their perpetrators. In some exchanges, participants also raised the possibility of carrying out further attacks.

Members of these groups examined, among other things, the methods used by those responsible for earlier attacks and treated them as a potential source of inspiration.

ABW further established that Paweł G. is believed to have belonged to the Atomwaffen Polska group and to have co-created the Bierut Soldier ZNB group. Both contained content and symbols referring to neo-Nazism, along with discussions of violence and terrorist activity.

Alleged attack plans

The most serious of the charges brought against Paweł G. concerns the preparation of a terrorist attack.

Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said Paweł G. had planned "a mass terrorist attack," including on a school and a mosque.

"There is no and will be no leniency for fascism, hatred and the planning of bloody attacks in Poland," the minister wrote on X.

"Anyone who raises a hand against the security of Poles will face the full severity of the law. Security is not an area for compromise. It is the foundation of our community," Żurek added.

Prosecutors are also examining information about planned purchases of weapons and military equipment, as well as the collection of materials linked to the activities of terrorist organisations.

The two remaining charges relate to participation in an organised criminal group. According to investigators, the group was involved in activities including preparing offences of a terrorist nature, promoting Nazism and fascism, and inciting hatred.

The likelihood that the suspect committed the offences with which he is charged is said to be supported by the evidence gathered during the investigation.

Particular weight is attached to the results of the search of his home and the analysis of his phones and other seized data carriers.

During the search, officers reportedly found, among other items, knives, a bayonet for an AKM-type rifle, as well as books, patches and other materials bearing fascist and Nazi symbols.

Analysis of the data stored on the seized devices is also said to have revealed correspondence about the planning of mass attacks, including a potential attack on a school and a mosque.

The conversations reportedly covered the surveillance of potential targets, methods of carrying out attacks and issues related to obtaining weapons, ammunition and military equipment. Messages were also said to contain information on the use of grenades and Molotov cocktails.

Paweł G was questioned as a suspect. He refused to make a statement.

World.title: New rotation of US troops bound for Lithuania, Lithuanian president says
World.content:
Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda announced on Tuesday that a new group of American troops was heading to Lithuania.

 

"I have just received confirmation that the new rotation of U.S. troops is already on its way," Nausėda wrote in a post on social media, while also thanking the Trump administration for the decision.

"The U.S. military presence in Lithuania is an indispensable part of our deterrence and collective defence," he said, adding that the move was "important not only for Lithuania, but also for the security of the entire region."

It comes despite repeated threats from US President Donald Trump to reduce the US' military presence in Europe, as he increasingly shifts his focus to the Middle East and Latin America.

Lithuanian media reported in June that around 1,000 US troops had begun withdrawing from the Baltic state as their deployment came to an end.

Presidential adviser Deividas Matulionis told Lithuania's LRT Radio on Tuesday that the number of new US soldiers arriving in the country would not be lower than the last deployment.

Kęstutis Budrys, Lithuania's Foreign Minister, has hailed the move, saying the "decision on continued U.S. military presence in Lithuania is a powerful signal of Allied unity and resolve."

"Lithuania stands proud as committed Ally, leading by example with 5% defence spending, strengthening national capabilities, and providing the best training conditions for Allied forces," he wrote on X.

NATO's eastern flank

Lithuania sits in a crucial spot on NATO's eastern flank, bordering Russia's Kaliningrad region to the southwest as well as Russian ally Belarus to the east and south.

Its strategic location has seen the country, along with its Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia, increasingly impacted by Moscow's war in Ukraine, including a growing number of drone and airspace incidents in recent months.

Speaking to Euronews in May following a drone incursion over Vilnius, Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas warned that the Baltics must be prepared for further such threats.

"This is the new reality of what the Baltic states face,” he told the Europe Today news programme.

“We need to adapt because the possibility of repeated similar scenarios is very high," he added.

World.title: Military aircraft crashes near US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany
World.content:
The F-16 pilot was able to safely eject from the plane and was taken to receive medical care. The incident occurred near Spangdahlem Air Base in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.

A fighter jet crashed near the US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany, on Tuesday.

The plane crash occurred at approximately 2:30 p.m. local time (12:30 UTC). The cause of the incident is currently under investigation.

The US military confirmed that the plane was an F-16 Fighting Falcon assigned to the 52nd Fighter Wing and that its pilot was able to safely eject from the aircraft.

"The pilot ejected safely and is receiving medical care," the base said in a statement.

At least one person was injured, authorities said Image: Harald Tittel/dpa/picture alliance

Local authorities in the remote Eifel region also confirmed that one person had been injured.

"Following a plane crash in the vicinity of US Air Base Spangdahlem, fire and emergency response teams from the Eifel District of Bitburg-Prüm were dispatched to the scene," the district said on its website.

"No comments can be made on the further details of the event from the side of the Eifel district at this time."

A NATO operations center

Spangdahlem Air Base is a NATO operations center that was built in the early 1950s. The US Air Force's 52nd Fighter Wing is garrisoned there. The base is home to an F-16 fighter jet squadron comprising around 20 aircraft.

It is located north of the city of Trier in Rhineland-Palatinate, not far west of the border to Luxembourg.

The facility at Spangdahlem is considered one of the most important airfields for the US military in Germany, alongside Ramstein base, outside the city of Kaiserslautern.

Some 5,000 US military and civilian personnel-plus dependents are stationed at Spangdahlem, with around 700 to 800 Germans also employed at the facility.

World.title: US-China AI race: Does Trump want to regulate AI by forming a new task force and a special envoy for artificial intelligence in the US?
World.content:
Do Trump's task force and a special envoy for artificial intelligence in the US indicate a move toward regulating this disputed technology, particularly vis-a-vis China?

Developers warning against their own technologies and a government unwilling to take action — that was the situation in the first half of September amid concerns in the US that AI models were becoming too powerful.

Several developers and decision-makers from major AI companies had also called for slowing down the development of the technology.

In response, US President Donald Trump posted one of his typical all-caps tweets on his social media platform Truth Social: "AI taking over the World, destroying Humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX." Trump also asked "Concerning AI, when, in the History of Business, did anyone see the Leaders of an Industry call for Regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy?"

Against this backdrop, it comes as something of a surprise that Trump announced over the weekend — following yet another tirade about various alleged Democratic scams — that he would establish an "AI Force" and appoint a special envoy to address the issue.

What exactly did Trump say?

In his post, Trump promised that he would by no means slow down the industry's growth. "However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System," he wrote. "To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI 'Czar' — Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!" he added.

Trump left open exactly what the individual's duties and powers would be and what resources would be allocated to the position.

Trump's announcement could be an attempt to undermine an initiative by California's Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom. The previous day, Newsom had announced plans to establish a commission to regulate Silicon Valley-based tech companies.

Among other things, Newsom wants to require these companies to build an emergency shut-off switch into their programs, which would allow humans to stop AI agents that have spun out of control. Several states, including some led by Republicans, are pushing for regulation.

US fear of China's dominance

The current "AI race" between the US and China is often compared to the space race between the US and the former Soviet Union in the 1960s. Several US companies are currently considered industry leaders. To ensure this remains the case, Trump intends to continue giving them free rein.

However, this is not just about economic interests. There is concern that Chinese dominance in artificial intelligence could also lead to Beijing's rise as the sole superpower.

In a widely discussed essay , Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, not only warned of the consequences of continued unchecked AI development; he also outlined the potential consequences of the AI competition between the US and China.

"If we greatly restrain our AI capabilities in the belief that China will do the same, and then China defects, AI could be so powerful that such a defection could lead to their geopolitical dominance. Therefore any agreement must either have ironclad verifiability, or must be limited enough that defection would not be militarily existential," Amodei wrote.

Tech leaders call for transparency and an emergency switch off for robots and AI technologies Image: Tingshu Wang/REUTERS

Does China regulate AI?

In China, technological developments have traditionally been much more closely tied to governmental objectives. As early as 2017, the State Council of China issued a development plan for a new generation of artificial intelligence.

Another strategy paper sets out milestones through which China aims to achieve global dominance in the field of AI by 2030. The regulations are primarily enforced by the Chinese Cyberspace Administration (CAC), which also issues licenses.

Regulation in China ensures that AI models do not run counter to official political doctrine. For example, the Chinese AI chatbot DeepSeek consistently provides answers loyal to the regime when asked politically sensitive questions — such as those regarding Taiwan, the Tiananmen Square massacre, or the oppression of the Uyghurs — as DW previously documented.

The underlying logic of Chinese regulation is thus based on the question: How does an AI system align with state objectives? This represents a clear distinction from the risk-based regulation envisaged, for example, by the European AI Act and now being called for in the US.

Could the US and China share information on AI technology as discussed between US Minister of Finance Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng? Image: Bai Xueqi/Xinhua/dpa/picture alliance

Is an AI agreement between the US and China imminent?

On Thursday, Trump will host Chinese President Xi Jinping at a state dinner at the White House. The topic of AI is likely to be very high on the agenda.

The US already proposed establishing a mechanism for exchanging information about serious risks posed by AI. The proposal was discussed at a meeting between Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday in New York.

"We think that, just like with any cross-border activity, that moving from opaque to more transparency between the number one and the number two AI powers in the world is very important," Bessent said.

Whether they actually decide to act on this will likely be left up to the two presidents. After all, for them, potential transparency obligations regarding AI are by no means the only point of contention in the negotiations.

For years, trade restrictions on high-performance AI chips and rare earth elements have been a recurring issue and the extension of a basic trade agreement is also on the agenda.

Whether mutual trust is strong enough to lead to reciprocal concessions on AI will likely only become clear at the meeting.

This article was originally published in German.

World.title: Young Berliners vote overwhelmingly for socialist Left  Party
World.content:
Berlin's young voters overwhelmingly supported the victorious socialist Left Party. Are the young more radical? Or are the election results just a reflection of current German politics?

The emphatic victory for the Left Party in last Sunday's state election in Berlin may not have been quite so emphatic if it hadn't been for a significant new rule: This was the first state election in the German capital's history where the voting age had been lowered from 18 to 16.

The actual change was relatively small: It only added around 55,000 voters to the city's electorate of 2.5 million, but it was massively significant to young people themselves: "Of course we talk a lot about politics at school or among our friends," 17-year-old Cecilia told DW's Franziska Wüst on the street outside her school in Berlin on Monday. "We're all very politically engaged; we go to a lot of demos."

Young socialists

That spirit of protest appears to have been reflected in young Berliners' voting habits. While the official exit poll statistics from infratest-dimap don't isolate under-18s, the age-group breakdowns suggest that the Left Party's voters (some 1 in 4 of Berlin voters) skew young. Some 43% of 16-24-year-olds voted for the socialist party — a huge 25-point leap on the last state election in 2023.

That makes sense to 17-year-old Liska, who voted for the socialists: "The Left Party did appeal to me, especially because of the social issues — getting prices down, making rents more affordable." Rents in Berlin are indeed rising at a massive pace — by some 7% in the last two years alone — and first-time tenants are likely to be the hardest hit. Polls also showed that by far the biggest proportion of Berlin voters — 37% — thought that the Left Party was the most likely to create affordable housing.

Cecilia also agreed that rents, as well as the conservative Berlin government's plans to cut education budgets, were the overwhelming concerns among her friends. "We're all getting to an age where we'd kind of like to move out, which in Berlin is almost impossible," she said. "Otherwise, of course it's issues like school, education, so it doesn't get cut everywhere."

Young radicals?

All those answers make a lot of sense to Kathrin Fehse of the German Children's and Youth Foundation (DKJS) , which represents the interests of Germany's young people. "It's all the issues that affect them personally," she told DW. "And for that they need to be taken seriously and asked. And the Left Party was one of the parties that mobilized a lot of non-voters, not just young voters — they're people that politicians were not addressing before."

Throughout the campaign, the Left Party had been portrayed as dangerous radicals by the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), the party of the incumbent mayor, Kai Wegner — regardless of how true this is or isn't, it did not appear to scare off young voters.

Some argue that young people are more likely to vote for the radical ends of the political spectrum. Cecilia can see that point: "I think that it's generally true that young people are always a lot more extreme than the older generations, and I do see that too, that it's always very extreme opinions," she said.

But there's also evidence that this is something of a stereotype: infratest-dimap statistics show that the biggest age group for the Left Party were the 25-34-year-olds (some 49% of the vote), while the biggest age group for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the Berlin election were 60-69-year-olds (23%). By comparison, only 12% of 16-24-year-old Berlin voters opted for the AfD.

What do young people want?

Gefjon Off, a political scientist who has researched the voting habits of younger generations, said that while it might be generally the case that younger people have more "radical" opinions than older people, the statistical evidence shows that middle-aged men vote for the AfD more than young men. People's age, in other words, "doesn't mean that they are more likely to vote for anti-democratic parties," she said.

German state elections reveal increasingly polarized country To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What characterizes young voters is not so much radical views, argued Off, but their looser affiliation to any particular party: "In the federal election in 2021, for example, climate protection was a huge issue, and a lot of young people voted for the Greens as the climate was their issue," she told DW. "In this election, affordable housing was a huge issue for the Left Party. That means young people vote more according to issues, and [find it ]easier to move from one party to another."

Off also thinks that young people are less scared off by the stigmatization around the Left Party that still hangs round older generations who associate it with the communist dictatorship of East Germany.

Fehse said that in the DKJS' own study on young people's opinions, named VoiceUp, was that "young people want solidarity, participation, positive prospects for their future, and at the same time they experience these things much too seldom."

She concluded that "at the end of the day, those experiences create the social context in which their political decisions are made."

Edited by: Rina Goldenberg

World.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
World.content:
Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.

For most, Los Angeles conjures images of a city of beaches, palm trees, and movie stars. Few realize LA County is also one of the largest oil-producing regions in the United States.

Oil wells are strewn everywhere across Los Angeles. Including on Pico Boulevard, next to the affluent neighborhood of Beverly Hills, where two fake buildings house and hide active oil wells. From the street, it's nearly impossible to tell what is inside.

Artificial islands off the coast of Long Beach disguise further drilling sites. And the disguise is so good that tourists who assume they are hotels often ask the city how they can book a night's stay there.

Other sites, such as the Inglewood Oil Field, are out in the open. The largest urban oil field in the US, it is right next to Kenneth Hahn State Park, where there is a fishing pond, hiking trails, and playgrounds. The pumpjacks are visible from inside the park.

Elsewhere there are yet more wells that have been built over, making them invisible to unknowing residents who pass them every day. A map created by CalGem, the state agency that manages oil and gas, shows them beneath neighborhoods, schools, and playgrounds.

An aerial view shows how far the Inglewood Oil Field, the largest urban oil field in the US, stretches into the surrounding Los Angeles landscape Image: Nils Hünerfürst/DW

And that is a big issue, as they are potential sources of pollution linked to respiratory disease, cancer, cardiovascular problems, reproductive harm, and other serious health issues.

For people living near oil wells, one of the most immediate concerns is air quality. Oil wells can release a range of pollutants, including volatile organic compounds such as benzene, as well as hydrogen sulfide and methane. Research has found that people living near oil and gas operations may experience reduced lung function and elevated rates of respiratory illness.

Residents who do live close to oil fields often describe odors and report physical impacts including headaches, nausea, eye irritation, coughing and breathing difficulties.

Community advocates in LA say such symptoms have impacted generations of families living close to oil and gas drilling infrastructure. Regina Martin, who grew up near the Inglewood Oil Field, recalls days when pollution was visibly present in the air.

Pumpjacks at the Inglewood Oil Field, the largest urban oil field in the US, are clearly visible from Kenneth Hahn State Park next door Image: Nils Hünerfürst/DW

"We used to be able to see the air that we were breathing," she says, adding that it was so bad that playing outside was not possible. "We had to stay in for recess. I used to deal with the nosebleeds, the headaches, the upset stomach, and the red eyes.”

Though the air has become clearer since Martin was a child, the oil field is still operational. She canvases with Black Women for Wellness to talk about issues affecting LA residents and says many local families do not know about the health impacts of living near oil extraction. She herself wasn't aware until she started doing community advocacy work.

"I always felt that everybody lived near an oil field,” she says. "So it was just really, really normalized for me.”

Impacts of proximity to drilling beyond breathing problems

Studies have linked proximity to oil and gas extraction with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, adverse birth outcomes, certain cancers, as well as reproductive health complications. Some studies have also explored associations between exposure to oil field pollutants and autoimmune conditions.

For Rosalinda Morales and Brenda Valdivia, the connection between oil drilling and health issues is all too familiar. The two women grew up in Vista Hermosa, a neighborhood scattered with oil wells.

Some, as Morales explains, are located close to schools and early childhood education centers. "To the right of us there's another school," she says.

"And down the block is a county preschool,” adds Valdivia.

This building on Pico Boulevard, near Beverly Hills, looks ordinary from the street — but it hides an active oil-drilling operation inside Image: Nils Hünerfürst/DW

The two are standing on the sidewalk next to a non-descript fence, which is impossible to see through or over from street level. But the smell is a giveaway. And behind the fence is a tank for storing oil as well as moving pumpjacks.

"This is mild today," Morales says, adding that the smell gets very strong. "You know, this is what we've grown up with."

While she struggles with respiratory problems, Valdivia has lupus, an autoimmune disease that contributed to multiple strokes.

Although proving that any individual illness was directly caused by nearby drilling is difficult, both women believe years of exposure to pollution from oil extraction played a role.

Inequality around the wells that are plugged

The health burden of urban oil extraction is not spread evenly across Los Angeles. Many of the city's most heavily drilled areas are predominantly Black and Latino neighborhoods, in South and East LA. In West LA, the neighborhoods close to the ocean, most of the oil wells have been plugged and sealed for decades.

Tianna Wakeman, who also does canvassing work with Regina Martin, argues that these communities have historically been forced to live with environmental hazards that wealthier neighborhoods were able to remove.

"There are protections that communities in South Los Angeles have been fighting for for decades, that whiter wealthy communities in West LA, have already received," she says, adding that there is very clear environmental racism at play.

"Black and brown people saying, I want clean air, I want clean water, I want clean soil for my kids to play in, is not received in the same way as when white, wealthy folks say the same thing."

Regina Martin (left) and Tianna Wakeman canvas with Black Women for Wellness to raise awareness of the health impacts of living near LA's oil fields Image: Nils Hünerfürst/DW

One frequently cited example is how residents successfully pushed for the closure and plugging of oil wells located on the grounds of one of LA's most affluent schools, Beverly Hills High. Morales and Valdivia, meanwhile, say they have been trying to find out the owner of oil wells in their neighborhood for years. So far, with no luck.

Morales, Valdivia, and others are advocating for the closure of LA's urban oil fields, and phasing out of drilling entirely in LA County.

Los Angeles is currently debating both banning oil extraction and how to manage thousands of aging wells.



Edited by: Tamsin Walker

World.title: After floods, Nepal minister demands 'climate justice'
World.content:
With Nepal still reeling from the devastating floods in August, Kathmandu is calling for climate justice and seeking compensation from the UN-backed Loss and Damage Fund, Environment Minister Geeta Chaudhary told DW.

Nepal is seeking $20 million (just under €17.5 million) from the international Loss and Damage Fund, the UN-backed mechanism designed to support countries suffering irreversible climate-related losses, Environment Minister Geeta Chaudhary said in an exclusive DW interview.

The move comes after floods and landslides killed more than 1,400 people in August and left thousands missing.

"We have already issued the official letter for the fund for the loss and damage," Chaudhary told DW. "Most of the countries have sent us a positive response."

The flash flooding caused widespread destruction across large swathes of Nepal, damaging homes, agricultural land and infrastructure. Rescue and recovery efforts are still ongoing in several areas, while authorities continue to assess the full scale of the losses.

In the Himalayan nation, the tragedy has become a powerful symbol of what developing countries describe as the unfair climate burden of contributing little to global emissions while facing disproportionate consequences.

'Sympathy alone will not work for us'

Talking to DW, Chaudhary repeatedly framed Nepal's response through the lens of climate justice, a concept that has become increasingly prominent in global climate negotiations.

"Sympathy alone will not work for us," she said. "We don't need sympathy. We need justice. It's high time. If you're not able to give us justice, then we also don't need the words."

"Those countries who are emitting the most and are able to contribute the funds, they need to pay for the climatic disasters like what we are facing," she said.

Nepal contributes roughly 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Its geography, however, makes it extremely vulnerable to climate-related risks. Rising temperatures in the Himalayas have accelerated glacial retreat and increased concerns about glacial lake outburst floods, landslides and extreme weather events across the region.

Alps warming fast: Europe's water lifeline is running dry To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In the wake of the most recent disaster, the government has intensified calls for more adaptation financing, direct access to climate funds and stronger international commitments to fight consequences of climate change.

'The world is watching'

Chaudhary pointed to melting glaciers, warming temperatures and changes in mountain environments as factors behind the deadly floods.

"Our evidence is showing that this catastrophic event is because of climate change," Chaudhary said.

While many scientists agree that climate change increases the likelihood and severity of such events, establishing a causal relationship between a specific disaster and global warming typically requires detailed attribution studies.

Researchers are more likely to point to a combination of factors, including glacier and permafrost degradation, extreme weather conditions and geological vulnerabilities.

The Nepali government, however, insists that the connection is clear.

"We are the real example and the world is watching us," Chaudhary told DW.

Building support ahead of COP31

The minister's comments come as Nepal seeks to build momentum for COP31, the UN's annual climate conference set to be held in Turkey this November.

When asked about her government's plans for the conference, Chaudhary said "Nepal will no longer negotiate on vague promises or slow-moving traditional and development aid."

According to the minister, Nepal intends to push for greater recognition of the specific challenges facing mountainous countries, arguing that global climate discussions often overlook the risks confronting Himalayan regions.

"Mountain issues need to be addressed," she said. "The world needs to see us, that we are victimized countries. We are paying the price."

Chaudhary also pointed out that Nepal received strong backing from fellow vulnerable nations at the recent gathering of Least Developed Countries (LDCs) in Timor-Leste.

"All the LDCs stood with us," she said. "They are very concerned."

The government plans to bring climate concerns to the UN General Assembly, highlighting the recent disaster and calling for concrete support from the international community.

Nepal to improve its early warning systems

The scale of the disaster has also prompted scrutiny inside Nepal, particularly of the country's warning systems and its disaster response.

Residents in some affected areas have complained that warnings came too late or did not adequately reflect the scale of the danger.

After Nepal floods, survivors return to ruins of their homes To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Chaudhary defended the government's response but conceded that existing systems were overwhelmed by the sheer scale of the event.

"We had sent them messages and information," she said. "But the situation was beyond imagination."

She acknowledged that Nepal's early warning systems must improve and said authorities are now reviewing and strengthening existing monitoring mechanisms.

"Our hydrology and meteorology departments are working on that," she said.

The floods also highlighted the importance of cooperation between Nepal and its neighbors, particularly China, in monitoring river systems and glacial hazards that cut through national borders.

"We are working closely," Chaudhary said, adding that technical teams from both countries are sharing information and examining future risks.

Himalayan catastrophe as a warning for the world

For Chaudhary, the disaster is not only a national tragedy but a warning about the future.

"Our snow is melting, our lakes are in danger," the minister said.

She warned that, unless global warming is limited in line with the Paris climate agreement of 2015, vulnerable countries could face increasingly severe disasters.

Asked whether the world is acting fast enough, the minister responded: "I don't think so."

Edited by: Darko Janjevic

World.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
World.content:
Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics but there are doubts about the next step, and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.

The form of mixed martial arts (MMA) making its debut at the Asian Games looks almost completely distinct from the visceral brawls of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), which have come to define combat sports in recent years.

In order to get a version of the sport into the Games, currently taking place in Nagoya in Japan, adaptations had to be made. The fights take place without the familiar cage, on an open mat and with small boxing-style gloves. While MMA's presence in the Asian Games is significant in itself, it's also a clear effort to get close to Olympic recognition.

"We think without the cage we will have a better alignment with the Olympic values and hopefully recognition from the IOC," Galastein Tan, the director general of Federation of International Mixed Martial Arts (FIMMA), told press agency AP . "It takes time to change a perception. We hope to be able to share that there is a new form of MMA, and this form is more aligned with the Olympics."

FIMMA is not the only body purporting to represent the sport, with the International Mixed Martial Arts (IMMAF) also staking a claim. But Tan, a Chinese billionaire property mogul, is a vice president of the Olympic Council of Asia. This could potentially open doors in a movement which has so far kept MMA at arm's length, with violence levels among its concerns. DW contacted both FIMMA and the IMMAF for comment but received no response.

UFC has outstripped MMA

In the past the UFC, a lucrative MMA-based competition, has also pushed for Olympic recognition. But the growth of that arm of the sport, highlighted by it staging an event on the South Lawn of the White House at the 250th anniversary celebrations of US independence earlier this year, has meant that the aims of a sport that was marginal two decades ago have shifted according to Karim Zidan.

UFC hosted matches at the White House earlier this year Image: Kent Nishimura/AP Photo/picture alliance

"I don't necessarily think it's that important to MMA. The sport has already found its success on a professional level, which is what the fan base demanded of it," said Zidan, who has written an upcoming book 'The Ultimate Strongmen: MMA and the Rise of the New Authoritarian Right' on the subject.

"The UFC is bigger than it's ever been in terms of the amount of money it's making" added Zidan. "The UFC's growth mainstreamed MMA as a sport, but it also cannibalized it. So there's really not much remaining. Olympic recognition might seem like a badge of honor, but it doesn't amount to much else."

With events for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles already set, the earliest MMA could make its bow would be 2032 in Brisbane. But the IOC told AP that "mixed martial arts does not meet ... eligibility criteria" at this point. DW has sought clarification from the IOC on this.

Does MMA have enough appeal for Olympics?

Tan appears to be trying to find a way to change that, citing the sport's popularity. "MMA is popular globally, able to engage fans at a gut level and attract fans at a youth level," he said.

But Zidan argues that its popularity is through the UFC, rather than any grassroots popularity.

"There isn't much of an MMA ecosystem outside of the UFC for me to say there's an entirely different worldview existing in the sport that's demanding this. There are pockets within the sport that enjoy amateur MMA and are operating within it, but I don't think it's a significant part of the fan base at all," Zidan said.

"I'm not particularly convinced that this is a turning point or a significant moment for mixed martial arts, honestly. I think the sport has suffered tremendously under the burden and the weight of the UFC over the past decade."

Senegal gears up for Youth Olympic Games To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

UFC's links with the Trump administration are deep and clear, with UFC president Dana White also speaking at the Republican convention in 2024.

But Zidan also pointed to the IMMAF's link up with Brave Combat Federation, a Bahraini organization headed by Khalid bin Hamad Al Khalifa, a son of King of Bahrain, Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. A 2025 Amnesty International Report said Bahrain continued to "to suppress the rights to freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly, including through arbitrary detention and prosecutions."

Authoritarian links remain for MMA

Such links with authoritarian governments have become, Zidan added, fairly commonplace in the sport.

"They've already had associations with authoritarian regimes in the past and it's very likely that relationship will build. If this [the Asian Games and potential Olympic acceptance] means that we will now have more amateur MMA events being hosted around the world in youth championships, it's very likely that authoritarian regimes will jump on that."

The challenge for FIMMA, who appear to want to take MMA in the Olympic direction and away from UFC and its associations, is to make the sport more "normal" and less about spectacle, FIMMA's vice president Alex Engelhardt told AP.

"It's very challenging in the sense that the whole mindset in the sport is so focused on promotions," he said.

Even if that can change, and sport's debut at the Asian Games adds some legitimacy, the Olympics still seem some way off.

World.title: Iran war spreads through region as Trump seeks way out
World.content:
Washington, Tehran and the Gulf states continue to pursue different objectives while searching for a way to end the Iran war.

Nearly seven months into the Iran war, negotiations between Washington and Tehran have led nowhere, and the conflict has spread from the Strait of Hormuz to another strategically important shipping route.

In September, Iran-backed Houthi militia in Yemen took over critical positions on the Yemeni coast and are threatening Red Sea trade routes while launching attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia. This compounds a global energy crunch brought on by the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

Earlier in September, Saudi officials blamed Iran-backed militias in Iraq for blowing up the critical East-West oil pipeline.

According to The New York Times, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called US President Donald Trump on Sunday to once again urge him to intervene and stop the Houthi's rapid advance.

Trump is reported to have considered airstrikes against the Houthis at one point, but later abandoned the plans. This weekend, Fox News reported that Trump said the Houthi rebels had agreed not to attack US targets. The US news outlet Axios also reported that Trump had rejected a Saudi request for strikes against the Houthis the previous week.

Why can't Saudi Arabia stop the Houthis? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Trump seeks a way out

Against the backdrop of record high gasoline and diesel prices coming down hard on voters ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, US President Donald Trump is under pressure to show results in the Iran war.

"President Trump wants to end the Iran war from a position that allows him to claim that Iran's nuclear and military capabilities have been significantly weakened, freedom of navigation has been restored, and Tehran has been forced back to the negotiating table," Iran expert Fatemeh Aman told DW.

Aman, who has worked with organizations including the Middle East Institute, the Atlantic Council, RFE/RL and Voice of America, however, added that a coherent strategy for achieving these objectives remains difficult to discern.

The US has imposed high military and economic costs on Iran and appears to have made progress in weakening the country's military capabilities. But Tehran has not capitulated and there is no lasting ceasefire agreement.

Trump is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week. China is by far the largest buyer of Iranian oil and an important political partner of Tehran. The US president is likely to bring up China's economic and financial ties with Iran and hope that Beijing will use its influence over Tehran — particularly when it comes to the security of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

At the same time, Trump has signaled that he is open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is traveling to New York for the United Nations General Assembly. Senior representatives from the Gulf states are also expected in the US over the coming days.

According to Axios, Trump plans to discuss the Iran war with representatives of several Gulf states on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

Houthi gains in Yemen threaten key Red Sea shipping route To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Gulf nations want regional stability

There is still no common position emerging between Iran and its Arab neighbors in the Gulf. A planned meeting involving Iran, the Gulf states and Iraq was canceled last week. The cancellation may be linked to the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

"At first glance, there appears to be little common ground between Iran and the Gulf states," Farzan Sabet, a Middle East expert at the Geneva Graduate Institute, told DW. "But behind the scenes, there is at least a shared interest in preventing further military escalation."

The Gulf states recognize that they would be unlikely to prevail in a direct military confrontation with Iran, and generally favor de-escalation and a pragmatic easing of tensions with Tehran.

An agreement, however, is not currently in sight. In particular, Iran's demands for greater control over the Strait of Hormuz go too far from the perspective of the Gulf states.

The war in Yemen further limits the scope for rapprochement. Saudi Arabia, for example, is unlikely to make concessions while it remains under pressure from the Iran-aligned Houthis.

Is Iran set to become an economic outcast? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Iran's two-track strategy

A permanently hostile, US-backed coalition of Gulf states would be strategically costly for Tehran, Aman said.

She added Iran could pursue a two-track strategy: This would involve resisting a US-led regional containment architecture, while simultaneously offering the Gulf states an alternative model of regional security based on accommodation and dialogue.

"After all, the Gulf states are not only Iran's rivals but also its neighbors — and neither side can change that geographic reality," Aman said.

According to Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei, Tehran is demanding that the US end the fighting on all fronts.

Tehran is also calling for the release of billions in frozen Iranian assets and the lifting of the naval blockade in the strait. Talks with Qatar and Oman are reportedly continuing. The Iranian regime is now waiting for a response from Trump. Whether these diplomatic signals can translate into a broader political process remains uncertain.

For now, the main obstacle is that Washington, Tehran and the Gulf states continue to pursue very different roadmaps for ending the months-long conflict.

This article was translated from German.

World.title: Turkey: Several pupils injured in shooting outside school
World.content:
The shooter, a pupil, allegedly took a rifle and shot indiscriminately at his schoolmates in front of their high school. Turkey was shocked by two back-to-back school shootings earlier this year.

A shooting near a high school in Turkey's Manisa province resulted in at least 11 injured pupils, two of whom were in critical condition on Tuesday, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said.

The shooter, a pupil at the school, was arrested together with both of his parents and his grandfather.

What do we know about the shooting incident?

The suspect is said to have taken the weapon from his grandparents' house, with his grandfather believed to have had a licence for it.

Local authorities said the attack took place at the Inci Uzmez Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School in the Turgutlu district at about 08:00am local time (07:00 CET).

The motive for the shooting is also under investigation. Some reports suggest the student had suffered from bullying.

Two back-to-back school shootings in April left around 10 killed and dozens more injured Image: Ensar Ozdemir/REUTERS

"When the ​security of our children is the issue, it is not possible for any ​negligence, any irresponsibility to be overlooked," the minister posted on his X account.

"The ‌circumstances under which the child obtained the gun used in the attack, the conditions of the weapon's storage, the parents' obligations regarding care ‌and supervision, and allegations of bullying prior to the incident ‌are ​being investigated thoroughly and from multiple angles," Gurlek added.

Footage posted online showed a male carrying a rifle near the school, while police told families to stay away from the area.

Gun control tightened after school shootings

School shootings are rare in Turkey, but this year alone saw two back-to-back shootings that shocked the nation.

Two school shootings that took place in April resulted in the tightening of gun controls and the increase of security measures at educational facilities as the academic year started last week.

Several students and their teacher were killed in one of the attacks, with the other resulting in 16 people being injured.

According to Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci, 31,000 school supervisors and police officers on duty were assigned to school seen as being at risk, as per a new measure introduced only on Monday.

President Recep Tayyip Erdogan responded to the latest shooting attack by promising even tighter gun controls.

"When we look at similar attacks around the world, especially in the United States, we see one of the perpetrators' aims is to terrorise society," the Turkish leader said.

World.title: Sánchez y Delcy Rodríguez se ven en la ONU y acuerdan mantener el contacto sobre el futuro de Venezuela
World.content:
La presidenta de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, se ha acercado durante la asamblea general de la ONU en Nueva York a saludar al presidente del Gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez. El encuentro ha sido breve, medio minuto, pero según fuentes de la delegación española ha servido para que la mujer que sustituyó a Nicolás Maduro cuando fue secuestrado por el ejército de EE UU le pidiera al líder español abrir un cauce para seguir hablando sobre la situación en Venezuela y su futuro político, presumiblemente con alguna reunión oficial de ambos en el futuro. Según esas fuentes, el presidente español le ha contestado que por supuesto se mantiene abierto ese canal porque “España está comprometida con el futuro de la región”. Otras fuentes del Ejecutivo señalan que fue Rodríguez la que más interés mostró, y arrancó la conversación con una petición para mantener el contacto. “España es muy importante para nosotros, tenemos que seguir hablando”, le dijo ella, según estas fuentes, a lo que el presidente contestó, “por supuesto, nosotros estamos para ayudar, para nosotros es muy importante apoyar a la región”. Pero no hubo decisiones, ni algún asunto pendiente clave por intereses de empresas españolas como Repsol ni nada muy concreto, simplemente una toma de contacto informal, insisten.

En las imágenes se aprecia claramente cómo Rodríguez se recorre toda la sala de la asamblea para ir expresamente a buscar a Sánchez, que corta una conversación telefónica para saludar y charlar brevemente con ella. La conversación se produce con Rodríguez de pie y Sánchez sentado. Ambos se despiden finalmente, emplazándose a una nueva conversación, y Rodríguez también charla muy brevemente con el ministro de Exteriores, José Manuel Albares, antes de volver a su asiento.

El encuentro no es pues casual, y parecía acordado previamente porque ella va a buscarlo expresamente y atraviesa toda la sala para hacerlo y él corta la conversación y deja el teléfono en cuanto ve que llega la presidenta. Distintas fuentes coinciden en que Rodríguez había mostrado interés por verse con Sánchez y la fórmula que se encontró fue esta, un saludo a iniciativa de ella. De momento no se ha concretado una reunión oficial en Nueva York o más adelante, pero Sánchez está intentando convencer a todos los líderes, incluida la venezolana, de que vayan a Madrid a la cumbre iberoamericana de noviembre, y ahí sí se podría concretar esa cita.

Sánchez había roto por completo la comunicación con Maduro, aunque en España se le acusaba de estar cerca de ese régimen, pero con Rodríguez sí ha mantenido ya una conversación cuando cayó Maduro, en enero, y otra más en junio para ofrecerle ayuda durante el devastador terremoto en Venezuela. Además hay gestiones discretas para que la presidenta acuda a la cumbre iberoamericana.

La Moncloa está interesada en mantener este contacto para tener influencia en el futuro de la región y proteger los intereses españoles. Rodríguez está ahora muy vinculada a la administración de Trump, con la que Sánchez está muy enfrentado, pero el Gobierno español insiste en que los vínculos con Caracas siguen siendo intensos y los cauces de todo tipo se mantienen. En La Moncloa minimizan la importancia de este encuentro en la ONU, y señalan que Sánchez se ve con muchos líderes de forma oficial, con contenido, como ha hecho con el británico Andy Burnham y otros como el de Panamá, y esto solo ha sido un saludo sin apenas fondo político. Pero simbólicamente la imagen es potente y es el primer encuentro entre el líder español y la máxima mandataria venezolana desde que se hizo con el poder.

En un primer momento, Sánchez fue uno de los líderes que más claramente mostraron su rechazo enérgico a la operación militar de Trump para sacar a Maduro del poder y de Venezuela. Entonces, la oposición española, incluido el PP, celebró la caída de Maduro y acusó a Sánchez de tener vínculos con él. La Moncloa reivindicaba entonces que el Gobierno había apoyado a la oposición venezolana, no había reconocido a Maduro como presidente tras las últimas elecciones, y había acogido tanto al candidato de la oposición como a más de 200.000 venezolanos huidos de su país hacia España.

Pero poco a poco se comprobó que Trump no iba a apoyar a la líder de la oposición, María Corina Machado, y prefería pactar con Rodríguez a cambio de dominar el país a través de ella y sobre todo sus enormes reservas petroleras. Desde entonces el debate en España ha cambiado y la oposición española ya no está tan contenta con la salida de Maduro porque el régimen continúa con Rodríguez pero ahora muy controlado por Washington, con Corina Machado fuera de juego.

En este contexto, Sánchez apuesta por mantener una relación con Rodríguez que ya no tenía con Maduro en ese intento de mantener una influencia en Venezuela ahora muy reducida porque es EEUU quien tiene el control de las decisiones más importantes del país, en especial las que tienen que ver con el petróleo, que interesan mucho a empresas españolas como Repsol.

World.title: Últimas noticias de la Asamblea General de la ONU, en directo | Trump amenaza con “aniquilar” Irán si no hay pacto, pero augura un acuerdo tras las elecciones de noviembre
World.content:
Lula: “Brasil no se mete en el patio trasero de nadie”

El presidente de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, el primer jefe de Estado en intervenir este martes ante la Asamblea General de la ONU, se ha erigido en el primer portavoz de los que defienden casi todo lo que los EE UU de Donald Trump y otras potencias atacan de manera sistemática, la arquitectura creada tras la Segunda Guerra Mundial para resolver conflictos y evitar guerras.

El brasileño ha criticado los ataques a la ONU, su falta de credibilidad y eficacia y ha demandado un regreso al multilateralismo ante un Consejo de Seguridad que mantiene “al resto del mundo rehén”.

Pegado a la actualidad, ha criticado el “genocidio de Netanyahu en Gaza”. Y, más cerca de casa, ha rechazado las interferencias de EE UU al sur del Río Bravo en un momento en que Brasil está a las puertas de unas elecciones cruciales y cunde el temor de que Washington interfiera.

“Brasil no se mete en el patio trasero de nadie, necesitamos socios con una agenda positiva, las diferencias ideológicas no deberían impedir la integración entre los vecinos”, ha dicho tras enfatizar que “los venezolanos deben decidir su propio destino”.

Lula viajó a la ONU a dos semanas de las elecciones generales brasileñas en las que busca la reelección, con su país sometido a una guerra arancelaria por EE UU y con la amenaza de que Washington imponga nuevas sanciones, que podrían influir en la campaña y los resultados.

Los servicios secretos, la ABIN, han elevado al “nivel crítico” el riesgo de interferencia estadounidense en los comicios del 4 de octubre.

El mandatario brasileño no tiene concertada una reunión con Trump, pero no se descarta un saludo informal en los pasillos, como el que hace justo un año les dio la oportunidad de conocerse en persona.

Aquel saludo en la sede de la ONU hace un año allanó el camino para reencauzar una de las peores crisis en la relación bilateral, desatada por las presiones para que Bolsonaro padre no fuera juzgado, y para que ambos mandatarios construyeran una relación personal que se ha plasmado en dos reuniones oficiales, la última en mayo en la Casa Blanca.

Pero eso no ha impedido que EE UU exhibiera su poder con una segunda tanda de aranceles contra Brasil.

Para esta décima intervención ante la ONU, Lula ha elegido su corbata de la suerte, con los colores de su patria. Su esposa, Janja da Silva, le ha acompañado vestida de nuevo con una chaqueta confeccionada con el bordado tradicional palestino.

World.title: La amenaza de un nuevo salto masivo este miércoles eleva a seis las alertas en Ceuta y Melilla desde la entrada de julio
World.content:
La amenaza de un posible nuevo intento de entrada masiva de migrantes irregulares este próximo miércoles en Ceuta y Melilla, verbalizada públicamente el pasado lunes por el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, será la sexta alerta de estas características a la que se enfrenten las fuerzas de seguridad desde que los pasados 30 y 31 de julio cerca de 80.000 personas cruzaran a nado desde Marruecos a la primera de las ciudades autónomas. Antes de esta última, que coincide con la celebración este día de elecciones legislativas en el país africano, también se dispararon las alarmas por la existencia en redes sociales y canales de mensajería de llamamientos multitudinarios para intentar cruzar la frontera los pasados 8, 9, 12 y 15 de agosto y 20 de septiembre, según detallan fuentes de Interior. Las tres primeras de estas alertas no habían trascendido públicamente hasta ahora y, de hecho, aquellos días finalmente no hubo movimientos significativos en la frontera.

De hecho, de todas ellas, la del 15 de agosto fue la que supuso mayor riesgo, con el intento de cientos de migrantes, en su mayoría subsaharianos, de llegar a la zona vallada y que fueron rechazados por las fuerzas de seguridad de Rabat con un dispositivo sin precedentes hasta la fecha. Para este miércoles, tanto Marruecos como España también han reforzado sus dispositivos en torno a la zona fronteriza. El pasado domingo ―coincidiendo con una de las alertas― ya eran visibles en el país magrebí estas medidas, con vallas metálicas que se internaban una decena de metros en el mar para impedir el paso de migrantes por la playa y las rocas, concertinas, controles policiales y patrullas de la Gendarmería en los desvíos de carretera que supusieron el despliegue de cerca de 3.000 efectivos, incluidos militares, según algunas fuentes.

En España, el refuerzo se empezará a notar en Ceuta entre este martes y el miércoles con el envío de cerca de 150 efectivos más a los ya desplegados. Así, la Guardia Civil ―que cuenta con 706 agentes de servicio, de los que 195 forman parte de los llegados tras el salto de julio― va a incrementar el número de servicios, para lo que suspenderá descansos y libranzas, según detallan fuentes de Interior. Además, desde esta próxima noche y hasta las cuatro de la tarde del miércoles, el instituto armado va a desplegar en frontera tres pelotones de los Grupos de Reserva y Seguridad (GRS, aproximadamente 60 efectivos) para apoyar la dotación habitual destinada en la zona. Esto supone 120 agentes durante las horas nocturnas y 90 en las diurnas, aunque las fuentes detallan que estas cifras se incrementarán “si la alerta se convirtiese en una amenaza real”. La Guardia Civil también duplicará el empleo de helicópteros y drones tanto de día como de noche.

Por su parte, la Policía Nacional tiene previsto enviar en las próximas horas dos nuevos grupos de la Unidad de Intervención Policial (UIP, los conocidos como antidisturbios), que representan 75 agentes, según las mismas fuentes. Uno de estos grupos debía dar relevo a otro desplegado desde hace días en la ciudad, pero Interior ha decidido que este segundo se mantenga al menos hasta la tarde antes de regresar a su base en previsión de que sea necesario incrementar la seguridad. El segundo grupo también llega de madrugada y, en principio, permanecerá en la ciudad únicamente hasta el jueves, según detallan fuentes sindicales.

Aumento de efectivos en Melilla

En Melilla, el envío de efectivos de refuerzo por parte de ambos cuerpos será menor. Así, la Guardia Civil ―que cuenta con 620 agentes en la ciudad autónoma, entre los 500 que conforman la plantilla y los 120 llegados en las últimas semanas― desplegará este miércoles ante la amenaza de un salto masivo un helicóptero “en servicio permanente” y sumará a la vigilancia de la frontera tres pelotones del GRS (unos 60 agentes), lo que representa duplicar el número de efectivos de esta unidad especializada en el control de masas.

Además, se sumará a las labores de prevención un buque de altura y se incrementará el número de miembros del Grupo Especial de Actividades Submarinas (GEAS), cuyos agentes tuvieron una labor destacada durante la entrada de julio en Ceuta en el auxilio de las personas que intentaban entrar a nado y la recuperación de los cuerpos de las 82 personas que murieron ahogadas en aguas españolas. Por su parte, la Policía Nacional, que envió a comienzos de agosto a la ciudad 60 efectivos de la UIP, no tiene previsto por ahora reforzar su plantilla en la ciudad autónoma.

World.title: Sanidad pide a la Abogacía del Estado que obligue a Madrid “con todas las medidas” a crear el registro de objetores al aborto
World.content:
El Ministerio de Sanidad ha requerido a la Abogacía del Estado a “llevar a cabo todas las medidas oportunas para obligar a Madrid” a poner en marcha el registro de médicos objetores de conciencia al aborto. Así lo ha anunciado este martes la ministra de Sanidad, Mónica García. “Hemos comprobado que, a 1 de septiembre, Madrid no ha avanzado más allá de los trámites iniciales de la creación del registro”, ha criticado.

Mónica García ha hecho estas declaraciones en la presentación de una nueva campaña que está centrada en dos ideas fundamentales: las mujeres deben poder decidir si abortar o no sin ninguna presión o estigma, y este proceso debe hacerse fundamentalmente en centros la sanidad pública.

“No hay una sola forma de vivir y de contar el aborto. No hay que demostrar sufrimiento para que la decisión merezca respeto. Hay mujeres que sienten alivio. Hay mujeres que sienten tristeza. Hay quienes tienen dudas y quienes lo tienen claro desde el principio. Una misma mujer puede atravesar emociones distintas. Y todas merecen ser escuchadas y atendidas con el mismo respeto. Y deben hacerlo en la sanidad pública”, ha afirmado García, que ha reprochado a Madrid que siga remitiendo prácticamente siempre a las mujeres que desean abortar a clínicas privadas concertadas.

La ministra ha querido dejar claro que “la campaña interpela también a quienes tienen la responsabilidad de garantizar este derecho dentro del sistema sanitario”. Sanidad censura que, según datos de 2024, “casi ocho de cada diez interrupciones voluntarias del embarazo se realizaron en centros privados”, un porcentaje que supera el 99% en la Comunidad de Madrid. “La sanidad pública debe estar preparada para atenderte cuando quieres ser madre, durante tu embarazo y tu parto, y también cuando decides interrumpir un embarazo”, ha defendido García.

En esta línea, la ministra también ha indicado que hay “otras dos comunidades” —Andalucía y Baleares— “que también van lentas en el proceso de crear el registro” de los objetores del aborto, aunque sin llegar al bloqueo del proceso de Madrid. “A ellos también les hemos advertido de que tener ese registro de objetores es una condición, primero, que la marca la ley y, segundo, que es una condición imprescindible para hacer coincidir los dos derechos el derecho a abortar en la comunidad [autónoma de residencia] con el derecho a la objeción de conciencia” de los profesionales sanitarios.

La ley obliga a las comunidades autónomas a tener un registro —siempre confidencial— de profesionales sanitarios objetores de conciencia. Aunque la presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, ha calificado este registro de “lista negra” ideológica, en realidad su función es meramente organizativa: permitir a los gestores de los hospitales públicos saber con qué plantilla cuentan en los servicios de Ginecología para garantizar que las mujeres puedan interrumpir el embarazo en hospitales de la sanidad pública.

La Comunidad de Madrid se ha opuesto frontalmente a la medida y aseguró inicialmente que no la elaboraría. Este bloqueo administrativo ha tenido un impacto asistencial. Los datos oficiales del Ministerio de Sanidad retratan que de las más de 18.000 interrupciones del embarazo practicadas en la región en 2024, menos del 1% (apenas un centenar) se llevan a cabo en hospitales de la red pública.

El Ministerio de Sanidad llevó a la Comunidad de Madrid a los tribunales el pasado mes de enero por su negativa a crear el registro y el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Madrid (TSJM) emitió en marzo un auto que obligó a la administración autonómica a poner en marcha la medida de forma inmediata. Madrid acabó finalmente publicando a principios de abril el proyecto de orden que regula la creación del registro, abriendo el periodo de trámite de audiencias y alegaciones públicas. Sanidad le reprocha ahora que no ha ido más allá.

World.title: Los hutíes prosiguen su avance en Yemen y acarician el control total del estrecho de Bab el Mandeb
World.content:
Tras la ofensiva relámpago que, en las últimas semanas, les ha llevado a conquistar la costa yemení del mar Rojo, los rebeldes hutíes avanzan ahora hacia las montañas Kahbub, un macizo en el suroeste de Yemen que separa la costa sur —en manos del Gobierno apoyado por Arabia Saudí— de las posesiones en el oeste del país de esta guerrilla aliada de Irán. Estas elevaciones permitirían a los hutíes asegurar sus recientes conquistas y amarrar definitivamente el control sobre la orilla septentrional del estrecho de Bab el Mandeb, crucial para el comercio entre Europa, África y Asia.

Medios locales y la cadena catarí Al Jazeera informan este martes de que los combates se están desarrollando en las provincias de Taiz y Lahij, en las estribaciones orientales y occidentales de las montañas Kahbub. “Las fuerzas gubernamentales permanecen a la defensiva tras haber perdido la zona de Bab el Mandeb, mientras que los hutíes buscan mantener el impulso de su avance, a pesar de estar expuestos a intensos ataques aéreos. Estas montañas resultarán decisivas para determinar si los hutíes logran consolidar sus recientes ganancias o si las fuerzas gubernamentales son capaces de defender las posiciones necesarias para lanzar una contraofensiva”, explica el analista Mohammed al Qadhi, citado por la agencia Reuters.

Al mismo tiempo, la toma de estas cordilleras les permitiría amenazar Adén, principal puerto del país y capital oficiosa del Gobierno internacionalmente reconocido de Yemen desde que los hutíes tomaron la capital oficial, Saná, en 2014.

Desde 2022, regía un alto el fuego mediado por Naciones Unidas en este país, dividido por la guerra civil y el más pobre del mundo árabe. Con todo, eso no había impedido que, en determinados periodos, los hutíes, un movimiento islamista de la rama zaidí del chiísmo –cuyo nombre oficial es Ansar Alá o “Partidarios de Dios”–, interviniesen en conflictos regionales: con el ataque de decenas de buques comerciales entre 2023 y 2024 en el mar Rojo en represalia por la masacre israelí contra los palestinos, y, este año, con el lanzamiento de misiles y drones a Israel en venganza por los bombardeos sobre su aliado Irán.

Sin embargo, en julio, fuerzas gubernamentales atacaron el aeropuerto de Saná cuando un avión con una delegación iraní se disponía a aterrizar, lo que hizo que los hutíes diesen por rota la tregua e iniciasen una ofensiva contra el resto de Yemen, así como contra Arabia Saudí, el principal apoyo del Gobierno yemení.

En septiembre, las fuerzas de Ansar Alá avanzaron rápidamente tomando el puerto de Moca y la isla de Mayun, emplazamientos estratégicos en el estrecho de Bab el Mandeb que permiten amenazar el tráfico entre el golfo de Adén y el mar Rojo, la ruta que —a través del canal de Suez— comunica el mar Mediterráneo con el océano Índico. Esta posibilidad de bloqueo, junto a las dificultades para transitar por el también crucial estrecho de Ormuz, ha lanzado los precios del crudo al entorno de los 100 dólares el barril.

Pese a su imagen de guerrilleros en chancletas, los hutíes cuentan con sistemas armamentísticos avanzados suministrados por Irán, desde misiles balísticos a drones. Además, en un informe de riesgos publicado el 11 de septiembre, Anthropic reconoció que “una célula del norte de Yemen” había utilizado su modelo de IA Claude para desarrollar un software destinado a guiar misiles, incluyendo proyectiles balísticos e hipersónicos. “Nuestras medidas de seguridad bloquearon muchas de sus solicitudes, pero no todas”, señaló la empresa tecnológica.

Civiles desplazados

Agencias de Naciones Unidas calculan que al menos 674 personas han muerto y unas 3.000 han resultado heridas desde que se retomaron los combates en agosto, y que unas 150.000 han sido desplazadas por el avance hutí. ACNUR ha contabilizado 3.000 personas que han cruzado el estrecho de Bab el Mandeb para buscar cobijo en la vecina Yibuti, donde se estima que, de continuar los combates, podrían llegar miles de refugiados más. El conflicto también está exacerbando la crítica situación de la población, donde la ONU calcula que la mitad de los 43 millones de habitantes se enfrenta a una grave escasez de alimentos.

Desde el lunes, las fuerzas gubernamentales han enviado refuerzos a la zona de Taiz y han bombardeado las rutas de abastecimiento de los hutíes. Según el general de división Abdulaziz al Majidi, jefe de la guarnición de Taiz, se han logrado “liberar algunas áreas” en el extrarradio de esa capital provincial, afirmó la agencia yemení Saba. La agencia YPA, vinculada al otro bando, ha acusado a los bombardeos saudíes en zonas residenciales de Moca y Yauf de matar al menos a siete civiles, entre ellos mujeres y niños.

Tanto el Gobierno de Yemen como los dirigentes de Arabia Saudí están tratando de que EE UU se una a su guerra contra los hutíes, después de que, este fin de semana, la milicia proiraní atacara con misiles balísticos y drones la capital saudí, Riad, e instalaciones de la petrolera Aramco. De acuerdo con The New York Times, el presidente Donald Trump ordenó el bombardeo de las posiciones hutíes este domingo, pero canceló su orden en el último minuto, cuando los militares ya estaban armando los cazas destinados al ataque.

Asistencia británica

Otros aliados de Riad sí que han respondido a las llamadas de apoyo saudí. Los ministros de Exteriores del G7 exigieron a los hutíes que “cesen toda acción militar” en Yemen y Arabia Saudí, y pongan fin a “sus amenazas a buques comerciales”.

El Reino Unido –antigua potencia colonial en Yemen– ha ido más allá y ha confirmado el envío de una aeronave de abastecimiento de combustible en vuelo para apoyar a los cazas saudíes que participan en la “defensa” de los ataques hutíes. “Lo hacemos por razones de seguridad nacional. En tiempos peligrosos, los buenos amigos se apoyan”, explicó el ministro de Defensa británico, Luke Pollard, en una entrevista con Sky News. Una fuente diplomática francesa citada por Al Jazeera, afirmó que su Gobierno también está listo para proteger la infraestructura energética saudí de los ataques hutíes.

Pakistán también ha reafirmado su “solidaridad inquebrantable” con Arabia Saudí. Ambos países mantienen un acuerdo bilateral de defensa al que este año se ha unido Turquía: el llamado Pacto de La Meca, que pretende convertirse en una OTAN regional, pero respecto al que todavía no se ha avanzado en los mecanismos de defensa mutua. Ankara, desde luego, no tiene intención de verse arrastrada a un conflicto en la zona.

El lunes, el líder de Ansar Alá, Abdulmalik al Hutí, advirtió directamente a Estados Unidos, Turquía y Pakistán de que no se dejen “enredar por Arabia Saudí en la agresión contra Yemen”, o, de otra forma, “sufrirán las consecuencias”.

Los hutíes han avisado de que ningún buque saudí puede transitar por Bab el Mandeb y el pasado día 10 de septiembre provocaron graves daños con sus ataques al oleoducto Este-Oeste de Arabia Saudí, con el que Riad intentaba compensar el estrangulamiento iraní del estrecho de Ormuz (crucial para la salida de hidrocarburos a los mercados internacionales). Tras días de reparaciones en la tubería, este martes, varios medios han publicado que algunas refinerías asiáticas han sido contactadas por Aramco, que les ha asegurado que “en breve” podrán volver a cargar petróleo en el puerto de Yanbu. Los clientes europeos, sin embargo, no podrán cargar hasta ya pasado octubre, debido a los retrasos en los contratos de suministro provocados por los ataques.

World.title: “Haría obligatoria la Educación Física hasta en Bachillerato”
World.content:
Antes de ser actor y humorista, David Amor estudió para ser profesor y llegó a la élite como balonmanista. Junto a Xabier Soutullo, graduado en Magisterio y también jugador, hablan de la importancia de integrar el deporte en la escuela y de cómo valores como la inclusión, la perseverancia o el trabajo conjunto construyen la educación del futuro

Antes de escuchar las carcajadas del público, el humorista David Amor (Salceda de Caselas, Pontevedra, 46 años) se rodeó de los gritos de ánimo desde las gradas como jugador de balonmano, deporte en el que alcanzó la gloria: fue internacional en las categorías júnior y juvenil, donde fue subcampeón del mundo en Moscú (1998) y de Europa en Suiza (1999). A nivel de clubes, jugó en División de Honor Plata (1999 y 2007) y en la Liga Asobal (2008). Todo ocurrió mientras estudiaba Ciencias de la Actividad Física y antes de que su vida tomara otro rumbo, el de la comunicación, el humor y la actuación. Hoy es conocido por una carrera que comenzó en la televisión gallega y que después le llevó a programas y series de ámbito nacional, en la que ha aplicado las enseñanzas que le dio el deporte durante años.

“Del deporte me llevo la satisfacción de la persistencia. A veces el resultado no es exactamente lo que tú querías, pero el camino es divertido”

De hecho, en su conversación con Xabier Soutullo (Vigo, 25 años), que también llegó al balonmano con siete años y que estudia para ser profesor, Amor rememora aquella etapa deportiva para hablar de algo que todavía mantiene: la perseverancia. Fue decisiva. Compañeros que parecían mejores terminaron por abandonar, mientras él se mantuvo firme. Esa misma forma de entender el esfuerzo, reconoce, la ha trasladado a su vida profesional. Soutullo además reflexiona sobre cómo en la pista se aprende a convivir, a trabajar con otros (aunque sean muy diferentes) y a perseguir un objetivo común.

“Me gustaría ser un profesor que atendiese a la inclusión del alumnado, crear un modelo del que todos formen parte”

A partir de sus similitudes, abordan la importancia de integrar el deporte en la escuela. “Yo haría obligatoria la asignatura de Educación Física hasta el Bachillerato, y la pondría todos los días”, reconoce Amor quien, a pesar de que estudió para ser docente de esta asignatura, nunca llegó a ejercer. Intrigado por la vocación que no siguió, le pregunta a Soutullo sus prioridades para cuando sea profesor. Su respuesta es lograr que en el aula los alumnos se complementen, que funcionen acompasados. En definitiva, escapar de la individualidad para trabajar como un equipo.

Pensemos la educación del futuro ‘Pensemos el mañana’, un proyecto de Fundación Unicaja, busca fomentar el conocimiento, los valores de la educación, un aprendizaje sostenible y responsable y dar respuestas a los grandes desafíos de la educación del futuro. El proyecto pivota sobre seis ejes: 1 Aprendizaje y sentido vital 2 Bienestar y salud mental 3 Futuro y empleabilidad 4 Sostenibilidad y sentido colectivo 5 Tecnología y ética 6 Carácter y ciudadanía ¿Qué está ocurriendo en estos tiempos de cambios profundos y transversales? ¿Cuáles son los grandes retos para afrontar la transformación que viene? ¿Qué educación necesitamos? Diferentes personalidades de todos los ámbitos nos ayudarán a responder a estas y otras preguntas destinadas a impulsar cambios, dinamizar ideas y apoyar propuestas con impacto pedagógico y social. ‘Pensemos el mañana’ es un proyecto inspirador para las futuras generaciones llamadas a conquistar nuevas cotas del saber en un mundo complejo y cambiante.
